title: migrate layout wedge: bare repo-root docs/ (or leftover .mindspec/docs) → permanent layout:mixed → spec create writes LEGACY canonical path (split-brain, orphans new specs); +doctor fossil-check exit 1
description:
LIVE P1 downstream (nologohq/lola, bead lola-qgoa; companion GH #194). Source-verified at v0.11.0 6947c86e. TWO independent bugs:

BUG A (the wedge, P1): layout classification is FILESYSTEM-ONLY and mistreats ordinary docs folders. internal/workspace/workspace.go: Legacy=exists(<root>/docs) (LegacyDocsDir=<root>/docs, bare dir existence), Canonical=exists(.mindspec/docs) (bare, even empty). ClassifyLayout (:175): Flat && (Canonical||Legacy) -> LayoutMixed. So a correctly-flattened repo that ALSO has a normal repo-root docs/ dir, OR any surviving/tracked .mindspec/docs entry, classifies MIXED FOREVER. Run-state does NOT drive it: migrationRecoveryActive (:239,288) only suppresses the mixed ERROR for a NON-TERMINAL stage; migrationTerminalStage='applied' (:286); resolver reads only Stage, never published. In mixed state, SpecDir's NEW-spec default is gated on isFlatTree==LayoutFlat (:352,434-437) -> mixed writes CanonicalDocsDir/specs/<id> = .mindspec/docs/specs/<slug>, while reads are flat-first per-artifact tiers -> every new spec orphaned/undriveable (fresh worktree still picks legacy because a TRACKED root docs/ or tracked .mindspec/docs entry is in the checkout). No config override exists (config.yaml layout: key read nowhere).

BUG B (exit 1 sidekick, P1): internal/doctor/migration.go checkMigrationMetadata is a FOSSIL of the spec-036 classify pipeline DELETED in spec 045 (97a0bc9f 'replace migrate plan/apply with prompt emission'). Armed whenever docs_archive/ OR .mindspec/lineage/manifest.json exists (:216-223) — and migrate layout (spec 106) legitimately writes that manifest — then demands the dead pipeline's 9-artifact set (inventory/classification/extraction/plan/validation/apply.json + plan.md, :277) -> 7x Missing + docs_archive Missing -> HasFailures -> exit 1. Hint text says 'run migrate apply', a verb that no longer exists. doctor --fix cannot help (Fix runs on Error|Warn only, not Missing; no FixFunc attached).

RELATED (fold in or split): (C) migrate layout --abort hard-RESETS an applied run (rollback() checks only Published which is never armed; mover.go:509-520) — a data-loss hazard; also arm State.Published at the point of no return per the mover.go:505-508 Bead-5 NOTE that never landed (closes #194 §7). (D) mover prints 'flatten complete' (migrate.go:198) while the tree classifies mixed, and leaves non-plan .mindspec/docs children (e.g. designs/) since removeEmptyDocsDir only rmdir's empty (mover.go:647) and the 8-group plan excludes them.

FIX-FORWARD: (1) scope the Legacy marker to lifecycle shape (docs/specs|docs/adr|docs/domains|docs/core), not bare docs/ (workspace.go:252) — un-wedges every consumer with a normal docs folder; (2) post-flatten precedence: a terminal applied layout run or a durable layout:flat marker (roadmap A3 .mindspec/schema.json) classifies flat + demotes leftovers to doctor WARN; mover finalize should re-run DetectLayout and FAIL LOUDLY while markers remain instead of printing success; (3) retire/rekey checkMigrationMetadata (layout runs need only state.json+lineage.json); (4) arm State.Published + rollback refuse on stage==applied. Distinct from sc0w (branch false-positives) and 3jq7 (link-check breadth); GH #194 §7 is orthogonal (its teeth = the --abort hazard). Validates roadmap Workstream A3.
close_reason: Shipped via spec 118 (layout-marker-scoping), released v0.11.1 (dcb7a5ef). Fix on main: internal/workspace/workspace.go IsLifecycleChildName/LifecycleChildNames marker scoping (ae716e22); executor/layout_guard.go BlobExistsAtRef + mergeLayoutRegression (418efbaf); doctor/migration.go rekeyed checkMigrationMetadata (d7de511b). PR #195.

title: Harden impl-approve/FinalizeEpic: panel-gate beads closed via raw 'bd close' before auto-merge (silent out-vote bypass)
description: Final-review panel of spec 114 (G2 codex, 0.99, code-traced) found: mindspec impl approve -> ApproveImpl -> FinalizeEpic (internal/executor/mindspec_executor.go:381-418) auto-merges unmerged bead branches that were closed via raw 'bd close' WITHOUT going through mindspec complete's panel gate. So an operator can bd-close an RC-bearing bead and impl-approve merges it un-gated — the same silent-out-vote hole spec 114 closed for 'mindspec complete', still open on the impl-approve/finalize path. Spec 114 scoped R1/R2 to the complete gate; this is the follow-up: make FinalizeEpic's pre-merge path run the same panel-gate + durable-refutation reconciliation as complete.Run (or refuse to auto-merge a bead lacking proof of panel settlement). Repro (G2): unresolved REQUEST_CHANGES -> raw bd close -> mindspec impl approve must NOT merge; recovery via mindspec complete must still block until resolved or durably refuted. This is the 'no silent out-vote IN THE BINARY' completion Max cares about. NOTE mindspec_executor.go:398 comment claims 'same rule as CompleteBead; mutates nothing on a block' — verify whether any gate actually fires there.

title: impl approve on protected-main orphans the finalize commit → bead/epic state self-reverts on next sync
description: Spec 106 finalization exposed this. On a branch-protected main, 'mindspec impl approve <spec>' cannot commit the epic-close/finalize JSONL directly to main; it pushes a finalize commit to the spec branch and instructs a PR. If the implementation PR was ALREADY merged (the normal flow) and the spec branch is then deleted as post-merge debris, that finalize commit (the epic+bead close in .beads/issues.jsonl) NEVER reaches main. main's committed JSONL stays stale (epic open / last bead in_progress). The bd post-merge git hook ('bd hooks run post-merge') re-imports the committed JSONL into Dolt on every merge/FF, so it SILENTLY REVERTS the closes each sync — observed live: spec-106 epic mindspec-3d3i + bead .6 reverted from closed to open/in_progress after a routine 'git merge --ff-only origin/main'. Combine with the recurring verify-close gotcha (bead .6's overnight 'complete' also failed to persist its close) and the bead tracker can disagree with reality indefinitely. FIX DIRECTION: impl approve on protected-main should fold the finalize JSONL into the SAME PR (or commit the close PRE-merge), OR land it via a dedicated auto-opened PR and refuse to 'complete' the lifecycle until that lands; at minimum, detect the orphaned-finalize condition and emit a recovery command. Also: the post-merge hook making committed-JSONL authoritative-on-import means any stale committed JSONL silently overwrites Dolt — consider a divergence guard. REPRO + EVIDENCE: this session's actions on spec 106; review/prerelease-plan/ panel (R1 confirmed the mechanism). Known-issue for v0.10.0 release notes if unfixed by tag.
acceptance_criteria: impl approve on a protected-main repo leaves main's committed .beads/issues.jsonl matching Dolt (no orphaned finalize commit); a regression simulates protected-main finalize and asserts no self-revert after a subsequent merge/FF.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #174 (merged 2026-07-07): FinalizeEpic detects the already-merged spec branch (IsAncestor vs fetched origin/main) and lands the finalize JSONL on chore/finalize-<specID> cut from origin/main, with observed-SHA force-with-lease reconcile, temp-worktree self-heal, baseline-push-first ordering, and an explicit operator NOTE. Panel wu7t-finalize-fix: r1 3A/3RC -> fix round -> r2 5A/1RC PASS. Deferred hardening tracked in mindspec-3xqm.

title: install.sh checksum verification fails on v0.8.0 — unanchored grep matches the .spdx.json SBOM line
description: v0.8.0 added syft SBOMs to checksums.txt, so each archive now has two matching lines: mindspec_VER_<arch>.tar.gz AND mindspec_VER_<arch>.tar.gz.spdx.json. install.sh:242 used an unanchored 'grep "$ARCHIVE_NAME"' which matches BOTH lines, so EXPECTED_CHECKSUM becomes two newline-joined hashes. The compare against the single real archive hash then fails and install aborts with 'Checksum verification failed!' for every user of the documented curl|sh one-liner. The binary itself was always valid (89c1ca75... matches). install.ps1:256 had the identical bug via 'Select-String -Pattern $archiveName'. Fix: exact filename-field match (awk $2==f in sh; -split/-eq field-2 in ps1). v0.8.0 regression (v0.7.0 had no SBOMs). P1 install-blocker.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #137 (merged f1c9fc5): install.sh + install.ps1 checksum extraction now exact field-2 match (was unanchored, matched the .spdx.json SBOM line on v0.8.0). Regression guard added (scripts/test-install-checksum.{sh,ps1} + install-smoke.yml). Also fixed a latent install.ps1 unparseable-script blocker. The curl|sh one-liner works again from main. 2026-06-12.

title: beads merge driver invokes 'bd merge' which no longer exists in bd 1.0.4 — every both-sides-changed jsonl merge fails, complete left closed-but-unmerged bead
description: Root cause: .gitattributes maps .beads/issues.jsonl to merge=beads; merge.beads.driver in /Users/Max/replit/mindspec/.git/config (the ONLY place it is configured — covers main + all worktrees, no worktreeConfig extension; nothing in mindspec source writes it, no git log -S hits) still runs 'bd merge %A %O %A %B'. That subcommand was removed by the bd 1.0.x upgrade (installed bd 1.0.4 suggests merge-slot, which is a merge-queue lock primitive, NOT a file merge driver — no %A/%O/%B semantics; audit of all 1.0.4 subcommands found no drop-in). Any merge where both sides changed the jsonl invokes the driver and fails: path left unmerged with 3 stages and zero textual markers. Impact observed live (spec-092 Bead 2, mindspec-fwo5.2, 2026-06-11): complete.Run closes the bead (complete.go:249) BEFORE merging (CompleteBead, mindspec_executor.go:173); merge failure is only warned (line 221) and the ancestor safety check (227-231) aborts cleanup -> bead CLOSED in Dolt but bead/mindspec-fwo5.2 unmerged, bead worktree retained, spec worktree stuck mid-merge. Repair (verified safe per ADR-0025/0023 — Dolt is canonical, bd export is a strict superset of both stages, byte-deterministic): in the spec worktree run bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl; git add; git commit --no-edit (MERGE_MSG matches MergeInto's message); verify merge-base --is-ancestor; then git worktree remove + git branch -d mirroring CompleteBead cleanup. git merge --abort remains full rollback until the commit. Fix: (now) point merge.beads.driver in .git/config at a tracked wrapper 'scripts/bd-jsonl-merge-driver.sh %A %O %B' that runs bd export -o $1 (regenerate-from-DB is the correct merge for this derived artifact; do NOT bd import %B — blind upsert can regress newer rows; do NOT drop the driver — textual merge of same-record divergence is meaningless). (PR) ship the wrapper, have bootstrap write the config for future repos, and add a mindspec doctor check (internal/doctor/beads.go) flagging a merge.beads.driver whose command does not exist; consider merge-before-close ordering in complete. Full proposal: /tmp/orchestrator-staging/incident-merge-driver/PROPOSAL.md. Incident reference: spec-092 Bead 2, 2026-06-11.
notes: PANEL CONSENSUS PR-SCOPE (incident 2026-06-11, 3/3): for FUTURE repos — (1) BOOTSTRAP (not 'mindspec setup <agent>': setup is per-agent, the merge driver is agent-agnostic per-clone git config) writes merge.beads.driver into the new repo's .git/config AND ships/tracks scripts/bd-jsonl-merge-driver.sh so fresh repos are covered from commit 0; mindspec doctor --fix for existing repos. (2) DOCTOR checks in internal/doctor/beads.go (alongside checkBdVersionFloor): (a) configured merge.beads.driver whose command does not resolve/is not executable (resolve relative paths against worktree top-level) — this incident was statically detectable at the bd 1.0.x upgrade; (b) .gitattributes merge=beads attribute with NO merge.beads.driver configured — git silently falls back to plain TEXT merge of the jsonl (the more dangerous sibling: silent semantic corruption vs loud failure). Keep wrapper export flags in lockstep with bd's auto-export profile (doctor assertion). (3) RESIDUAL (document, don't fix here): GitHub PR merges never run local merge drivers — impl-approve 'pr' strategy and chore/beads-sync PRs do a plain text merge of issues.jsonl on GitHub; acceptable because the post-merge beads-sync pattern compensates, but it must be written down. (4) Interim wrapper shipped via PR #124 (merged e3154ba, 2026-06-11); live repo config points at the absolute path /Users/Max/replit/mindspec/scripts/bd-jsonl-merge-driver.sh %A %O %B.

title: Usability roadmap 2026-06: agent-contract hardening + skills thin-down + 091 + backlog burn-down
description:

UNIFYING DIAGNOSIS: the agent contract lives in prose (16 skills, instruct templates, docs) while the binary's errors are dead-ends (no recovery path, dishonest exit codes, location/artifact-blind guards). Skills grew large BECAUSE they compensate for what the CLI doesn't say at point of use. Fix the CLI's contract and the skills shrink naturally.

Steps 1 and 2 are each a normal mindspec spec (~6-8 beads). title: impl approve / complete delete the worktree the caller is standing in — getcwd errors and spurious exit 1 in agent harnesses
description: Both terminal lifecycle commands remove the worktree the agent is typically standing in. impl approve auto-chdirs INTO the spec worktree (cmd/mindspec/impl.go:54-57) then FinalizeEpic removes it; withWorkingDir (internal/executor/mindspec_executor.go:513-528) silently fails to restore cwd into the deleted dir. Worse, the invoking shell's cwd is left pointing at a deleted directory, so agent harnesses (Claude Code Bash tool) see 'pwd: error retrieving current directory: getcwd: cannot access parent directories' and exit code 1 — AFTER the command fully succeeded. Agents then treat the approve/complete as failed and retry/repair. Compounding: mindspec next's own completion guidance (cmd/mindspec/next.go:272) instructs agents to 'cd into the worktree, then run mindspec complete', i.e. mindspec tells the agent to stand in the directory that complete will delete. Fix: (1) os.Chdir(root) immediately after the terminal mutation, before emitInstruct; (2) when invoked from inside a worktree that the command will remove, print a prominent final line 'NOTE: your shell's directory was removed — run: cd <root>'; (3) change next.go:272 guidance to say complete may be run from the repo root (it is location-agnostic — it resolves the bead worktree from the worktree list). Reported via Claude Code agent field notes 2026-06-10.

title: impl approve: phase-mismatch deadlock when stored mindspec_phase is stale — no recovery path
description: When the epic's stored mindspec_phase metadata disagrees with the child-derived phase (e.g. last bead closed via bd close or a crashed complete, leaving stored=implement while all children are closed), 'mindspec impl approve' fails with: expected review mode, got "implement" (internal/approve/impl.go:121-123). Fix options: (a) when stored phase disagrees with derived phase AND derived phase satisfies the gate, self-heal the metadata; (b) emit the exact recovery command in the error message; (c) add --reconcile-phase flag. title: plugins/mindspec: gaps + workflows research findings
description:
Captured live during lola spec-050 session (Beads 2 r2 fix, 3 r1, 4 r1) that wrote and exercised the plugin. Full findings at plugins/mindspec/FINDINGS.md.

Top items (10 follow-ups):

1. README naming — name the 4 Anthropic patterns the plugin implements (parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer, prompt chaining) + flag routing as the unused one.
2. /ms-bead-prep — sibling to /ms-bead-impl for drafting impl prompts. Biggest lever on impl-subagent quality, currently undocumented.
3. Codex-substitution as deterministic check — grep for 'ERROR: You've hit your usage limit' rather than prose 'detect failure'.
4. PreToolUse hook on mindspec complete — enforce >=5/6 APPROVE declaratively, not as orchestrator convention.
5. bd Dolt 1105 — large bead descriptions block --claim event-recording. Either resize events.old_value column or have plugin auto-fall-back.
6. .gitignore ADR-divergence — bead merges consistently hit [adr-divergence-unowned] on .gitignore. Either claim under infra domain, treat root dotfiles as repo-infra-by-default, or pre-include --override-adr.
7. bd ready vs plan dep graph drift — Bead 5 showed ready before Bead 4 merged. mindspec plan approve should walk plan **Depends on:** lines and bd dep add automatically.
8. mindspec instruct (SessionStart hook) extension — add --panel-state surfacing in-progress beads, pending panel rounds, locked agent worktrees. Post-compaction state recovery was slow without this.
9. parallel-window in /ms-spec-autopilot — currently prose, not algorithm. Either remove as YAGNI or add a worked example.
10. /ms-panel-halt-recover — resume path after halt/REJECT undefined.

Workflows research (Claude Code Dynamic Workflows, research preview May 2026):
- Real feature: JS runtime, 1000/run, 16 concurrent subagents
- Invoked via /deep-research, ultracode, custom commands
- Distinct from skills/hooks/subagents

- Recommendation: stay with skills for panel-review (need mid-run intervention to swap codex-subs); future port for /ms-spec-autopilot only (background-durable across context compaction)

title: [ZFC-2] Remove "Decomposition Heuristics" block from plan.md template
description:
`internal/instruct/templates/plan.md:95-109` pre-bakes a six-step research-cited rubric into the model's decomposition reasoning (target 3-5 beads, R≈0.50 redundancy, chain depth ≤ 3, etc.). This is exactly the "hand-rolled prompt scaffolding that pre-bakes decision categories" anti-pattern from ZFC: instead of letting the model judge decomposition, the prompt hands it a fixed script with numeric cutoffs.
Replace with a short open-ended directive: "Decompose the spec into the fewest, most-independent beads you can. Justify each split. Prefer fewer larger beads over many small ones; prefer parallel over serial chains." Let the model size the work.
Note: this bead and ZFC-1 are companion fixes — both encode the same opinion, just in different places.
close_reason: Re-review: not actually a ZFC violation. ZFC governs application code, not prompt content. Telling the model 'research suggests 3-5 beads, here's why' informs its judgment with priors — the model still decides. A pure-ZFC prompt that withheld this guidance would be worse, not better. Worth periodic 'is this guidance still right?' review, but that's prompt-design, not ZFC.

title: [PERF-1] Add per-CLI phase.Cache to dedupe redundant bd subprocess calls
description:
`mindspec instruct` (run by SessionStart on every agent turn) makes 5-11 redundant `bd` subprocess calls. The call stack threads `FindEpicBySpecID` 3× through `ResolveTarget` (`resolve/target.go:87`) + `ResolveMode` (`resolve/resolve.go:44`) + `ResolveContextFromDir` (`cmd/mindspec/instruct.go:89`). Inside, `queryEpics` (`phase/derive.go:457-503`) and `queryChildren` (`phase/derive.go:487`) each loop over the three known statuses with one `bd list --status=… --json` per status.
On macOS, fork+exec of a Go binary is ~3-8ms; cold Dolt is far worse — each `bd` call is roughly 30-100ms. Going from 8 calls to 2 saves ~200-600ms per `mindspec instruct`, a 2-5× SessionStart speedup.
design:
1. Introduce `internal/phase/cache.go` with a `Cache` struct memoizing `epicID→EpicInfo`, `epicID→[]ChildInfo`, `specID→epicID`, and a `[]EpicInfo` for all-epics.
2. Make `phase.ResolveContext`, `DerivePhase`, `FindEpicBySpecID`, `resolve.ResolveMode`, `resolve.ResolveTarget`, `state.checkBeadStatus` accept the cache.
3. In `cmd/mindspec/instruct.go:68-105`, build the cache once and thread through; eliminate the duplicate `ResolveContextFromDir` call.
4. Replace the per-status loops in `queryEpics`/`queryChildren` with a single `bd list --json` (no `--status` filter) and filter in-process.
acceptance_criteria:
- `mindspec instruct` makes ≤3 bd subprocess calls in the warm case (verified via `mindspec trace`).
- All `phase`/`resolve` unit tests pass.
- SessionStart wall-clock drops measurably (compare `time mindspec instruct` before/after).

title: [PERF-2] Replace SessionStart subprocess spawn with in-process instruct call
description: `cmd/mindspec/hook.go:126-138` does `exec.CommandContext(ctx, os.Args[0], "instruct").Run()`. The hook is already running inside the mindspec binary; spawning itself doubles cobra init, doubles trace setup, doubles ADR/config loading. There is no reason to fork — the same `instructCmd.RunE` body can be invoked in-process.
design:
1. Extract the shared body from `instructCmd.RunE` into `internal/instruct.Run(format, specFlag string) error`.
2. Replace the subprocess call in `runSessionStartHook` with `instruct.Run("", "")`.
3. Remove the 12s context timeout (errors should surface directly).
close_reason: Shipped via PR #94 commit a1e4443; hook.go:131 calls instruct.Run in-process; verified 2026-06-10

title: [SEC-1] Validate spec/ADR/bead IDs at all CLI entrypoints before filesystem joins
description:
User-supplied IDs reach `filepath.Join` + `os.ReadFile`/`os.WriteFile` without `validate.SpecID` at many call sites. Only 4 sites currently validate.
Concrete locations:
- `cmd/mindspec/validate.go:31` — `validate.ValidateSpec(root, specID)` (no SpecID check)
- `cmd/mindspec/validate.go:50` — same for `ValidatePlan`
- `cmd/mindspec/spec.go:96` — `approve.ApproveSpec(root, specID, …)`
- `internal/approve/plan.go:71-78` — same pattern
- `cmd/mindspec/adr.go:104-119` — `store.Get(args[0])` → `filepath.Join(dir, id+".md")` and `filepath.Glob(...)`
- `internal/adr/create.go:29` — `--supersedes` flag value joined with ADRDir; `Supersede(root, oldID, newID)` does `ReadFile`/`WriteFile` on the joined path. `--supersedes ../../../tmp/poisoned` writes an ADR template to `/tmp/poisoned.md`.
- `cmd/mindspec/domain.go:32` (via `workspace.DomainDir`)
- `cmd/mindspec/record.go:48,70` (via `recording.HasRecording`/`RecordingDir`)
- `cmd/mindspec/spec.go:41` (via `workspace.SpecDir`)
- `internal/recording/manifest.go:33-44` — `RecordingDir`/`ManifestPath`/`EventsPath` don't validate
The bite is bounded because mindspec runs as the local user, but scripts/CI that pass IDs derived from branch names, tickets, or external strings get a "read/write arbitrary `.md`-named file" primitive.
design:
Two-layer fix:
1. Add `validate.BeadID`, `validate.ADRID`, `validate.DomainName` helpers next to existing `validate.SpecID`.
2. Make every workspace path-builder return `(string, error)` so the type system forces the check — `workspace.SpecDir(root, specID string) (string, error)`, similar for `ADRDir(root, adrID)`, `DomainDir(root, domain)`, `recording.*Path`.
3. After path construction, optionally also pass through `validate.SafePath(root, resolved)` (already exists) as defense-in-depth.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #108; helpers live in internal/idvalidate (not internal/validate); verified 2026-06-10

title: Spec epics left open when merged via PR without mindspec impl approve
description:
Specs 068, 071, 072 were merged to main via GitHub PRs but their lifecycle epics remain open with zero children.

Design intent:
- Epics auto-close via beads molecule completion when all child beads close
- impl approve then sets the mindspec_done metadata marker to distinguish 'all beads done' from 'explicitly finalized'

Why it failed for these specs:
- plan approve didn't create child beads under the epic (likely due to SpecIDFromMetadata slug bug — mindspec-xd3g — preventing epic lookup)
- With zero children, molecule completion can't fire
- impl approve was never run (and would also fail due to the slug bug)

Root cause: mindspec-xd3g (SpecIDFromMetadata doesn't slugify). Once that's fixed, plan approve will create beads under the correct epic, molecule completion will auto-close the epic when all beads close, and impl approve will set the done marker.

Immediate cleanup: close these three orphaned epics with done marker manually.
close_reason: Root cause (mindspec-xd3g slugify) is fixed. All 3 orphaned epics (068, 071, 072) are already closed.

title: Agent can bypass bead worktree workflow: instruct doesn't guide to mindspec next
description:
When starting a session with an active spec in implement phase, the agent is not told to use 'mindspec next' to claim beads and create bead worktrees. This allows the agent to commit implementation code directly to the spec branch.

Three contributing factors:

1. **instruct from main shows 'No Active Work'**: Even with spec 073 active (branch + worktree + beads), running instruct from the main repo shows idle. It should detect the active spec branch/worktree and tell the agent to cd to the worktree and use 'mindspec next'.

2. **instruct from spec worktree shows stale test epics**: The phase resolver finds hundreds of stale test epics from LLM test sandbox runs, flooding the output. The real spec 073 is buried.

3. **Pre-commit hook only protects main**: The hook checks cfg.IsProtectedBranch() which only matches main/master. It does NOT enforce that implementation code belongs on bead/ branches instead of spec/ branches. Even if core.hooksPath weren't bypassed, the hook would have allowed the commits.

The primary fix should be in instruction — the agent should be told what to do. Hooks are a last resort.
notes: Root cause is mindspec-xd3g (SpecIDFromMetadata slug bug). Without the epic match, phase derivation fails and instruct gives wrong guidance. The hook bypass (core.hooksPath) and missing spec-branch enforcement are secondary — hooks should be a last resort. Fix mindspec-xd3g first, then DiscoverActiveSpecs should filter done-phase specs.
close_reason: All three factors fixed: (1) SpecIDFromMetadata slugify (ce44c21), (2) DiscoverActiveSpecs filters done/childless epics (cc2a287), (3) pre-commit hook blocks impl commits on spec/ branches (1088d19).

title: SpecIDFromMetadata doesn't reconstruct slug format — plan approve can't find epic
description:
SpecIDFromMetadata(73, "Llm Test Coverage") returns "073-Llm Test Coverage" but the actual spec ID is "073-llm-test-coverage". The function does fmt.Sprintf("%03d-%s", specNum, specTitle) without lowercasing or hyphenating.

Impact chain:
1. FindEpicBySpecID fails — can't match epic to spec ID from worktree context
2. Phase derivation fails — spec worktree context falls back to default mode
3. instruct gives wrong guidance — "No Active Work" or "Multiple Active Specs" instead of implement mode instructions
4. Agent bypasses workflow — works directly on spec branch without mindspec next / bead worktrees

Also contributes to DiscoverActiveSpecs pollution: stale test epics generate specIDs like "001-Test Feature" (unslugified) and show as active specs.

Fix: SpecIDFromMetadata should slugify the title (lowercase, spaces→hyphens) to match the original slug format.
close_reason: slugify() added to SpecIDFromMetadata, DiscoverActiveSpecs filters done/orphan epics

title: [126-panel-review-discipline] Bead 4: Portable CI-parity slot + delivery reach — pre-126 snapshots and the upgrade-refresh proof
description:
R8b, AC-16, and guard-table completion (AC-11 rows, AC-12). Runs last:
final-review is its third sequential editor, and the Refreshed
assertions are only non-vacuous once Beads 1–3 have diverged every
edited surface from its base bytes.

**Steps**
1. `ms-spec-final-review/SKILL.md` (R8b): the F2 full-regression slot
   is instructed to reproduce the project-declared CI invocation
   VERBATIM — `commands.ci`, falling back to `commands.test` — on the
   spec branch before sign-off, and to record the explicit advisory
   finding ("no declared CI invocation — CI parity not reproduced")
   when neither key is declared. Extend the retained "Not a CI
   substitute" line (`:62`) with the local-green ≠ CI-green rationale.
   ABSTRACT only: config keys, never a concrete invocation (no
   `go test`, no `bd` choreography — R8c).
2. Capture the seven byte-exact pre-126 snapshots into
   `internal/setup/historical_skills/`: `ms-panel-run.pre126.md`,
   `ms-panel-tally.pre126.md`, `ms-bead-cycle.pre126.md`,
   `ms-bead-fix.pre126.md`, `ms-spec-final-review.pre126.md` from
   `git show <base>:plugins/mindspec/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`
   (base = `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`, `7ec96295` at plan
   time); `ms-spec-approve.pre126.md` and `ms-plan-approve.pre126.md`
   as the exact bytes the BASE binary installs (base-build
   `mindspec setup claude` into a scratch dir, copy the installed
   SKILL.md files; cross-check against `git show
   <base>:internal/setup/claude.go`). The `<name>.<tag>.md` convention
   (`skills.go:26-36`) resolves them automatically — no code change
   needed for pickup.
3. NEW `internal/setup/upgrade_refresh_pre126_test.go` (AC-16),
   following the `skills_test.go:236-244` seeding precedent. **FIRST
   leg — the provenance-digest oracle (plan-gate correction):** for
   each of the seven snapshots, assert the embedded `.pre126.md` body
   hashes (SHA-256) to its PINNED digest — the five plugin-skill
   digests recorded in this plan's snapshot-provenance block
   (computed from base `7ec96295`), the two lifecycle-literal digests
   computed by the recorded base-binary install-capture procedure and
   pinned in the same test — BEFORE any seeding. This is what makes
   AC-16 non-vacuous: without it, a wrongly-captured snapshot passes
   every downstream leg, because `matchesShipped` trusts whatever
   bytes sit in `historical_skills/` (the bad fixture is itself in
   the shipped-history set). THEN the behavioral legs: for EACH
   of the seven edited skills, seed the `.pre126.md` bytes on disk in
   `t.TempDir()`, run `installSkills` with the current canonical
   `wanted` set, assert the file is classified **Refreshed**
   (`Result.Refreshed`) and its bytes now equal the new canonical;
   PLUS the user-modified-preservation leg (a body matching no shipped
   snapshot → left in place, `Result.Notices` HC-6 message). Deleting
   any one snapshot REDs TWICE: the digest assertion fails on the
   missing embedded body, and the seeded pre-126 bytes then match
   nothing shipped → classified user-modified, not Refreshed → the
   seed row REDs too. (Note the asymmetry the digest leg exists for:
   DELETION is caught by the behavioral legs, but a WRONGLY-CAPTURED
   snapshot is caught ONLY by the digest oracle.)
4. Append to `internal/setup/review_discipline_test.go`: AC-11 rows —
   the `commands.ci` fragment (+ fallback + no-declaration-advisory
   fragments) in the embedded final-review bytes, and the four
   negative tripwire rows (`go test`, `npm test`, `pytest`,

   confirm every AC-1/2/4/5/6/7/8/9/10/11 fragment is one traceable
   row; record the full stash-matrix demonstration.
5. Update the AC-10 allowlist ONLY if this bead's R8b text introduces

design:
## Requirements

1. **R1 — One authoritative panel-size story, pinned defaults, consistency
guard** (bead `mindspec-yt96`).
The configured panel mix is the single authority. (a) Every skill sentence
that hard-codes "6" / "5-of-6" (`ms-panel-run` name/description/lines 3, 6,
8, 32, 143; `ms-panel-tally:26,125`; `ms-spec-final-review:40`) is rephrased
to derive from the configured mix, with the shipped default stated once in
canonical form: "the configured panel mix (shipped default: 6 reviewers — 3
`claude` + 3 `codex` — threshold `n-1`)". (b) The scale-by-gate-cost ladder
(bead 8, spec/plan ≈ 9, final 12) ships as a commented `panel.gates` EXAMPLE
in `ms-panel-run` (and the ADR-0043 amendment), explicitly labelled operator
preference, family-level only — reviewer entries carry ONLY `family` +
`count` keys, no model values (structurally enforced by AC-2). (c) A Go
consistency test (in `internal/setup`, beside the `skills_test.go:482-483`
fragment-guard precedent) asserts all three surfaces agree:
`config.DefaultConfig().Panel` sums to 6 reviewer slots across families
{claude, codex} with `ApproveThreshold == "n-1"`; the embedded
`ms-panel-run` + `ms-panel-tally` bytes (`pluginmindspec.SkillFiles()`)
contain the canonical default sentence; and `.mindspec/adr/ADR-0043-*.md`
contains the amendment marker. Changing any one surface REDs the test until
all agree. (d) `DefaultConfig` panel VALUES are unchanged, full stop
(zero-config installs keep their sizes, per the spec-112 note at
`config.go:459-462`); the scale-by-gate-cost ladder ships ONLY as the (b)
documented `panel.gates` example, labelled operator preference.

2. **R2 — Reviewer mutation-isolation** (bead `mindspec-0skg`).
`ms-panel-run` (a new "Reviewer conduct" section + a note on the
empirical-prober row of the Slot lens defaults table, `SKILL.md:206-217`)
and `ms-spec-final-review` (F2 row) instruct: any reviewer that EXECUTES or
MUTATES code (runs tests, deletes an escape to probe it, edits a fixture)
must do so in its OWN isolated checkout — `git worktree add --detach
/tmp/rev-<panel-slug>-<slot> <reviewed_head_sha>` (or `git archive`) —
never in the shared bead worktree; read-only inspection of the shared tree
remains fine; the reviewer removes its worktree when done. `ms-panel-tally`
Step 2 gains the orchestrator half: before acting on a CONTESTED finding
(an empirical claim another slot or the fix author disputes), re-verify it
yourself in a fresh detached checkout at the reviewed SHA; the reproduction
(or its failure) is the refutation `evidence`. The in-skill motivation is
stated PORTABLY (failure mode, no incident ID): "reviewers that mutate a
shared checkout contaminate each other's probes — one slot's deleted escape
becomes another slot's false REQUEST_CHANGES"; the spec-116 provenance
lives in ADR-0044 only.

3. **R3 — Verify-never-confirm for CLI-reviewer findings** (bead
`mindspec-8hvn`).
The doctrine is stated family-symmetric — an empirical finding from ANY
reviewer is a VERIFY, never a CONFIRMED — and the codex rows are its
documented instance. (a) `ms-bead-cycle`'s family-asymmetry table row at
`SKILL.md:135` ("trust the empirical check") is rewritten: treat the codex
REQUEST_CHANGES as verify-first — reproduce the claim (test-execution AND
code-reasoning findings alike) in an isolated checkout (R2 mechanics)
before treating it as confirmed; the shipped text carries BOTH directions
of the field evidence, phrased portably (CLI reviewers catch real bugs the
interactive reviewers miss, AND CLI reviewers false-flag "red suite in
clean checkout" / "hollow fixture" claims that a clean-checkout
reproduction refutes) — the spec-119 provenance lives in ADR-0044 only.
(b) Never out-vote by count in either direction; weight the reviewer that
did the deeper code trace (extends the existing `ms-panel-tally:127-128`
confidence/single-dissent rules). (c) `ms-panel-tally` requires every
BLOCKING finding from a non-interactive CLI reviewer to be reproduced in
isolation before fix-dispatch or refutation. (d) `ms-panel-run`'s
substitution material documents the security-classifier fallback: when a
reviewer family's safety classifier refuses an adversarial/security-framed
lens, re-dispatch the SAME slot with a correctness-framed persona (keep the
slot id, mark the substitution in `reviewer_id`, as the existing quota-sub
convention at `SKILL.md:187` already does).

4. **R4 — Document-gate panel doctrine: guidance, not enforcement** (bead
`mindspec-s05u`; GH #212, crosslinks #182/#181).
R4 ships the document-panel DOCTRINE — the lens tables and the invocation
step — NOT a gate: the approve verbs have NO binary preflight
(`cmd/mindspec/spec.go:111` calls `approve.ApproveSpec` and
`cmd/mindspec/plan_cmd.go:52` calls `approve.ApprovePlan` with no panel
check; the panel.json `gate` field is decision-inert), so a compliant agent
runs the document panel because the installed skill says to, and a
non-compliant agent CAN skip it — by design, per ADR-0040's L4 staging.
(a) The `ms-spec-approve` and `ms-plan-approve` literals
(`internal/setup/claude.go:808,:825`) gain a pre-approve panel step: run
`/ms-panel-run` with `mindspec panel create <slug> --spec <id> --gate
spec_approve|plan_approve --target <ref>` (per-gate config keys from spec
112 `PanelGateKeys`, `config.go:129`; the `--gate` flag itself from spec
113 R3) against the spec/plan DOCUMENT, and do not run `mindspec spec
approve` / `plan approve` until `/ms-panel-tally` returns Allow — as
instructions in the installed skill text. (b) `ms-panel-run` gains
document-review lens defaults for these gates (falsifiability of ACs,
scope/domain honesty, contradiction hunting, feasibility/blast-radius)
parallel to the existing bead table. (c) Escalation guidance: a
high-blast-radius document (multiple domains, security surface, public
contract) scales the mix via `panel.gates` — family-level guidance only.
(d) Enforcement is OUT OF SCOPE: mechanized gate-before-mutate on the
spec/plan approve verbs (and any `loop.gate_authority` wiring) is tracked
as **`mindspec-0pij`** (the L1 ratchet, sibling to spec 115's
complete-side ratchet). Bead `mindspec-s05u` is therefore PARTIALLY
delivered by this spec (the guidance half); the mechanization half is
`mindspec-0pij`. (e) NO new skill files: R4 ships entirely inside the
existing `ms-spec-approve`/`ms-plan-approve` lifecycle literals plus the
document-gate lens tables in `ms-panel-run` — panel mechanics stay
single-homed in `ms-panel-run`, and existing installs receive the edits
via the snapshot-refresh mechanism (Delivery reach, AC-16).

5. **R5 — BRIEF quotes acceptance criteria verbatim** (bead `mindspec-ljfz`).
`ms-panel-run` step 0.2 replaces the `SKILL.md:78` guidance ("Don't paste
the plan; summarise it.") with: the BRIEF MUST paste each Rn/ACn the work
claims to satisfy VERBATIM from `spec.md` (byte-exact, with its Rn/ACn id);
the plain-English summary is additive, never a replacement — aligning the
BRIEF with the impl-prompt rule (`ms-bead-impl:51,155`). One slot's lens
carries the AC-provenance duty: trace every claimed AC clause to a
landed+passing test against the SPEC text, not the BRIEF summary
(final-review F5 keeps its artifact-path half). This targets the
SKILL-authored BRIEF body; the machine-managed header (`renderBriefHeader`,
`create.go:186-208`) is unchanged. Additionally, `briefStubBody`
(`create.go:26`) gains an `## Acceptance Criteria (verbatim from spec.md)`
heading (with its `<!-- TODO(skill): ... -->` stub comment) — a
string-constant-only edit, guarded by AC-15 — so a fresh install's very
first BRIEF skeleton demands the verbatim ACs.

6. **R6 — Findings-never-out-voted, reviewer-facing** (bead `mindspec-f8ra`).
`ms-panel-run` (in the reviewer-prompt composition guidance and the R2
"Reviewer conduct" section) and `ms-spec-final-review` gain a short "how
your verdict is adjudicated" statement addressed TO reviewers: the doctrine
by name (findings-never-out-voted, ADR-0043:17); every finding is fixed or
evidence-refuted via the audited `refutations` procedure
(`ms-panel-tally:109-117`), never dropped because the APPROVE count cleared
the threshold; the threshold is a floor, not a license (the gate Blocks on
any unresolved REQUEST_CHANGES — `gate.go:299`, `ms-panel-tally:125`); a
"minor" finding still gets adjudicated. This is teaching text for what the
binary already enforces — no gate change.

7. **R7 — Absolute scratch for ALL reviewers/fixers + clean-worktree check +
portability sweep** (bead `mindspec-fr0o`).
`ms-panel-run`, `ms-bead-fix`, and `ms-spec-final-review` generalize the
existing codex-only `/tmp` plumbing (`ms-panel-run:97-201`) into a blanket
rule: every reviewer/fixer scratch file lives at an ABSOLUTE path under
`/tmp` (or, for verdicts, the panel directory) — never a relative path,
because harness cwd-resets turn relative writes into sibling-worktree
corruption, and stray files reach `mindspec complete`'s dirty-tree Block
(gate leg 7, `gate.go:139-156` matrix) only after the mess exists.
`ms-bead-cycle` gains, adjacent to its merge terminal (`SKILL.md:116,146`):
verify the bead worktree is CLEAN (`git status --porcelain` empty) before
every `mindspec complete`, and REMOVE strays rather than letting them be
committed — stated as the advisory complement of the mechanized leg-7
Block, not a replacement. As part of the same edit, the five skills are
SWEPT for operator-environment leaks: the pre-existing
`/Users/Max/.codex/memories` at `ms-panel-run:195` is generalized to
`$HOME/.codex/memories`, and every other absolute home path or
project-incident reference found by the AC-10 scan is either generalized
to a portable form or entered in the AC-10 allowlist table with a
one-line filed reason (e.g. the pre-existing `lola spec-050` / `lola-f4a8`
case-history citations are per-hit decisions for the plan: generalize the
prose or allowlist the intentional provenance).

8. **R8 — Portable CI-parity kernel** (bead `mindspec-oxnr`).
(a) The project declares its CI invocation via the existing free-form
`commands:` map (`config.go:80`, spec 123 R7b): `commands.ci` is the
documented vocabulary key beside `build`/`test`, with `commands.test` as
the fallback when `ci` is undeclared (Commands field comment + a `"ci"`
entry in `commandOrder`, `config.go:233`; NO schema change and no new
config field — the map already accepts any key, and populated entries
already render into the managed AGENTS.md "Build & Test" section via
`RenderBuildTestSection`, `config.go:320`). Because the sorted-rest path in
`CommandLines` already renders ANY declared key, the `commandOrder` entry
alone is not observable by output presence — its effect is ORDER (`ci`
renders in vocabulary position before lexically-sorted extension keys), so
it gets its own render-order guard test (AC-17).
(b) `ms-spec-final-review` instructs one designated slot (the F2
full-regression lens is the natural home) to reproduce the project-declared
CI invocation VERBATIM (`commands.ci`, falling back to `commands.test`) on
the spec branch before sign-off, and to record an explicit advisory finding
("no declared CI invocation — CI parity not reproduced") when neither key
is declared. The existing "Not a CI substitute" line
(`ms-spec-final-review:62`) is retained and extended with the local-green ≠
CI-green rationale. (c) NO mindspec-specific invocation ships in any skill
(no `go test -short`, no `bd`-off-PATH choreography) — the rule is
abstract; the value is per-project config.

lens, re-dispatch the SAME slot with a correctness-framed persona (keep the
slot id, mark the substitution in `reviewer_id`, as the existing quota-sub

check; the panel.json `gate` field is decision-inert), so a compliant agent
runs the document panel because the installed skill says to, and a
non-compliant agent CAN skip it — by design, per ADR-0040's L4 staging.

(`internal/setup/claude.go:808,:825`) gain a pre-approve panel step: run

design:
## Requirements

Each requirement carries a hard falsifier. "Real topology" below means the shape production `complete` actually runs: merge performed in the spec worktree, locate/bind driven from the main root (`g.Root`), bead branch and worktree deleted immediately after.

**Root-of-trust principle (applies throughout R2–R5).** Two orthogonal facts are established by two different sources, and neither alone suffices:
- **OWNERSHIP — "which bead does this merge belong to?" — is the merge SUBJECT's bead-branch name.** A candidate merge is bead X's merge ONLY if its subject names `bead/X`, parsed as the bead-branch name from EITHER subject shape: `Merge bead/mindspec-X` OR git's default conflict-recovery form `Merge branch 'bead/mindspec-X' into '…'` (the branch name survives in both, so ownership is robust to the conflict-recovery variation).
- **LANDED-NESS — "did this merge actually land?" — is git TOPOLOGY**: a first-parent merge commit on `<specBranch>`, with exactly two parents, whose SECOND parent EQUALS the bead's landed tip (an EXACT second-parent match against a REAL merge), unique for that bead.

The agent-writable landed-binding metadata and a panel's `reviewed_head_sha` are a git-CORROBORATED CACHE, never authorities: they are trusted ONLY when they resolve to a merge that BOTH names this bead (ownership) AND has the exact second parent (landed-ness). A cached SHA that points at another bead's real merge fails the ownership check; one that points at no real exact merge fails the topology check; either way it is discarded, not followed. Git-corroborating a binding proves it points at a real merge — NOT that the merge is THIS bead's, which is why the subject-parsed ownership nominator is required alongside it. This stays consistent with ADR-0041 §2(ii) "never subject text ALONE": the subject only NOMINATES which bead, and topology proves landed-ness — neither is trusted alone.

Identification FAILS CLOSED — refuse — whenever ownership+landed-ness cannot be jointly established: no exact match, or the only candidates are ancestor-consistent (not exact), or competing candidates naming DIFFERENT beads. (Multiple merges that share the SAME exact second parent are NOT an ownership ambiguity — they are the same bead's re-merges; see R5's newest-exact rule.)

**Path asymmetry.** The AUTOMATIC `FindLandedMerge` path requires an EQUAL/exact corroborating datum and refuses the bare no-datum case (AC-10 pins the subject-only-spoof refusal there). The EXPLICIT, operator-invoked R4 re-attest path additionally admits subject-name nomination + topology corroboration + an audit record + operator vouching — a strictly more permissive but deliberately-gated surface; R4's nominate-then-corroborate datum MUST NOT leak into the automatic path.

Scoped to what the ACs pin: this principle closes the two concrete misattribution/spoof shapes exercised here — a cached SHA pointing at NO real exact merge (forgery, AC-2c) and one pointing at a DIFFERENT bead's real merge (ownership, AC-2d) — and the bare-fleet refusal; it does not claim to close shapes no AC exercises.

**Threat model / boundary (stated honestly).** Landed-merge identification trusts the INTEGRITY of the spec branch's git history. A party who can WRITE commits to the spec branch can forge a landed merge — author a `Merge bead/X` commit (either subject form) over an arbitrary second parent, plus a matching binding — and it will pass ownership+topology, because git history alone cannot distinguish a genuine merge from a forged one without out-of-band signatures. This is **INHERENT to any git-history-based attestation and PRE-EXISTING**: spec 121 already trusts the subject to name the bead, and that party already has full repository control AND the audited `--allow-not-ready` override (spec 124). Such an actor is therefore OUT of 125's defended threat model, and 125 attempts no git-only "fix" (there is none). What 125 DOES defend — and pins with ACs — is **accidental/mistaken misattribution and silent failure** under an honest, non-adversarial history: the wrong-cache→another-bead's-honest-merge case (AC-2d), the descendant-merge misattribution (AC-2c), the conflict-recovery subject variation (AC-1b/AC-2b), stale/non-exact bindings (AC-2c), and the silent-nil persistence failure (R1/R2). 125 does NOT worsen the pre-existing subject-trust: it ADDS topology corroboration (exact second parent + real merge) ON TOP of the subject-name ownership check spec 121 already relied on, so every path is strictly more constrained than before, never less.

1. **`complete` reliably persists the landed-binding.** After every bead→spec merge performed by `mindspec complete` (and by `FinalizeEpic`'s auto-merge leg) for a bead branch with at least one own commit, the landed-binding (`mindspec_landed_merge_sha` + `mindspec_landed_second_parent`, per the existing key contract) MUST be durably recorded on the bead — surviving into `bd show <id> --json` metadata and matching the actual first-parent merge commit on the spec branch — across the real topology, BEFORE the branch/worktree cleanup that destroys the surviving-branch datum. **WRITE vs READ (no contradiction with the R5 ownership model).** The WRITE path here (`ensureLandedBinding` during `complete`) knows the bead identity DIRECTLY — it is completing bead X — and writes the binding from that ground truth; it does NOT parse the merge subject to establish ownership, which is precisely why R1 persists **regardless of the merge's subject FORMAT** (default conflict-recovery or exact `Merge bead/X`). Subject-name parsing (the R5 ownership nominator) is a READ-path concern only: `FindLandedMerge` reading a branch-deleted bead with no surviving binding, and R4 re-attest, use it to NOMINATE which bead an unattributed historical merge belongs to. So "persist regardless of subject line" (write-time ground truth) and "subject must name bead/X" (read-time nomination) are consistent — they govern different paths. The fix MUST target the pinned root cause (Background; Requirement 5): the R1 regression fixture reproduces the real miss shape (conflict on `.beads/issues.jsonl` → default-subject recovery merge → recovery re-run) so it is RED on today's `main`, and the binding is persisted whenever the bead's work has actually landed as a merge on the spec branch. *(Residual, stated: a merge with a wholly-custom subject naming NO bead is READ-identifiable only via a binding written at complete-time — which R1's ground-truth write guarantees going forward; a historical such merge with no binding fails closed at read, which is safe.)*
   *Falsified if*: a bead with own commits, completed by a real `mindspec complete` run (including via the conflict-recovery path), lacks `mindspec_landed_merge_sha` in its bd metadata afterward; or the recorded SHAs do not match the actual merge commit and its second parent; or the binding is written only after cleanup has already deleted the branch datum.

2. **A genuine locate/bind failure is LOUD (fail-closed), never silent.** `ensureLandedBinding` MUST NOT return nil on a locate miss for a bead that DID merge. The legitimate "nothing to bind" state (a trivially-ancestor bead branch that never produced a bead→spec merge commit — a bd_close orphan that is already an ancestor of `spec` with zero own commits, so `git merge --no-ff` created no merge) MUST be POSITIVELY classified by **first-parent MEMBERSHIP**: whether the bead's tip appears as the SECOND parent of any first-parent merge on `<specBranch>` (`git log --first-parent --merges <specBranch>`, inspecting each merge's second parent — the root-of-trust exact-match test above). A bead that landed via a bead→spec MERGE has its tip as such a second parent; a true orphan does not. **A count/merge-base classifier is proven insufficient** (Background/diagnostic): after the merge, a genuinely-merged-then-ancestor bead is byte-identical to a true orphan under both `rev-list beadTip ^specBranch` (both 0) and `merge-base==tip` (both yes), because `ensureLandedBinding` runs AFTER the merge — so an own-commit-count classifier reads "nothing to bind" for a real merge and RE-HIDES the bug. "Nothing to bind" is therefore admissible ONLY when the bead's tip is the second parent of NO first-parent merge on `spec`. Any other miss — a bead whose tip IS such a second parent (it did merge) but whose merge commit cannot otherwise be located, or whose binding cannot be written — refuses via `guard.NewFailure`, suppresses branch/worktree cleanup (preserving the surviving-branch datum, so re-invocation converges per §2(ii)), and names the recovery.
   *Falsified if*: any code path swallows a bind failure or locate miss for a bead that did merge and proceeds to cleanup; or the nothing-to-bind classification is derived from own-commit-count / merge-base (which cannot distinguish a merged-then-ancestor bead from a true orphan) rather than from first-parent-membership (second-parent-of-a-merge) evidence; or the refusal deletes the branch it needs for recovery.

3. **Revert-vs-evolved discrimination is correct.** *(Round-3 note: the R3 CONTRACT and ACs are unchanged — code-verified sound in round 2; this is a PROSE-ONLY tightening to word the predicate to MATCH the `ContentSubsumedOutcome` primitive rather than backwards.)* For a two-parent merge M in the spec branch's first-parent history, the landed-identity decision is the three-way content merge (base = M^1, ours = tip, theirs = M) at the granularity of **M's CHANGED CONTENT — the region/hunks M actually introduced — NOT per-file-path**. Reading the primitive's outcomes:
   - **EVOLVED (identified)** — M's content is PRESENT at the tip. Either re-applying M's diff to the tip is a NO-OP (the merge result's tree equals the tip's tree → `SubsumptionLanded`), or it CONFLICTS because the tip advanced past base on M's own region (`SubsumptionConflict`, today's already-correct leg, preserved). "Present" includes content that later honest work moved to a DIFFERENT path, renamed, or rewrote/superseded — it still exists at the tip. This covers the `mindspec-8nhe.2` clean-divergence-but-present shape that is today's false-reject. Per-file-path reasoning is explicitly WRONG: later honest work on a DIFFERENT region of a file M also touched leaves M's own content present, so it is EVOLVED, never a revert.
   - **REVERTED (not identified)** — M's content is ABSENT at the tip: the tip sits at the base (M^1) state on M's touched content. Operationally, the three-way applies M's diff CLEANLY but the result DIFFERS from the tip (`SubsumptionCleanDivergence`) — re-applying M would RE-INTRODUCE content the tip no longer carries. This is exactly the `git revert M` shape.
   - **Stated residual (REFUSE, not over-claimed)** — M's content is ABSENT because later honest work removed it CLEANLY AND FULLY, or deleted/relocated-to-nowhere M's own paths. Absent-because-reverted and absent-because-cleanly-removed are content-INDISTINGUISHABLE, so this residual refuses too — a deliberate false-negative floor: any datum that accepted clean full removal would accept every real revert. (Contrast the EVOLVED "relocated": content moved-to-a-different-path is PRESENT and identifies; content relocated-to-NOWHERE is ABSENT and refuses.)
   **Scope — 125 fixes ONLY the CleanDivergence arm.** Spec 125's R3 change is confined to the `SubsumptionCleanDivergence`-on-evolved false-NEGATIVE (the 8nhe.2 bug: evolved-content-present wrongly refused). The `SubsumptionConflict → identified` arm (`landed.go:355-382`, the spec-121 F2-2r fix) is left UNTOUCHED. A KNOWN pre-existing residual lives on that untouched arm: an extreme revert-then-DIVERGENTLY-rewritten region can present as `SubsumptionConflict` and thus be identified — a false-POSITIVE. This is a DELIBERATE spec-121 trade-off, NOT a 125 regression: refusing the Conflict case resurrects the permanent-refusal DEADLOCK ADR-0041 §2(i) forbids (evolved work that conflicts would never converge). 125 does not worsen it — the implementation MUST change only the CleanDivergence path (grep-confirmable: the Conflict arm's behavior is byte-identical before/after 125). A precise content-presence discriminator that closes this residual WITHOUT re-introducing the deadlock is a named FOLLOW-UP, not in 125's scope (see Non-Goals).
   **Octopus/parent guard**: MindSpec bead→spec merges are exactly two-parent; the identity/discrimination MUST require a candidate with ≥2 parents AND the bead's second-parent among them, and MUST NOT attempt this discrimination on an octopus (>2-parent) or non-bead merge — such a candidate is excluded, never guessed. The discrimination mechanism (a sub-classification of `SubsumptionCleanDivergence`, the region-level three-way, or a sibling primitive) is plan-level; the boolean `ContentSubsumed`/`NetEffectLanded` projections consumed by the protected-main probe and the doctor merged-carrier suppression (spec 121 R4) keep their existing behavior.
   *Falsified if*: the evolved-content-PRESENT fixture (later first-parent commits leave M's content present but move the tip off base — removed-AND-replaced or M's region rewritten, NOT a pure delete/relocate-to-nowhere — such that today's `ContentSubsumedOutcome` returns `SubsumptionCleanDivergence`) is still refused; or later work on a DIFFERENT region of a path M touched is read as a revert of M; or a genuine `git revert M` (M's content now ABSENT) with no later rework is identified as landed; or the spec-121 revert-then-reapply and boolean-consumer contracts regress.

4. **A git-corroborated re-attest recovery — recovers the corroborable, refuses the rest.** An **explicit operator-invoked** `mindspec`-surface operation (verb naming plan-level; it MUST NOT be an implicit-writing `doctor` check — the mass-mutation vector across the merged-bead history stays gated behind a deliberate command) MUST exist to (re)attest the landed-binding of an already-merged bead. It is **fail-closed and DERIVES the binding from INDEPENDENT git topology, never from the assertion it is validating.** The bead-branch NAME (from the subject or the bead ID) may only NOMINATE a candidate; the WRITE requires a git-corroborated EXACT second-parent match under the Requirement 5 rule — ownership (the exact-matched merge's subject must name THIS bead, so a cache pointing at another bead's real merge is refused) AND landed-ness (exact second parent, real merge); fail-closed on ambiguity; for two same-second-parent exact matches, the newest names the merge while Requirement 3's content-check anchored on the OLDEST merge M₁ governs landed-vs-reverted (per Requirement 5). It writes ONLY the SHAs that scan derives. This is the deliberately more-permissive EXPLICIT path (subject-name nomination + topology + audit + operator vouching); its nominate-then-corroborate datum MUST NOT leak into the automatic `FindLandedMerge` path, which refuses the bare no-datum case (per the root-of-trust path-asymmetry note). An operator-asserted merge/second-parent pair is **NOT admissible as its own corroboration** (circular). The admissible corroborating data, each STANDALONE (matching the §2(ii) amendment enumeration): **(a)** the git-derived exact second-parent merge from the scan — this is the branch-deleted HAPPY PATH and needs NO surviving tip; **(b)** a surviving bead-branch tip, when one exists, whose SHA the exact match must equal; **(c)** a registered panel's `reviewed_head_sha`, admissible only when it equals an exact match's second parent; **(d)** an existing binding, admissible only when git-corroborated per R5. NEVER a subject match alone, NEVER an agent-asserted pair alone, and with NO per-spec or global bypass flag.
   **Honest recovery scope (not fleet-wide over-claim).** This operation RECOVERS exactly the beads whose landed merge is still git-corroborable by an exact second-parent match; it REFUSES — to the audited ADR-0035 q9ea human attested-restore exit — every bead with no corroborable exact merge (a truly-bare state: branch deleted, no binding, no exact merge, no panel-sha) rather than guessing. It therefore does NOT claim to recover the entire merged-bead history: the corroborable subset is re-attested; MF-3 (spec 124) safely fail-closes on the unrecoverable remainder; and R1 fixes attestation going FORWARD so the remainder stops growing. The q9ea exit MAY be used only for the genuinely-no-mechanical-corroboration case, is explicitly ADR-blessed (enumerated in the §2(ii) amendment, see ADR Touchpoints), is audited, and is NEVER the sole corroboration where a scan could instead derive the identity.
   **Audit — inspectable in metadata, honestly scoped.** Every write records, in bd metadata via the existing helpers (option (b) of the two honest choices — no external anchor is introduced), the acting identity/authority, the before/after binding values, the timestamp, the invoking operation, and the corroborating git datum. This record is INSPECTABLE — a wrong backfill is detectable and reconstructable BY INSPECTION of the recorded before/after values — but it lives in the same mutable bd metadata map, so it is **detectable-by-inspection, NOT cryptographically immutable/tamper-proof**; the spec claims exactly that and no more (a git-trailer/append-only external anchor is a deliberate non-goal here). On an already-correct binding it converges as a no-op; on a contradictory existing binding it follows the G3-1 discipline (overwrite only with the git-corroborated exact identity, recording the prior value in the audit — never silently keep the contradiction, never write an uncorroborated replacement). Refusals name the state and the forward exit.
   *Falsified if*: the operation attests on a subject-only match, an agent-asserted pair, or any non-exact (ancestor-only) candidate; or writes a binding not derived from an independent git exact-match scan; or a crafted subject-matching decoy merge (or a descendant bead's merge, per R5) gets attested; or it claims to recover a bead with no git-corroborable exact merge instead of refusing to the audited exit; or a write leaves no inspectable before/after/actor audit record; or the spec claims the metadata audit is tamper-proof rather than detectable-by-inspection; or a bypass flag disables corroboration; or the surface writes bindings implicitly (e.g. from a `doctor` run) rather than under explicit operator invocation.

5. **Merge-candidate identity is an EXACT second-parent match, fail-closed on ambiguity.** Landed-merge identification MUST NOT be gated on the merge commit carrying the exact `"Merge "+beadBranch` subject; a merge whose SECOND PARENT identifies the bead's landed tip MUST be identifiable even when its subject is git's default conflict-recovery form `Merge branch 'bead/x' into 'spec/…'`. But an ANCESTOR-consistent match misattributes across beads: if bead Y branches off `spec` AFTER bead X lands, X's tip is an ANCESTOR of Y's tip, so a naive newest-first `IsAncestor(X_tip, secondParent)` scan returns Y's merge M_Y for `FindLandedMerge(X)` — the revert-leg then reads M_Y's content, so a genuine revert of only X's content reads as landed. Per the root-of-trust principle above, positive identification therefore REQUIRES a git-corroborated EXACT second-parent match, and REFUSES on every ambiguity:
   - **Ownership + landed-ness are BOTH required.** A candidate is bead X's landed merge only if (ownership) its subject names `bead/X` — parsed from either `Merge bead/X` or the default `Merge branch 'bead/X' into '…'` form — AND (landed-ness) it is a two-parent first-parent merge on `spec` whose second parent EQUALS X's landed tip (an EXACT match against a real merge). An ancestor-only-consistent candidate is NEVER a positive identification on its own; a candidate that exact-matches but whose subject names a DIFFERENT bead is rejected (it is that other bead's merge). Ownership matching MUST use FULL bead-branch-name EQUALITY (the parsed token equals `bead/<full-id>` exactly), never `HasPrefix`/`Contains` — so a prefix-colliding pair like `mindspec-8nhe.1` vs `mindspec-8nhe.12` never cross-matches: a collision fails SAFE (no positive ID → refuse), never a false attribution. The parsed subject token is COMPARED DATA, never a git operand, and is `termsafe.Escape`-d before appearing in any refusal message (the spec-116/120 G2-1 discipline for agent-writable text).
   - **The agent-writable binding / panel-sha is a git-corroborated CACHE, never an authority.** A recorded `mindspec_landed_second_parent` (or `reviewed_head_sha`) is trusted ONLY when it resolves to a real merge that BOTH exact-matches the bead's tip AND whose subject names THIS bead. A forged/stale cache that points at no real exact merge (fails topology) OR at another bead's real merge (fails ownership) yields no valid identification — it is discarded, and identification refuses rather than following the cache. This closes both the no-real-match forgery (G1-3, AC-2c) and the another-bead's-real-merge misattribution (G2-R3-B1/F1-7, AC-2d).
   - **No exact-and-owned match ⟹ REFUSE (never newest-ancestor).** When no first-parent merge both names the bead and exact-matches its tip — and only ancestor-consistent or differently-owned candidates remain (reachable in the branch-deleted fleet state via an ancestor `reviewed_head_sha`, where a panel reviewed an EARLIER head, or via a cache pointing at a non-exact SHA) — identification FAILS CLOSED (`*LandedMergeNoEvidence` / refusal), NEVER a newest-ancestor pick. This "refuse on ambiguity" applies to candidates with DIFFERENT second parents or competing bead-ownership — genuine ambiguity about WHICH merge is this bead's.
   - **Two merges sharing the SAME exact second parent ⟹ same bead's re-merges: identify the merge as newest, but base the content-check on the ORIGINAL landing.** A revert-then-reapply or a re-merge lands the SAME second parent (and the SAME owning bead) on `spec` more than once. These are NOT an ownership ambiguity — they are one bead's repeated merges of the same tip — so the merge COMMIT reported (the `*LandedMerge.SHA`) is the NEWEST such same-second-parent exact match (nearest the tip on the first-parent chain). But the landed-vs-reverted CONTENT-CHECK MUST NOT be anchored on that newest merge: a later re-merge's own `M^1` can itself be the POST-REVERT state, so Requirement 3's three-way taken over the newest merge reads "no change" and MIS-attests a bead whose content is actually reverted at the tip (G2-R4-B1). The content-check REUSES Requirement 3's discrimination VERBATIM — it defines NO three-way of its own — parameterized by **M = the OLDEST same-second-parent merge M₁** (the pre-first-landing anchor): Requirement 3's three-way `(base = M₁^1, ours = current tip, theirs = M₁)` — equivalently `ContentSubsumedOutcome(base = M₁^1, ref = M₁, target = tip)`, exactly R3's argument mapping with M = M₁. The newest merge M₂ governs ONLY the reported `*LandedMerge.SHA`; it supplies NEITHER the base NOR the `theirs = M` merge of the R3 check. This yields: a revert-then-re-merge where the bead's landed content is absent at the tip → `SubsumptionCleanDivergence` → REVERTED → refuse (never `SubsumptionLanded` via a post-revert no-op anchor). The single-merge case is identical to R3: one merge ⇒ M₁ == M₂ == that merge ⇒ R3's `(base = M^1, ours = tip, theirs = M)` exactly. This is disambiguation AMONG same-owner exact matches only; it never promotes an ancestor-only or differently-owned candidate, so it does not contradict the fail-closed-on-ambiguity principle (which governs different-owner/non-exact candidates).
   The three identity sites — `MergeInto` (`gitutil/gitops.go:154`), `locateLandedMergeByIdentity` (`mindspec_executor.go:1469`), `FindLandedMerge` (`lifecycle/landed.go:257`) — MUST identify by this ownership-named, exact-match-required, fail-closed-on-ambiguity rule. The anti-forgery posture is UNCHANGED and consistent with §2(ii): the subject NOMINATES ownership but is never landed-ness evidence ALONE, and an agent-writable cache alone is likewise inadmissible unless git-corroborated to an exact, owned merge. Additionally, the conflict-recovery message (`beadToSpecConflictFailure:1623`) MUST print a recovery that produces an IDENTIFIABLE merge — supplying `-m "Merge <beadBranch>"` on the recovery `git merge --no-ff` line (and/or relying on the second-parent identification above making the subject irrelevant) — so an operator following it verbatim does not strand the binding.
   *Falsified if*: a bead whose merge commit carries git's default `Merge branch '…' into '…'` subject but whose second parent is the bead's landed tip is not identified as landed; or, given bead X and a later descendant bead Y both merged with default subjects, `FindLandedMerge(X)` returns M_Y instead of M_X, whether the exact-match for X exists (AC-2b) or NOT (AC-2c: with no binding, an ancestor `reviewed_head_sha`, and a descendant merge present, identification returns the newest ancestor-consistent merge instead of REFUSING); or a cached SHA pointing at a merge whose subject names a DIFFERENT bead is followed to a positive identification instead of being discarded (AC-2d); or a `git revert` of only X's content is not refused because the revert-leg read the wrong merge; or a revert-then-re-merge-of-the-same-second-parent whose content is ABSENT at the current tip is attested as landed because the content-check used the newest re-merge's `M^1` base instead of the original-landing base / content-at-tip (G2-R4-B1); or ownership matches by prefix/substring so a prefix-colliding bead id cross-attributes instead of failing safe; or identity is accepted on a subject/cache hint with no git-corroborated exact AND owned merge; or the printed conflict-recovery recovery still yields an unidentifiable merge.

6. **Regression evidence, CI-hermetic.** Every fixed class MUST be pinned by an automated test that is RED on today's `main` (or on fix-revert) and runs in CI's bd-less `go test -short ./...` lane: (a) a real-git e2e through the production `CompleteBead` path in the real topology — INCLUDING the pinned conflict-recovery miss shape (add/add conflict on `.beads/issues.jsonl` → default-subject recovery merge → recovery re-run → binding today absent) — merge, binding persisted, branch deleted, followed by `lifecycle.FindLandedMerge` positively identifying the merge for the branch-DELETED bead (the exact contract spec 124's MF-3 consumes); (b) an explicit `*LandedMergeNoEvidence` fail-closed test preserving the no-datum refusal; (c) the evolved-vs-true-revert discrimination pair of Requirement 3 (evolved shape = tip-moved-BEYOND-base on M's touched content, NOT a pure delete/relocate); (d) the loud-miss refusal of Requirement 2, driven by a merged-WITH-own-commits bead whose locate is forced to miss (not the orphan fixture, which cannot distinguish a correct impl from a re-hiding one); (e) the exact-second-parent identification of Requirement 5 INCLUDING the multi-bead X-then-descendant-Y misattribution guard BOTH when the exact match exists (AC-2b) AND when it does not — the fail-closed-on-ambiguity case (AC-2c), the ownership check that discards a cache pointing at another bead's real merge (AC-2d), the revert-then-re-merge content-base masked-revert guard (AC-2e), and the full-name-equality no-prefix-collision guard (AC-2f); (f) the `FinalizeEpic` auto-merge/already-ancestor producer legs persisting the binding. Hermeticity per the spec-119 bd-less no-skip-gating convention: bd-touching legs run through the existing injectable seams (`mergeBindingFn`/`mergeBindingReadFn`) backed hermetically, with the seam DEFAULTS pinned to the real `bead.MergeMetadata`/`bead.GetMetadata` symbols by an anti-drift test (the `netEffectLandedFn` AC-17 pattern), so the gate cannot go hollow — no new test may skip-when-bd-missing, and any test that genuinely requires a real `bd` FATALs rather than skips when its declared environment lacks it.
   *Falsified if*: any of the six classes lacks a test that fails on today's behavior; or a new gating test silently skips in the bd-less CI lane; or the seam defaults can be rewired off the real bd write path without a test going red.
