title: [124-impl-readiness-gate] Bead 1: Mechanical-floor engine + `bead ready-check` verb + the readiness fixture pair
description:
R1 + R2 + R6 in full, plus R7a's first slice (the `ready-check` ceremony
pin). The deterministic core: four signals, a read-only report verb, and
the CI-pinned NEGATIVE/POSITIVE fixture pair that makes the gate
falsifiable both ways.

**Steps**
1. `internal/bead/readiness.go` (new, execution-domain): the two
   dedicated metadata key constants
   (`MetaKeyReadinessOverride = "mindspec_readiness_override"`,
   `MetaKeyReadinessAttempt = "mindspec_readiness_attempt"`) with doc
   comments stating the carrier contract: written only via
   `MergeMetadata` by their owning verbs (Beads 2/3), NEVER read by any
   mechanical signal, advisory-not-lifecycle (ADR-0023).
2. The sub-package `internal/validate/readiness/` (new — see the
   placement rationale in the preamble):
   - `report.go`: the `ReadinessReport` type (four per-signal results —
     stable IDs `MF-1`..`MF-4`, PASS/FAIL, evidence path +
     offending/missing element, one recovery lever per FAIL) and its
     renderer as a reachable exported API, so Bead 2's `next` refusal
     reuses it (ADR-0040 no-restate).
   - `readiness.go`: the engine. `EvaluateReadiness(root, beadID)` returns
     a `ReadinessReport`. Ingress: `idvalidate.BeadID`. Owning-spec
     resolution from LINEAGE (the `internal/complete/complete.go:369`
     fail-closed pattern via `phase` epic lookup — never cwd; real lookup
     errors refuse, they never degrade to cwd resolution). Bead index
     N = the ID's numeric suffix, mapped positionally to
     `work_chunks[N-1]` / the Nth `## Bead` section via
     `internal/validate`'s existing plan frontmatter + section parsing.
     It declares the **package-level bd seam covering EVERY bd read
     `EvaluateReadiness` performs** (plan-gate G2-BDLESS-ENGINE-SEAM),
     func vars defaulting to the real `internal/bead` helpers (the
     `adr_memo.go:20` precedent). The COMPLETE bd read-set, each routed
     through the seam so the engine is fully hermetic with bd absent (no
     `t.Skip`):
     - the **bead's OWN record** — its bd description (MF-2 harvest
       context + the MF-4 description scan) and, indirectly, the plan
       path resolved from lineage (MF-1's `## Bead N` section, MF-2's
       plan-section harvest, MF-4's plan-section scan all read the plan
       FILE, not bd — but the bead→spec LINEAGE lookup that locates the
       plan is a bd/phase read and is behind the seam);
     - each **dependency edge's bd record** — the dependency ID list, and
       per dep its bd STATUS/closure (MF-3);
     (MF-3's landed-merge leg is `lifecycle.FindLandedMerge`, a git read,
     not bd — it is exercised over real temp repos, not faked.) No MF
     signal reaches `internal/bead` except through these func vars, so
     the engine unit tests swap them ALL to in-memory returns and consult
     no real bd for the bead's-own-record reads OR the dependency reads.
3. The four signals, exactly as R2 pins them:
   - **MF-1**: section exists; `**Acceptance Criteria**` block has ≥1
     entry that is not the scaffold's angle-bracketed template literal
     (matched against the actual `scaffoldPlan` emission);
     `work_chunks[N-1].key_file_paths` non-empty, no `path/to/file.go`.
   - **MF-2**: harvest the bead's OWN claimed `R<n>`/`AC-<n>` tokens
     (bd description + its plan section) under the three harvest rules
     from the preamble — foreign-citation exclusion, code-span/code-fence
     exclusion, and clause-enumerator normalization (`AC-9(i)`→base
     `AC-9`). Resolve each against spec.md by the exact rule — whole-token
     OR base-of-sub-lettered for letterless claims (`R5` via `R5a`;
     `R5(b)`→`R5b` only when the letter form targets a real spec token),
     EXACT token only for genuinely sub-lettered claims, numeric-prefix
     never resolves (identifier-boundary matching).
   - **MF-3**: for every bd dependency edge (authoritative — the prose
     `**Depends on**` section is never parsed): dep closed in bd AND
     `lifecycle.FindLandedMerge(root, specBranch, depID)` returns a
     positive `*LandedMerge`. FAIL fail-closed on ANY error, with
     state-specific messages: open dep; `ErrLandedMergeNotFound` (the
     2u0u closed-but-unmerged split); `*LandedMergeNoEvidence` (the
     spec-121 uncorroborated candidate); infra errors verbatim. No
     file-existence leg (spec Out of Scope).
   - **MF-4**: whole-word `TBD` / whole-phrase `OPEN QUESTION`
     (case-insensitive) over the bead's plan section + bd description,
     scanned OUTSIDE inline-code spans and fenced code blocks; unchecked
     `- [ ]` items only under a designated blocking region
     (`**Blocking Questions**` / `**Open Questions**` / `**Blocked on**`
     sub-blocks). BOTH the token scan AND the blocking-region-HEADER
     detection exclude backtick-spanned/fenced text (plan-gate F2-2) — so
     a section that merely NAMES `**Blocking Questions**` inside a code
     span (as this plan's Bead-1 section does when describing MF-4) is not
     read as an actual blocking region. Routine
     `**Verification**`/`**Acceptance Criteria**` checklists never
     blocking.
4. `cmd/mindspec/bead_ready.go` (new file, own `init()` on `beadCmd` —
   `cmd/mindspec/bead.go` is NOT edited): the `ready-check <bead-id>`
   subcommand, calling `readiness.EvaluateReadiness` and rendering via
   the sub-package's `report.go` renderer. Prints one line per signal;
   all bead/plan-derived text through `termsafe.Escape`; exit 0 all-pass;
   on any FAIL exit non-zero via `guard.NewFailure` carrying one
   `recovery:` line per failing signal (edit the named plan section;
   `mindspec complete <dep-id>`; `--allow-not-ready` documented as the
   claim-time override). No bd write, no git write, no file write on ANY
   path.
5. Fixtures + engine tests: `internal/validate/readiness/fixtures.go`
   (the exported NEGATIVE/POSITIVE builders per Testing Strategy) and
   `internal/validate/readiness/readiness_test.go`: MF-2 all-classes
   table (AC-14 i-iv, both false-positive-refusal and
   false-negative-refusal arms) PLUS the enumerator-parenthetical arm
   pinning the FORM-based Roman-vs-sub-letter classification: a claimed
   `AC-9(i)` PASSes via base `AC-9` EVEN WHEN a coincidental `AC-9i`
   sub-token also exists in spec.md (form wins — collision-free), a
   claimed `R5(b)` resolves to exact `R5b`, and a genuinely
   dangling-as-written literal `AC-9i` FAILs — so strict-exact,

## Requirements

Each requirement carries a hard falsifier. "Readiness fixture pair" below means the two committed test fixtures of R6: NEGATIVE (deliberately under-specified) and POSITIVE (well-specified, carrying the repo's ordinary benign features).

1. **A deterministic, read-only readiness verb: `mindspec bead ready-check <bead-id>`.** The verb resolves the bead's owning spec from its lineage (never from cwd — the ADR-0041 lesson from `complete`), evaluates the four mechanical signals of R2, and prints a per-signal report: one line per signal with a stable signal ID (`MF-1`..`MF-4`), `PASS`/`FAIL`, and for each FAIL the evidence (file path + the offending or missing element). Exit 0 when all four pass; on any FAIL, exit non-zero via `internal/guard` with one `recovery:` line per failing signal. The verb performs **no mutation**: no bd writes, no git writes, no file writes — two consecutive runs against unchanged state produce identical output and leave `git status` and bd state untouched. Malformed bead IDs are refused at ingress via `idvalidate.BeadID` (the existing `cmd/mindspec/bead.go` pattern). All bead/plan-derived text rendered in the report passes through `termsafe.Escape` before reaching the terminal (bead descriptions and plan prose are agent-authored free text — the spec 113/120 trust-boundary rule).
   *Falsified if*: the NEGATIVE fixture exits 0 or the POSITIVE fixture exits non-zero; or any FAIL line lacks a signal ID or a recovery line; or a run mutates bd state, git state, or any file; or a bead description containing terminal-escape bytes reaches the report unescaped.

2. **The mechanical floor — four signals, all mechanical, each grounded against shipped artifacts, none judging prose quality.** The bead-index `N` is the bead ID's numeric suffix, mapping positionally to `work_chunks[N-1]`/`bead_ids[N-1]` per the spec 097 contract in `internal/validate/plan.go`.
   - **MF-1 — plan section concrete-by-structure**: the plan's `## Bead N` section exists; its `**Acceptance Criteria**` block contains at least one entry that is not the scaffold's angle-bracketed AC placeholder (the "Specific, measurable criterion for this bead" template literal emitted by `scaffoldPlan`, `internal/approve/spec.go`); and `work_chunks[N-1].key_file_paths` is non-empty and contains no scaffold placeholder (`path/to/file.go`). Authoritative files-in-scope is the frontmatter, not prose (spec 097 R3/R4) — MF-1 never parses prose "Files:" lines.
   - **MF-2 — claimed Rs/ACs resolve, by an EXACT rule**: MF-2 harvests only the bead's OWN claimed `R<n>` / `AC-<n>` tokens — those declared as its criteria (its bd-description claim context and its `## Bead N` plan section), NOT tokens appearing inside a prose citation of another spec (a named foreign-spec reference like "the spec 123 AC-17 pattern" is a citation, not a claim, and is excluded from harvesting; harvest heuristic plan-level, pinned by the POSITIVE fixture's benign feature (iv)). Each harvested token MUST resolve in the owning `spec.md` by this pinned rule: **(letterless claim)** a claimed letterless token `X` (`R5`, `AC-1`) resolves iff spec.md contains, as a **whole token** (identifier-boundary delimited), either `X` itself OR any sub-lettered form `X<letter>` (`R5` resolves via `R5a`; a parenthesized claim `R5(b)` normalizes to `R5b` before matching); **(sub-lettered claim)** a claimed sub-lettered token `X<letter>` (`R5a`, `AC-2b`) resolves iff spec.md contains that EXACT sub-lettered token — never the bare `R5`, never a sibling `R5b`. **Numeric-prefix matches NEVER resolve**: `AC-1` does not resolve via `AC-19`, `R1` not via `R10` (boundary-enforced; `AC-1` and `AC-19` are distinct tokens). A claimed token with no resolving counterpart is a dangling promise → FAIL naming it.
   - **MF-3 — dependencies closed AND landed-merged (branch-deletion-tolerant)**: for every bd dependency edge of the bead (the authoritative source — bd edges wired from `work_chunks[].depends_on`, spec 097 R3; the prose `**Depends on**` section is explicitly non-authoritative and is not parsed), the dependency bead MUST be **closed** in bd AND its work MUST be a **landed merge into the spec branch** as determined by `internal/lifecycle.FindLandedMerge` — which tolerates the deleted `bead/<id>` branch that `mindspec complete` leaves behind (`mindspec_executor.go:468`) and corroborates via `mindspec_landed_*` binding / branch-tip / first-parent subject scan. The general rule is **PASS iff `FindLandedMerge` returns a positive `*LandedMerge`; FAIL (fail-closed) on ANY error** — a dependency that is open, or closed but for which `FindLandedMerge` returns `ErrLandedMergeNotFound` (the 2u0u closed-but-unmerged split state — no first-parent merge positively identified, `landed.go:35`) OR `*LandedMergeNoEvidence` (the spec-121 case: a subject-scan candidate exists but no admissible corroboration, `landed.go:48`), FAILs with a state-specific message and a recovery line; no error is ever silently treated as "merged" (never a false PASS). **Helper-locatability is NOT a mechanical file-existence check** — `key_file_paths` is the dependency's *context surface*, not a produced-artifact contract (spec 097 R4), and a valid dep may delete/rename/merely-inspect a path; whether the helper API is actually usable is the semantic judgment SR-3 (the subagent reads the files the prompt names). **Drift scope (recorded):** MF-3 evaluates bd-edge state only; a `work_chunks[N-1].depends_on` entry hand-added after approval that was never wired to a bd edge is out of MF-3's scope by design — the named backstops are SR-3 (an absent helper surfaces at Phase 0) and the cycle's step-0.1 `bd ready`-vs-plan reconciliation.
   - **MF-4 — no GENUINE blocking marker (routine checklists AND quoted literals excluded)**: FAIL only on (a) the token `TBD` (whole word, case-insensitive) or the phrase `OPEN QUESTION` (whole-word/phrase, case-insensitive) appearing in the bead's `## Bead N` plan section or bd description **outside** any inline-code span (`` `…` ``) or fenced code block (` ``` `) — so a bead that QUOTES those literals as fixture data or described behavior is not false-refused, and the whole-phrase qualifier stops `OPEN QUESTION` from substring-matching the `Open Questions` section convention (5 such hits in plans 121–123); or (b) an unchecked `- [ ]` item appearing under a **designated blocking region** — a `**Blocking Questions**`, `**Open Questions**`, or `**Blocked on**` sub-block inside the bead section. Routine `**Verification**` and `**Acceptance Criteria**` checklists (the scaffold convention; spec 123 Bead 1 carries ~17 such entries) are EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED and are never blocking. Spec-level open questions remain gated at spec-approve (`internal/validate/spec.go` `open-question` error) and are not re-scanned here.
   *Falsified if*: any signal PASSes on the NEGATIVE fixture's planted defect for that signal (placeholder AC; a dangling `AC-99` AND a prefix-dangling `AC-1` present only as `AC-19`; a closed-but-unmerged dependency; a genuine `TBD`/blocking-region marker); or any signal FAILs on the POSITIVE fixture (which carries scaffold Verification/AC checkboxes, a bare-base `R`/`AC` claim resolving via a sub-lettered spec token, and a prose pattern-citation); or MF-3 false-PASSes any `FindLandedMerge` error state (`ErrLandedMergeNotFound` or `*LandedMergeNoEvidence`), or false-FAILs a dependency completed normally via `mindspec complete` (branch deleted); or MF-2 resolves `AC-1` against only `AC-19`, or resolves a sub-lettered claim `R5a` against a bare `R5` or a sibling `R5b`; or MF-4 FAILs a routine Verification/AC checkbox or a `TBD`/`OPEN QUESTION` quoted inside an inline-code or fenced span. (A review-time obligation, not a mechanical falsifier: the bead panel confirms no signal's implementation reads prose *quality* rather than presence/resolution/merged-ness — the POSITIVE-fixture pin is the mechanical backstop for that class.)

3. **`mindspec next` gates the claim on the mechanical floor (gate-before-mutate), with a durable override.** After bead selection and before **any** mutation (no `bd update --claim`, no `bead/<id>` branch, no worktree), `next` evaluates R2 against the selected bead. On NOT READY it refuses: prints the per-signal report, exits non-zero, and leaves bd state, branches, and worktrees byte-identical to before the invocation; the refusal's recovery lines name the per-signal fixes plus the two escape hatches (`mindspec bead ready-check <id>` for the standalone report; re-run with `--allow-not-ready` to claim deliberately). `--allow-not-ready` proceeds past a failing floor AND records a **durable override marker** on the bead (a dedicated bd metadata key naming the overridden signals) so the later dispatch-ingress re-check (R4) honors the deliberate claim instead of re-blocking it; a warning naming every failing signal is emitted (the override is visible in the transcript, never silent). `--allow-not-ready` is distinct from the existing `--force` (session-freshness only, `cmd/mindspec/next.go`), which MUST remain orthogonal and gains no readiness authority. A passing floor adds no interactive step and no output beyond a single OK line.
   *Falsified if*: `next` against the NEGATIVE fixture's bead claims it, creates a branch, or creates a worktree without `--allow-not-ready`; or the refusal path leaves any mutation behind; or `--allow-not-ready` proceeds without recording the durable override marker or without naming the failing signals; or `--force` alone bypasses the readiness gate; or `next` against the POSITIVE fixture's bead is refused or prompts interactively.

4. **`/ms-bead-impl` runs the ready-check as an UNCONDITIONAL dispatch ingress and stages the semantic Phase 0.** (a) The `mindspec bead ready-check <bead-id>` re-check MUST run on **every** dispatch path as an ingress step **before** the Phase-A-skip decision — so a supplied `prompt-path` (which today skips Phase A, `SKILL.md:23`) and the documented manual `bd update`/`git worktree add` fallback cannot bypass it. This covers the stale-claim window: a bead claimed before this spec ships, or a plan/spec edited after the claim, is caught at dispatch. On FAIL the dispatch STOPS (no prompt staged, no dispatch) UNLESS the bead carries the R3 durable override marker for the failing signals, in which case dispatch proceeds with a warning naming the overridden signals — so a deliberately force-claimed bead has a coherent path to implementation rather than dead-ending. (b) The staged-prompt skeleton gains a mandatory **`## Phase 0 — readiness review (before any edit)`** section instructing the subagent to evaluate five semantic signals against the quoted spec/plan material (and any `## Readiness Clarification` entries surfaced into the prompt per R8) before touching any file: **SR-1** the plan steps + ACs are implementable without inventing unstated behavior; **SR-2** each claimed AC is decidable (a concrete pass/fail check exists or is directly constructible); **SR-3** every helper the prompt says to reuse actually exists at the stated import path with the stated shape; **SR-4** the bead does not contradict the spec or a sibling bead's landed work; **SR-5** no ambiguity remains that would force the subagent to choose between materially different implementations. If any signal fails, the subagent makes **zero commits** and returns a report whose first line is exactly `NOT READY: <bead-id>` followed by reasons numbered by **ordinal** (1, 2, …; each unique within the report), each tagged with its signal ID and quoting the offending or missing span verbatim (the grill's anchoring discipline) plus the concrete unblocking question. The Phase 0 block MUST also carry the clarification-handling rule (R8): on a re-dispatch, any cited NOT-READY reason ordinal lacking a mapped, span-grounded clarification entry MUST be re-reported NOT READY, and the reviewer judges whether the clarification RESOLVES the ambiguity against a cited authoritative span — a bare "it's ready" never suffices. If all pass, Phase 0 costs one line ("Phase 0: READY") and coding proceeds.
   *Falsified if*: the shipped `ms-bead-impl` SKILL.md runs the ready-check inside a phase that a `prompt-path` or manual-fallback dispatch can skip (it must be unconditional ingress); or dispatch proceeds on a mechanical FAIL with no override marker; or the prompt skeleton lacks any SR signal ID, the zero-commit rule, the `NOT READY: <bead-id>` first-line + ordinal-numbered verbatim-span shape, or the clarification-handling rule (pinned by AC-5/AC-6).

5. **`/ms-bead-cycle` routes NOT READY as its own outcome — pre-damage triage, not an impl failure.** A subagent return whose first line is `NOT READY: <bead-id>` is handled distinctly from every existing outcome: **no panel round is consumed** (nothing was implemented), and the outcome does **not** count toward `loop.halt.max_consecutive_impl_failures` (that brake, `internal/config/config.go:382`, stops *repeated failed implementations* — post-damage; NOT READY is the pre-damage refusal that prevents them, and conflating the two would punish the gate for working). On a NOT READY the cycle chooses exactly one of two dispositions: **ACCEPT** (the default) — **halt the bead and surface the reasons** with the routing instruction (revise the plan/spec section the reasons quote, then re-dispatch); or **DISAGREE/clarify** — the bounded R8 loop. Either way it **never routes a NOT READY into `/ms-bead-fix`** (there is no implementation to fix), and the bead worktree remains intact (zero commits). Autopilot treats an ACCEPTed NOT READY as the existing bead-level halt class.
   *Falsified if*: the shipped `ms-bead-cycle` SKILL.md routes a NOT-READY return into the panel or the fix loop, counts it toward the impl-failure halt counter, or lacks the ACCEPT halt-and-surface routing (pinned by AC-7's content test).

6. **The gate is falsifiable in both directions via a committed readiness fixture pair modeled on real shipped beads.** The repo carries, under the test tree, (a) a NEGATIVE fixture with exactly one planted defect per mechanical signal: a placeholder-only AC block (MF-1); a claimed `AC-99` absent from spec.md AND a prefix-dangling `AC-1` whose spec.md contains only `AC-19` (MF-2, both false-negative-and-false-positive classes); a dependency bead closed-but-unmerged with its branch **present** (MF-3, the 2u0u split); and a genuine blocking marker — a `TBD` token and/or an unchecked item in a `**Blocking Questions**` region (MF-4). (b) a POSITIVE fixture: a fully-specified bead section modeled faithfully on spec 123 Bead 1 that MUST carry, and still PASS, the benign features that distinguish a real shipped section from a sterile ideal — (i) an unchecked `**Verification**` checklist in scaffold shape; (ii) at least one AC entry in `- [ ] AC-n — …` checkbox form; (iii) a bare-base `R`/`AC` claim whose spec.md counterpart is sub-lettered only (exercising the MF-2 base-resolution rule); (iv) a prose citation of another spec's pattern (e.g. "the spec 123 AC-17 pattern") that must NOT be harvested as a dangling claim; with named files, resolvable ACs, and a merged (branch-deleted) dependency. CI pins the NEGATIVE fixture to FAIL naming all four planted signals and the POSITIVE fixture to PASS with zero findings — a sanitized positive fixture (stripped of the benign features) is itself a falsification.
   *Falsified if*: either fixture is absent; or the NEGATIVE fixture passes while any planted defect goes unflagged; or the POSITIVE fixture passes while the verb reports any finding against it; or the POSITIVE fixture lacks any of the four enumerated benign features (the sanitized-fixture trapdoor).

7. **Surface inflation is paid for, and prose cannot drift from the binary.** (a) The spec-122 ceremony non-inflation baseline (`cmd/mindspec/ceremony_guard_test.go`) is updated in the same bead that adds each new surface — `bead ready-check`, `bead clarify`, and `--allow-not-ready` — the guard trips red on each and the baseline update is the deliberate, reviewed acknowledgment; the guard test itself is never weakened or deleted (guard-weakening detection is a review-time obligation of the bead panel — AC-9(i) provides the git-diff evidence). (b) Skill↔binary contract pins (the spec 123 AC-17 pattern): content tests assert the shipped `ms-bead-impl` SKILL.md contains the unconditional-ingress ready-check invocation, the Phase 0 block with the five SR IDs, the `NOT READY:` ordinal-report contract, AND the clarification-handling rule; and the shipped `ms-bead-cycle` SKILL.md contains the NOT-READY routing of R5 and the R8 loop contract — so a future skill edit cannot silently detach the prose layer from the verb.
   *Falsified if*: any new surface lands without a same-bead ceremony-baseline update; or the `ms-bead-impl` clarification-handling rule (R8 anti-browbeat) can be removed from the shipped prompt with every pinned test still green; or either skill's mandated content can be removed without a test going red.

8. **The semantic clarification loop — a bounded, layer-scoped, GROUNDED, audited DISAGREE disposition (not a bypass).** When Phase 0 returns a semantic `NOT READY: <bead-id>` and the orchestrator judges the concern resolvable, `/ms-bead-cycle` MAY answer it **once per bead** instead of halting:
   - **(a) Carrier OFF the mechanical scan surface.** The clarification is written to a **dedicated bd metadata key** (via a thin `mindspec bead clarify <id>` verb — or equivalent single new surface — wrapping the existing `internal/bead` `MergeMetadata` helper; a skill LLM cannot call Go helpers and raw `bd update --metadata` is ADR-0035-banned). The key is one MF-2/MF-4 **never scan** (they read the bd description and plan section, not this key), so a clarification whose prose legitimately contains an `AC-<n>` token, `TBD`, or `- [ ]` cannot flip a mechanical PASS→FAIL — invariance holds by construction, both directions.
   - **(b) Grounded, reason-keyed entries.** The record is an append-only **readiness attempt**: the original NOT-READY report (each reason's **ordinal**, verbatim reason/question, and signal tag), plus one clarification entry per cited ordinal, each carrying `{ordinal, verbatim reason, concrete answer, source span in spec.md / plan.md / landed code}`. `bead clarify` REJECTS an entry that names an ordinal absent from the recorded report or that omits a source span — this is a **presence** check only (the entry must cite a span); whether the cited span actually SUPPORTS the answer is a semantic judgment left to the fresh Phase-0 subagent (ADR-0040: the binary validates structure, the model judges meaning), not verified by the verb. A clarification may DISAMBIGUATE existing authority but may not CREATE new normative behavior; when no authoritative span supports the answer, the correct disposition is ACCEPT (revise the plan/spec), not clarify.
   - **(c) Surfaced into re-dispatch, and JUDGED not just mapped.** `/ms-bead-impl`'s dispatch ingress reads the attempt record and injects its clarification entries (keyed by ordinal) into the re-dispatched prompt's Phase 0 section. The fresh Phase-0 subagent re-reports NOT READY for any cited ordinal lacking a mapped, span-grounded entry, AND judges whether each clarification actually RESOLVES the ambiguity against its cited span — a syntactically reason-keyed but unsupported "ignore it / it's ready" does not flip the verdict.
   - **(d) Bounded — one round PER BEAD, then forced revision.** The cap is categorical and durable: the presence of ANY prior readiness-attempt record on the bead means the single clarification round is already consumed — the next NOT READY (regardless of whether it repeats an addressed reason or raises a NEW one) MUST escalate to the ACCEPT disposition (plan/spec revision). No second `clarify` write is permitted; `bead clarify` refuses when an attempt record already exists (recovery: escalate to revision). This survives orchestrator restart / context loss because the marker is durable bd state, not transcript memory. The cap assumes a **single writer per bead** — the honest, grounded assumption, since `/ms-bead-cycle` is serial per bead by design (it claims and drives exactly one bead at a time; `ms-bead-cycle` SKILL.md "Don't claim multiple beads at once"). Two concurrent orchestrators racing `MergeMetadata` on one bead (an ordinary lost-update window) is out of scope for the cap's guarantee and is not defended against here; the serial-per-bead cycle is the enforced invariant that makes the single-writer assumption hold in practice.
   - **(e) Layer boundary + DERIVED audit resolution.** A clarification affects only the semantic Phase-0 SR signals; the mechanical floor (`ready-check` MF-1..MF-4, run by `next` and by the R4 dispatch ingress) is evaluated as if the record were absent — a bead failing any mechanical signal stays NOT READY regardless of any clarification (a missing AC, dangling `AC-n`, or unmerged dependency never passes via clarification; the blunt override for a known-acceptable mechanical FAIL is `--allow-not-ready`, recorded as a bypass). The append-only **attempt record** (original ordinal-keyed report + the grounded clarification entries) is the single durable audit anchor and is written exactly once — consistent with the (d) one-write cap and the AC-9 two-verbs accounting. The **terminal disposition is DERIVED, not a second write**: READY-after-clarification = a successful re-dispatch occurring after the record exists; escalated-to-revision = the forced-revision path a repeat NOT-READY takes (the cycle transcript + the bead's subsequent state show which). A fresh `bd show` reveals the NOT-READY → clarification trail durably; the outcome is inferable from it plus the subsequent re-review, so no additional write surface (a `--finalize` verb or a two-phase idempotent `clarify`) is introduced — the concern is resolved-with-evidence or acted-on, never silently bypassed (the "findings never out-voted" discipline applied to the readiness verdict).
   *Falsified if*: a clarification record changes any mechanical signal's verdict in either direction (fail-stays-fail AND pass-stays-pass are both pinned); or Phase-0 re-review accepts a reason-keyed but span-ungrounded / unsupported clarification, or flips READY on an entry that creates new normative behavior; or a second clarification round is authored after any first-round NOT-READY re-return (same OR new reason); or the attempt record — original report and clarification entries — does not survive worktree teardown / a fresh `bd show`; or a second write surface for the terminal disposition is added (derive-don't-write is the contract); or `bead clarify` is absent from the AC-9 ceremony baseline.

9. **ADR-0041 amendment.** ADR-0041 §1 MUST be amended with the fourth-verb clause named in ADR Touchpoints, carrying the distinctive anchor phrase **"preflight-leg-only addition"** and naming `mindspec next`: `next` adopts the gate-before-mutate **preflight leg** (readiness refusal before any mutation; byte-identical-on-refusal; the distinct `--allow-not-ready` override). The amendment is a SCOPE-DEFERRAL, not a governance certification: it adds only the preflight leg and makes no claim about `next`'s existing success-path claim/branch/worktree mutation chain, which retains whatever commit/forward-reconcile contract it already carries (this spec neither grants nor removes it); the "three verbs" wording is reconciled to name `next` as a preflight-leg fourth member. The amendment is pre-drafted at plan time and lands in the same bead as the `next`-gate code, so the ADR-divergence gate sees the declared touchpoint.
   *Falsified if*: the code landing the `next` readiness gate ships without an ADR-0041 amendment carrying the "preflight-leg-only addition" fourth-verb clause naming `next`, or the amendment certifies `next`'s success path as commit/reconcile-exempt, or the code cites a clause the amendment does not contain — operationally pinned by AC-16.

design:
## Requirements

1. **Reject non-resolving Impacted-Domains labels EARLY and FORWARD-ONLY, with a fix hint that works (#178; #147's early-surfacing ask).** The trigger: a workspace where the ownership model is IN USE — defined mechanically as the layout-aware domain enumeration (`resolveDomains`) returning ≥1 domain dir whose OWNERSHIP.yaml loads — carrying an `## Impacted Domains` entry that is a bare token naming no domain dir (`normalizeImpactedDomains` Rule 2, `ownership_resolve.go:119-125`). **Forward-only gating (the corpus-collision resolution), by EXPLICIT pre-approval status.** This condition MUST become a hard `impacted-domains-resolve` ERROR ONLY when the spec's own frontmatter status — read via `validate.SpecStatus`/`SpecStatusAt` (`internal/validate/frontmatter.go:21`/`:33`), the parse-the-contract spec-status signal, NOT `plan.go`'s `isApproved` which reads the PLAN's status — is an EXPLICIT case-folded pre-approval authoring status (`Draft`). The polarity is defined precisely against the real corpus: a spec whose `spec.md` has NO YAML frontmatter, or frontmatter with NO `status:` key (both of which `SpecStatus` returns as the empty string), is treated as **legacy-grandfathered — NOT hard-failed**; `Approved` (and any other non-`Draft` explicit status) is likewise grandfathered. Only an explicit `Draft` triggers the reject. This is a deliberate bypass-tradeoff, stated: a status-less legacy spec can carry a non-resolving label without being caught here — accepted so that the ~22 pre-frontmatter legacy specs (the 007–037-era specs with no frontmatter, plus 038/039/041 with no `status:` key) are NEVER retroactively broken; the forward-only gate exists to catch NEW authoring, and new specs are scaffolded `status: Draft`. The gate runs at the authoring consumers: `validate spec`/`spec approve` (via `checkImpactedDomainsResolutionParity`, `spec.go:217` — its "Rule 2 still passes" carve-out comment is retired) and `validate plan` (`plan.go:143`). This is STRICTLY cleaner than the fallback (demote-pre-existing-to-WARN + hard-fail-new): a grandfathered spec emits nothing new at all, so no WARN noise on the legacy corpus. Because the status signal lives at the authoring gates, the SHARED helper distinguishes the Rule-2-non-resolving finding and the CALLER applies it as an error only in forward mode; the exact plumbing (a mode flag into the helper, or a caller-side severity gate on the distinguished finding) is plan-level, fixed observably by the ACs. The error text MUST contain, in one message: the offending entry verbatim (escaped per the existing `termsafe` discipline at this site), why it failed (neither a domain dir nor a path claimed by any OWNERSHIP `paths:`), the enumerated available domain-dir names, and both working remedies — replace the label with one of the listed domain names, or declare a claimed path instead (claiming it in `<layout-aware domains root>/<name>/OWNERSHIP.yaml` if not yet claimed). **Carve-outs**: (i) any spec whose `SpecStatus` is not the explicit case-folded `Draft` — i.e. `Approved`, any other explicit non-`Draft` status, empty-because-no-frontmatter, or empty-because-no-`status:`-key — is grandfathered; (ii) a manifest-less workspace (zero loadable OWNERSHIP.yaml) — Rule 2 keeps verbatim exactly as today, no new failure for repos that never adopted the ownership model. **Falsified if**: the #178 repro (domain dir `orders` owning `src/orders/**`; a `status: Draft` spec declaring `api (orders — models)`) still passes `mindspec validate spec` or `validate plan` clean; if ANY corpus spec that is `Approved`, non-`Draft`, frontmatter-less, or `status:`-key-less NEWLY fails `validate spec` after this change (the ~22 status-less legacy specs like `007-beads-tooling`, green today, must stay green); if the error message omits the entry, the available-domain list, or either remedy; or if a manifest-less workspace with bare-name domains newly errors.
2. **Resolve the ADR side of every coverage comparison through the same owner resolution (`mindspec-6ou2`; the red tail of #147).** Before any spec-domains-vs-ADR-domains decision, the cited ADR's parsed `Domain(s)` entries MUST pass through the same DETERMINISTIC explicit-manifest resolution the spec side already gets: an entry that names a domain dir stays verbatim; a path-shaped entry that is claimed by exactly one domain's OWNERSHIP `paths:` resolves to that owner's dir-name; a non-resolving, ambiguous, or non-path (tuple/prose) entry stays verbatim and compares literally (it can only fail to intersect, exactly as today — ADR-side resolution introduces NO new error class, because ADR `Domain(s)` lines are historical documents this spec must not force churn on; this repo's own ADR-0032 line `validation, adr, lifecycle, workflow` keeps working via its literal `workflow`, and its non-domain tokens stay literal and simply do not match). **Directory-shape completeness (point-to-glob):** the path resolution MUST claim a directory-shaped ADR label in BOTH forms — with a trailing slash (`api/app/lola/`, `src/orders/`) and without one (`api/app/lola`, `src/orders`) — against an OWNERSHIP glob like `src/orders/**`, so an ADR that writes either form resolves identically; a bare file path (`src/orders/api.py`) resolves the same way. The resolved sets feed ALL comparison sites: `intersectFold` in `checkADRCitations` (`plan.go:485` → `adr-cite-irrelevant`), the membership test inside `coverageOf`/`IsDomainCovered` (`plan.go:641`/`:628` → `adr-coverage-missing`/`adr-coverage-proposed`), and the bead-time coverage probe (`divergence.go:230`). Resolution MUST read through the same per-run ownership cache/ref plumbing as the spec side (`newOwnershipCache`, `ownerRef`-anchored at bead time) so both sides see the same tree; per-run memoization beside the existing `newMemoStore` is a plan-level performance choice (no observable contract, so not a MUST here). **Falsified if**: the 6ou2 repro (below, both slash forms) still emits `adr-cite-irrelevant` or `adr-coverage-missing` at `validate plan`; if the same shape still fails the bead-time coverage probe at `complete`; if either directory slash form fails to resolve where the other succeeds; or if an ADR whose `Domain(s)` line holds only legacy prose/tuple labels newly produces any error today's build does not.
3. **The `adr-coverage-missing` hint must name the governing fix, including uncited ADRs (#145 friction 1, completed).** WHENEVER `checkADRCoverage` finds domain `d` notCovered — regardless of whether the plan cites zero ADRs OR cites some ADRs none of which covers `d` — and the ADR store (the same worktree-overlay store already in hand, `plan.go:157`) contains one or more UNCITED Accepted ADRs whose resolved `Domain(s)` (per Requirement 2) cover `d`, the error MUST name those ADR IDs and the actual remedy — add them to the plan's `adr_citations` frontmatter — as the FIRST hint, ahead of the existing spec-100 remedies (amend a cited Accepted ADR's `Domain(s)` line; `mindspec adr create --domain <d>` last, only as the create-new fallback). The trigger is the EXISTENCE of an uncited covering ADR in the store, NOT the emptiness of the citation list — a plan that already cites some non-covering ADRs still gets the name-the-covering-ADR hint. The hint set MUST stay truthful in the degenerate case: when the store holds no covering ADR at all, the existing `:548`/`:550` behavior stands unchanged. **Falsified if**: the #145 repro (store contains Accepted ADR-0001 whose `Domain(s)` cover `d`; plan cites nothing) still emits a hint whose only action is `mindspec adr create --domain <d>`; if a plan that cites ≥1 non-covering ADR while an uncited covering ADR exists gets NO name-the-covering-ADR hint; or if the hint names an ADR that is already cited, non-Accepted, or non-covering.
4. **Every gate hint names a path and an owner that are TRUE in the operator's workspace (#197; #178's unowned-message vagueness).** (a) The three hard-coded pre-flatten hint paths — `divergence.go:221` ("create a new domain dir at `.mindspec/docs/domains/<name>/OWNERSHIP.yaml`") and the two `internal-docs` templates (`docsync.go:517`, `:585`) — MUST render through one shared layout-aware helper that prints the domains root the loaders actually resolve in that workspace (flat `.mindspec/domains` when flattened; canonical `.mindspec/docs/domains` pre-flatten; matching `workspace.DomainsDir`'s precedence, `workspace.go:617`), and a sweep guard MUST pin that no operator-facing gate message string hard-codes a domains root again. (b) The `adr-divergence-unowned` finding MUST split into two truthful findings: when the changed file IS claimed by some domain's OWNERSHIP but that domain is not in the spec's declared (resolved) Impacted Domains, the message names the real owning domain and the remedy "add `<domain>` to `## Impacted Domains`" — the scope-drift signal #178's option 2 identified as the gate's actual intent; only a file claimed by NO domain's manifest keeps the "genuinely unowned" message with the (now layout-aware) claim-it remedy. The real-owner attribution reads the same full-enumeration path doc-sync already uses (`resolveDomains` + `attributeDomainCached`, the `docsync.go` pattern) — no new discovery mechanism. The gate's PASS/FAIL boundary is unchanged: both findings remain errors under the same `--override-adr`/`--supersede-adr` escapes; only the message truth changes. **Falsified if**: in a flattened workspace any doc-sync or adr-divergence failure output contains `.mindspec/docs/domains/`; if in a pre-flatten workspace the hint stops naming the canonical path that actually resolves there; if a file owned by an undeclared domain is still reported with the unqualified "not claimed by any OWNERSHIP.yaml" text instead of naming its owner; or if the sweep guard fails to go red when a literal domains-root string is reintroduced into a gate message.
5. **Close #147 and #145 on evidence: cite the EXISTING regression pins; add only the genuinely-missing #147 end-to-end fixture.** Most of the shipped-fix pins these issues need ALREADY EXIST as named tests — the requirement is to CITE them as the issue→test evidence map at close, not re-author them: the #147 spec-100 resolution core is pinned by `TestValidateDivergenceFilePathImpactedDomainResolves` (`internal/validate/divergence_test.go`); #145 friction 2 (worktree ADR visibility) by `TestPlanSpecWorktreeADRVisible` (`internal/validate/plan_test.go`) and the user-facing `TestAdrShowWorktree_FindsWorktreeLocalADR` / `TestAdrListWorktree_ListsWorktreeLocalADR` / `TestAdrShowWorktree_StillFindsMainOnlyADR` (`cmd/mindspec/adr_test.go`), plus worktree-local `adr create` by `TestADRCreate_WritesIntoInvokingWorktree` (`cmd/mindspec/adr_test.go:92`); #145 friction 3 (both `Domain(s)` header forms) by `TestParseADR_NonListDomainLine` (`internal/adr/parse_test.go`). The GENUINELY-NEW pin this spec must ADD is the #147 END-TO-END fixture — really the red/green AC for Requirement 2 — through the `complete`-shaped divergence path with the FULL #147 shape (impacted domains as file paths; a cited Accepted ADR whose `Domain(s)` are those same file-path strings): green only through Requirement 2, RED today at the coverage step (the resolution half alone is already green via the existing test above). Additionally pin the #145-bonus scaffold comment — `internal/approve/spec.go:255` emits the commented `adr_citations` key in the plan scaffold — beside its sibling scaffold-content assertions, so the documented-key remedy cannot silently drop. And add the 6ou2-item-1 regression pin: a `internal/contextpack/spec_test.go` fixture asserting a backtick-/bold-wrapped `## Impacted Domains` entry is stripped to its bare token before normalization (`spec.go:79-81`) — none exists today, so it is new. **Falsified if**: the issue→test evidence map names a test that does not exist or does not pin the claimed behavior; if the new #147 end-to-end fixture passes on today's `main` (it must be red at the coverage step until Requirement 2 lands); or if reverting the `Contains`-based header match at `parse.go:74`, the overlay store at `plan.go:236`, or the spec-100 normalization call at `divergence.go:155` leaves its cited pin green.
6. **ADR-0032 third amendment section, landing with the code.** ADR-0032 MUST gain a NEW `## Amendment` section (its third, after tri-state coverage and spec-100 normalization) carrying Requirement 1's forward-only authoring-time-resolvability rule (including both carve-outs: already-Approved grandfathering and manifest-less workspaces) and Requirement 2's symmetric-comparison rule (including the ADR-side no-new-error doctrine, the directory-shape completeness, and the pinned rejection of path-overlap intersection with its new-ADR trigger), AND the evidenced-supersession paragraph explicitly superseding bead `mindspec-6ou2`'s 6/6 panel decision (2026-06-26) with its three-objection refutation — all in the same bead as the first code that implements them, so the ADR-divergence gate sees the declared touchpoint. **Falsified if**: the amendment text lacks either rule, lacks either carve-out, lacks the new-ADR trigger sentence, lacks the 6ou2 evidenced-supersession paragraph, or lands in a different bead than the implementing code.
7. **Net ceremony goes DOWN — nothing new to operate.** This spec adds NO new gate lane, NO new CLI flag, NO new config key, and NO new override mechanism; every change either rejects earlier (Requirement 1, with the message carrying the complete remedy), passes a previously-false-failing correct input (Requirements 2, 3), or corrects hint text (Requirement 4). The existing escapes (`--override-adr`, `--supersede-adr`; `complete.go:229-252`, `impl.go:119-135`) are untouched. This repo's own lifecycle corpus stays green: no spec that passes `validate spec`/`validate plan` today turns red after this spec (the forward-only, explicit-`Draft`-only gate grandfathers every `Approved`, non-`Draft`, and status-less legacy spec; the only new error lands on the already-red `Draft` scaffold 067, crossing no green→red boundary — see AC-14). **Falsified if**: `mindspec complete --help`, `impl approve --help`, or `mindspec config` output gains any new flag/key; if any spec in this repo's corpus that validates green before this change validates red after it; or if a new blocking check fires on an input class not named in Requirements 1–4.

## Requirements

1. **Reject non-resolving Impacted-Domains labels EARLY and FORWARD-ONLY, with a fix hint that works (#178; #147's early-surfacing ask).** The trigger: a workspace where the ownership model is IN USE — defined mechanically as the layout-aware domain enumeration (`resolveDomains`) returning ≥1 domain dir whose OWNERSHIP.yaml loads — carrying an `## Impacted Domains` entry that is a bare token naming no domain dir (`normalizeImpactedDomains` Rule 2, `ownership_resolve.go:119-125`). **Forward-only gating (the corpus-collision resolution), by EXPLICIT pre-approval status.** This condition MUST become a hard `impacted-domains-resolve` ERROR ONLY when the spec's own frontmatter status — read via `validate.SpecStatus`/`SpecStatusAt` (`internal/validate/frontmatter.go:21`/`:33`), the parse-the-contract spec-status signal, NOT `plan.go`'s `isApproved` which reads the PLAN's status — is an EXPLICIT case-folded pre-approval authoring status (`Draft`). The polarity is defined precisely against the real corpus: a spec whose `spec.md` has NO YAML frontmatter, or frontmatter with NO `status:` key (both of which `SpecStatus` returns as the empty string), is treated as **legacy-grandfathered — NOT hard-failed**; `Approved` (and any other non-`Draft` explicit status) is likewise grandfathered. Only an explicit `Draft` triggers the reject. This is a deliberate bypass-tradeoff, stated: a status-less legacy spec can carry a non-resolving label without being caught here — accepted so that the ~22 pre-frontmatter legacy specs (the 007–037-era specs with no frontmatter, plus 038/039/041 with no `status:` key) are NEVER retroactively broken; the forward-only gate exists to catch NEW authoring, and new specs are scaffolded `status: Draft`. The gate runs at the authoring consumers: `validate spec`/`spec approve` (via `checkImpactedDomainsResolutionParity`, `spec.go:217` — its "Rule 2 still passes" carve-out comment is retired) and `validate plan` (`plan.go:143`). This is STRICTLY cleaner than the fallback (demote-pre-existing-to-WARN + hard-fail-new): a grandfathered spec emits nothing new at all, so no WARN noise on the legacy corpus. Because the status signal lives at the authoring gates, the SHARED helper distinguishes the Rule-2-non-resolving finding and the CALLER applies it as an error only in forward mode; the exact plumbing (a mode flag into the helper, or a caller-side severity gate on the distinguished finding) is plan-level, fixed observably by the ACs. The error text MUST contain, in one message: the offending entry verbatim (escaped per the existing `termsafe` discipline at this site), why it failed (neither a domain dir nor a path claimed by any OWNERSHIP `paths:`), the enumerated available domain-dir names, and both working remedies — replace the label with one of the listed domain names, or declare a claimed path instead (claiming it in `<layout-aware domains root>/<name>/OWNERSHIP.yaml` if not yet claimed). **Carve-outs**: (i) any spec whose `SpecStatus` is not the explicit case-folded `Draft` — i.e. `Approved`, any other explicit non-`Draft` status, empty-because-no-frontmatter, or empty-because-no-`status:`-key — is grandfathered; (ii) a manifest-less workspace (zero loadable OWNERSHIP.yaml) — Rule 2 keeps verbatim exactly as today, no new failure for repos that never adopted the ownership model. **Falsified if**: the #178 repro (domain dir `orders` owning `src/orders/**`; a `status: Draft` spec declaring `api (orders — models)`) still passes `mindspec validate spec` or `validate plan` clean; if ANY corpus spec that is `Approved`, non-`Draft`, frontmatter-less, or `status:`-key-less NEWLY fails `validate spec` after this change (the ~22 status-less legacy specs like `007-beads-tooling`, green today, must stay green); if the error message omits the entry, the available-domain list, or either remedy; or if a manifest-less workspace with bare-name domains newly errors.
2. **Resolve the ADR side of every coverage comparison through the same owner resolution (`mindspec-6ou2`; the red tail of #147).** Before any spec-domains-vs-ADR-domains decision, the cited ADR's parsed `Domain(s)` entries MUST pass through the same DETERMINISTIC explicit-manifest resolution the spec side already gets: an entry that names a domain dir stays verbatim; a path-shaped entry that is claimed by exactly one domain's OWNERSHIP `paths:` resolves to that owner's dir-name; a non-resolving, ambiguous, or non-path (tuple/prose) entry stays verbatim and compares literally (it can only fail to intersect, exactly as today — ADR-side resolution introduces NO new error class, because ADR `Domain(s)` lines are historical documents this spec must not force churn on; this repo's own ADR-0032 line `validation, adr, lifecycle, workflow` keeps working via its literal `workflow`, and its non-domain tokens stay literal and simply do not match). **Directory-shape completeness (point-to-glob):** the path resolution MUST claim a directory-shaped ADR label in BOTH forms — with a trailing slash (`api/app/lola/`, `src/orders/`) and without one (`api/app/lola`, `src/orders`) — against an OWNERSHIP glob like `src/orders/**`, so an ADR that writes either form resolves identically; a bare file path (`src/orders/api.py`) resolves the same way. The resolved sets feed ALL comparison sites: `intersectFold` in `checkADRCitations` (`plan.go:485` → `adr-cite-irrelevant`), the membership test inside `coverageOf`/`IsDomainCovered` (`plan.go:641`/`:628` → `adr-coverage-missing`/`adr-coverage-proposed`), and the bead-time coverage probe (`divergence.go:230`). Resolution MUST read through the same per-run ownership cache/ref plumbing as the spec side (`newOwnershipCache`, `ownerRef`-anchored at bead time) so both sides see the same tree; per-run memoization beside the existing `newMemoStore` is a plan-level performance choice (no observable contract, so not a MUST here). **Falsified if**: the 6ou2 repro (below, both slash forms) still emits `adr-cite-irrelevant` or `adr-coverage-missing` at `validate plan`; if the same shape still fails the bead-time coverage probe at `complete`; if either directory slash form fails to resolve where the other succeeds; or if an ADR whose `Domain(s)` line holds only legacy prose/tuple labels newly produces any error today's build does not.
3. **The `adr-coverage-missing` hint must name the governing fix, including uncited ADRs (#145 friction 1, completed).** WHENEVER `checkADRCoverage` finds domain `d` notCovered — regardless of whether the plan cites zero ADRs OR cites some ADRs none of which covers `d` — and the ADR store (the same worktree-overlay store already in hand, `plan.go:157`) contains one or more UNCITED Accepted ADRs whose resolved `Domain(s)` (per Requirement 2) cover `d`, the error MUST name those ADR IDs and the actual remedy — add them to the plan's `adr_citations` frontmatter — as the FIRST hint, ahead of the existing spec-100 remedies (amend a cited Accepted ADR's `Domain(s)` line; `mindspec adr create --domain <d>` last, only as the create-new fallback). The trigger is the EXISTENCE of an uncited covering ADR in the store, NOT the emptiness of the citation list — a plan that already cites some non-covering ADRs still gets the name-the-covering-ADR hint. The hint set MUST stay truthful in the degenerate case: when the store holds no covering ADR at all, the existing `:548`/`:550` behavior stands unchanged. **Falsified if**: the #145 repro (store contains Accepted ADR-0001 whose `Domain(s)` cover `d`; plan cites nothing) still emits a hint whose only action is `mindspec adr create --domain <d>`; if a plan that cites ≥1 non-covering ADR while an uncited covering ADR exists gets NO name-the-covering-ADR hint; or if the hint names an ADR that is already cited, non-Accepted, or non-covering.
4. **Every gate hint names a path and an owner that are TRUE in the operator's workspace (#197; #178's unowned-message vagueness).** (a) The three hard-coded pre-flatten hint paths — `divergence.go:221` ("create a new domain dir at `.mindspec/docs/domains/<name>/OWNERSHIP.yaml`") and the two `internal-docs` templates (`docsync.go:517`, `:585`) — MUST render through one shared layout-aware helper that prints the domains root the loaders actually resolve in that workspace (flat `.mindspec/domains` when flattened; canonical `.mindspec/docs/domains` pre-flatten; matching `workspace.DomainsDir`'s precedence, `workspace.go:617`), and a sweep guard MUST pin that no operator-facing gate message string hard-codes a domains root again. (b) The `adr-divergence-unowned` finding MUST split into two truthful findings: when the changed file IS claimed by some domain's OWNERSHIP but that domain is not in the spec's declared (resolved) Impacted Domains, the message names the real owning domain and the remedy "add `<domain>` to `## Impacted Domains`" — the scope-drift signal #178's option 2 identified as the gate's actual intent; only a file claimed by NO domain's manifest keeps the "genuinely unowned" message with the (now layout-aware) claim-it remedy. The real-owner attribution reads the same full-enumeration path doc-sync already uses (`resolveDomains` + `attributeDomainCached`, the `docsync.go` pattern) — no new discovery mechanism. The gate's PASS/FAIL boundary is unchanged: both findings remain errors under the same `--override-adr`/`--supersede-adr` escapes; only the message truth changes. **Falsified if**: in a flattened workspace any doc-sync or adr-divergence failure output contains `.mindspec/docs/domains/`; if in a pre-flatten workspace the hint stops naming the canonical path that actually resolves there; if a file owned by an undeclared domain is still reported with the unqualified "not claimed by any OWNERSHIP.yaml" text instead of naming its owner; or if the sweep guard fails to go red when a literal domains-root string is reintroduced into a gate message.
5. **Close #147 and #145 on evidence: cite the EXISTING regression pins; add only the genuinely-missing #147 end-to-end fixture.** Most of the shipped-fix pins these issues need ALREADY EXIST as named tests — the requirement is to CITE them as the issue→test evidence map at close, not re-author them: the #147 spec-100 resolution core is pinned by `TestValidateDivergenceFilePathImpactedDomainResolves` (`internal/validate/divergence_test.go`); #145 friction 2 (worktree ADR visibility) by `TestPlanSpecWorktreeADRVisible` (`internal/validate/plan_test.go`) and the user-facing `TestAdrShowWorktree_FindsWorktreeLocalADR` / `TestAdrListWorktree_ListsWorktreeLocalADR` / `TestAdrShowWorktree_StillFindsMainOnlyADR` (`cmd/mindspec/adr_test.go`), plus worktree-local `adr create` by `TestADRCreate_WritesIntoInvokingWorktree` (`cmd/mindspec/adr_test.go:92`); #145 friction 3 (both `Domain(s)` header forms) by `TestParseADR_NonListDomainLine` (`internal/adr/parse_test.go`). The GENUINELY-NEW pin this spec must ADD is the #147 END-TO-END fixture — really the red/green AC for Requirement 2 — through the `complete`-shaped divergence path with the FULL #147 shape (impacted domains as file paths; a cited Accepted ADR whose `Domain(s)` are those same file-path strings): green only through Requirement 2, RED today at the coverage step (the resolution half alone is already green via the existing test above). Additionally pin the #145-bonus scaffold comment — `internal/approve/spec.go:255` emits the commented `adr_citations` key in the plan scaffold — beside its sibling scaffold-content assertions, so the documented-key remedy cannot silently drop. And add the 6ou2-item-1 regression pin: a `internal/contextpack/spec_test.go` fixture asserting a backtick-/bold-wrapped `## Impacted Domains` entry is stripped to its bare token before normalization (`spec.go:79-81`) — none exists today, so it is new. **Falsified if**: the issue→test evidence map names a test that does not exist or does not pin the claimed behavior; if the new #147 end-to-end fixture passes on today's `main` (it must be red at the coverage step until Requirement 2 lands); or if reverting the `Contains`-based header match at `parse.go:74`, the overlay store at `plan.go:236`, or the spec-100 normalization call at `divergence.go:155` leaves its cited pin green.
6. **ADR-0032 third amendment section, landing with the code.** ADR-0032 MUST gain a NEW `## Amendment` section (its third, after tri-state coverage and spec-100 normalization) carrying Requirement 1's forward-only authoring-time-resolvability rule (including both carve-outs: already-Approved grandfathering and manifest-less workspaces) and Requirement 2's symmetric-comparison rule (including the ADR-side no-new-error doctrine, the directory-shape completeness, and the pinned rejection of path-overlap intersection with its new-ADR trigger), AND the evidenced-supersession paragraph explicitly superseding bead `mindspec-6ou2`'s 6/6 panel decision (2026-06-26) with its three-objection refutation — all in the same bead as the first code that implements them, so the ADR-divergence gate sees the declared touchpoint. **Falsified if**: the amendment text lacks either rule, lacks either carve-out, lacks the new-ADR trigger sentence, lacks the 6ou2 evidenced-supersession paragraph, or lands in a different bead than the implementing code.
7. **Net ceremony goes DOWN — nothing new to operate.** This spec adds NO new gate lane, NO new CLI flag, NO new config key, and NO new override mechanism; every change either rejects earlier (Requirement 1, with the message carrying the complete remedy), passes a previously-false-failing correct input (Requirements 2, 3), or corrects hint text (Requirement 4). The existing escapes (`--override-adr`, `--supersede-adr`; `complete.go:229-252`, `impl.go:119-135`) are untouched. This repo's own lifecycle corpus stays green: no spec that passes `validate spec`/`validate plan` today turns red after this spec (the forward-only, explicit-`Draft`-only gate grandfathers every `Approved`, non-`Draft`, and status-less legacy spec; the only new error lands on the already-red `Draft` scaffold 067, crossing no green→red boundary — see AC-14). **Falsified if**: `mindspec complete --help`, `impl approve --help`, or `mindspec config` output gains any new flag/key; if any spec in this repo's corpus that validates green before this change validates red after it; or if a new blocking check fires on an input class not named in Requirements 1–4.

## ADR Decisions

Cited by ID — full text under `.mindspec/adr/`:

- see ADR-0032 — Semantic ADR Coverage Gates with Override and Supersede Flags
- see ADR-0041 — Gate-Before-Mutate — Preflight, Commit, Forward-Reconcile
- see ADR-0036 — Ownership Discovery — Zero Framework Cognition for OWNERSHIP.yaml and source_globs
- see ADR-0039 — Flat `.mindspec/` Layout v2 — Per-Artifact Three-Tier Resolver, Permanent Multi-Prefix Matchers, and Co-Located Reviews
- see ADR-0035 — Agent Error Contract — Recovery Lines and Exit Codes

title: [122-domain-adr-gate-truthfulness] Bead 2: ADR-side symmetric name-resolution + the 6ou2 and #147 end-to-end repros
description:
R2 in full plus R5a (the one genuinely-new #147 pin). Resolves the
cited ADR's `Domain(s)` entries through the same deterministic
explicit-manifest owner resolution the spec side already gets, so both
sides of every coverage comparison meet as domain names — closing
6ou2 items 3/4 and the still-red coverage tail of #147, with NO new
ADR-side error class.

**Steps**
1. Add `internal/validate/adr_domain_resolve.go`: the deterministic
   entry resolver (Rule-1 keep domain-dir names verbatim; path-shaped
   entries owner-resolved through the shared `newOwnershipCache` +
   `matchesAny` mechanics honoring `exclude:`; directory-shape
   completeness via trailing-slash trim + the `<label>/x` synthetic
   child probe per the plan choice above; zero/ambiguous/non-path
   tuple-or-prose entries kept VERBATIM with no error) and the
   decorating store `newDomainResolvingStore(inner adr.Store, exec
   executor.Executor, root, ownerRef string) adr.Store` whose
   `Get`/`List` return ADRs with `Domains` mapped through it, memoized
   per ADR ID per run. Doc comment cites ADR-0032's third amendment
   §(b) (landed by Bead 1 — the merge-order edge) and states the
   no-new-error doctrine verbatim.
2. Wrap the two gate-lane store constructions:
   `plan.go:157` (`newMemoStore(adrStoreForSpecFn(root, specDir))` →
   additionally wrapped, `exec nil`/`ownerRef ""` — the working-tree
   read) and `divergence.go:137` (wrapped with the lane's `exec` +
   `ownerRef`, so ADR-side resolution reads the SAME ref-anchored tree
   as the spec side). This feeds every comparison site
   (`intersectFold` `:485` → `adr-cite-irrelevant`;
   `coverageOf`/`IsDomainCovered` `:641`/`:628` →
   `adr-coverage-missing`/`-proposed`; the bead-time probe `:230`)
   with zero signature churn. The cmd-side `adrReadStore` is NOT
   wrapped (`adr show`/`list` render the literal document). Note in a
   code comment that `adr-cite-irrelevant`'s message now renders the
   RESOLVED domain set (it only fires when the intersection is still
   empty).
3. AC-5 fixtures (6ou2's actual filed scenario, both slash forms):
   domain `orders` claiming `src/orders/**`; spec Impacted Domains
   `src/orders/api.py` (spec-side resolves via spec 100); plan citing
   Accepted ADR-0090 with `- **Domain(s)**: src/orders/` in one sibling
   fixture and `- **Domain(s)**: src/orders` in the other. Assert:
   today both emit `adr-cite-irrelevant` AND `adr-coverage-missing` at
   `validate plan` (RED-today probe); after, ZERO errors from both
   lanes for BOTH forms; same fixtures through the `complete`-shaped
   divergence probe with changed file `src/orders/api.py` pass with no
   `--override-adr`.
4. AC-6 both polarities: (i) cited Accepted ADR whose `Domain(s)` is
   only legacy prose (`validation, lifecycle`) vs impacted `orders` —
   the SAME error CODES fire as today (`adr-cite-irrelevant` /
   `adr-coverage-missing`), no new class; the assertion is scoped to
   error CODES + count (the `adr-cite-irrelevant` message body now
   renders the RESOLVED impacted-domain set, which for a prose-only ADR
   is byte-identical to today because prose tokens stay literal — so
   the test asserts codes/count and that no NEW code appears, not exact
   message bytes). (ii) an ADR-side path claimed by NO domain resolves
   to nothing, compares literally, produces no resolve-style error.
5. AC-7, the #147 END-TO-END fixture (the genuinely-new R5a pin):
   spec Impacted Domains `genevieve/review.py` +
   `genevieve/summarizer.py`; domain `genevieve` claiming
   `genevieve/**/*.py` + `.github/workflows/code-review.yaml`; cited
   Accepted ADR whose `Domain(s)` lists those same file-path strings;
   bead diff touching `genevieve/summarizer.py` +
   `.github/workflows/code-review.yaml`. The `complete`-shaped
   divergence lane returns ZERO errors (no unowned, no coverage
   failure, no override). RED today at the coverage step; the
   resolution half stays pinned standalone by the EXISTING
   `TestValidateDivergenceFilePathImpactedDomainResolves`
   (`internal/validate/divergence_test.go:546` — cited, not
   re-authored; red if the `divergence.go:155` normalization is
   reverted).

**Verification**
- [ ] `go test ./internal/validate/ -run 'TestADRDomainResolve|TestSixOUTwo|Test147EndToEnd'` passes (final names in review evidence); both AC-5 slash forms green through plan AND complete-shaped lanes
- [ ] AC-5 + AC-7 subtests RED on the spec-init SHA at the pinned steps (6ou2 items 3/4; the #147 coverage tail); AC-6 passes today and red only against an ADR-side error-gating implementation (deviation tag in-test)
- [ ] `TestValidateDivergenceFilePathImpactedDomainResolves` still green and cited in the AC-7 evidence as the standalone resolution-half pin
- [ ] `adr show`/`adr list` output unchanged for a path-`Domain(s)` ADR (cmd store un-wrapped — asserted)
- [ ] `go build ./... && go test ./...` no new red (z4ps caveat); `golangci-lint run ./...` clean; bead completes with zero `--override-adr`

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] AC-5 — 6ou2 end-to-end, both slash forms: zero `adr-cite-irrelevant`/`adr-coverage-missing` at plan time AND a passing complete-shaped coverage probe (RED today)
- [ ] AC-6 — ADR-side no-new-error, both polarities (legacy prose compares literally; unclaimed path resolves to nothing silently)
- [ ] AC-7 — the full #147 shape through the complete-shaped lane returns zero errors (coverage tail RED today); existing resolution pin cited

**Depends on**
Bead 1 (cites the ADR-0032 §(b) amendment text Bead 1 finalizes — a
merge-order pin; also sequences the `plan.go` seam). (bd edges wired
from `work_chunks[].depends_on`.)

design:
## Requirements

Each requirement carries a hard falsifier. "Greenfield fixture" below means: an empty directory, `git init`, then the named mindspec verbs — no manual file creation.

1. **`init` scaffolds a first-run-complete workspace, including the context map (#207).** The `bootstrap.Run` manifest MUST additionally scaffold `.mindspec/context-map.md` — a skeleton with a title and a `## Bounded Contexts` section followed by a `---` separator, so `appendContextMap`'s existing insertion scan (`scaffold.go:118-150`) inserts entries at the intended place, not the file's tail. The item follows the manifest's existing additive discipline: never overwrites an existing file. This restores `init`'s own stated contract (`cmd/mindspec/init.go:14-16`) that the workflow is immediately usable.
   *Falsified if*: a greenfield fixture running `mindspec init` then `mindspec domain add alpha` still errors, or produces a context map without an `### Alpha` entry under `## Bounded Contexts`, or `init` overwrites a pre-existing `context-map.md`.

2. **`domain add` converges from every partial state (#207).** (a) When `context-map.md` is absent, `appendContextMap` MUST create the Requirement-1 skeleton before appending — `domain add` succeeds even in a pre-123-initialized repo. (b) The already-exists refusal (`scaffold.go:40-42`) MUST become a convergence check: when the domain dir exists but its context-map entry is MISSING, `domain add <name>` backfills the entry (and any missing standard file: the four templates + `OWNERSHIP.yaml`, each written only if absent — existing files are never overwritten) and succeeds; only when the domain is fully scaffolded AND mapped does it refuse with "already exists". (c) The write order or failure handling MUST guarantee no terminal partial state: any failure after the dir is created leaves a state a bare re-run of the same command repairs.
   *Falsified if*: any sequence of `domain add <name>` invocations (including against the #207 legacy state: dir present, entry absent) reaches a state where the domain dir exists, its context-map entry is missing, and re-running `mindspec domain add <name>` does not produce the entry; or a re-run duplicates an existing entry; or a re-run overwrites operator-edited domain docs.

3. **`doctor` detects the missing/incomplete context map (#207).** Two new checks in the docs lane: (a) **missing-context-map** — `context-map.md` absent at the layout-resolved path → `Missing`, with a `--fix` that scaffolds the Requirement-1 skeleton (mechanical, ZFC-safe: structure only, no invented content); (b) **unmapped-domain** — a directory under `domains/` whose name has no corresponding entry heading in `context-map.md` → `Warn` naming each unmapped domain with the recovery line `mindspec domain add <name>` (the Requirement-2 backfill). Detection uses the same entry-shape `appendContextMap` writes (the `### <Title>` heading for the domain), so the check and the writer cannot disagree about what "mapped" means (single shared helper, not two parsers).
   *Falsified if*: `doctor` exits green on a repo with domain dirs and no `context-map.md`, or on a repo with a scaffolded-but-unmapped domain; or the two checks' notion of "has an entry" is a second independent parse that can drift from `appendContextMap`'s emission.

4. **Runtime state is gitignored by scaffolding, and doctor checks ignore-ness, not just tracked-ness (#208).** (a) `init` MUST ensure the two runtime entries (`.mindspec/session.json`, `.mindspec/focus`) are present in the root `.gitignore` even when the file already exists — an idempotent, entry-granular append (exact-line presence check, the `appendGitignoreEntry` discipline at `git.go:66-83`) that never reorders or rewrites existing content; the greenfield create-from-scratch path (`bootstrap.go:232`) is unchanged. (b) `setup claude`, `setup codex`, and `setup copilot` MUST each ensure the same entries (setup is the onboarding verb for repos that never ran the greenfield-only `init`). (c) `doctor` MUST add a proactive check per runtime file: not tracked AND `git check-ignore` misses → `Warn` ("runtime file not gitignored — one `git add .mindspec/` from being committed") with a `--fix` that appends the entry (reusing `appendGitignoreEntry`); ignored → `OK`; the existing tracked → `Error` + untrack `--fix` (`git.go:24-46`) is unchanged and takes precedence.
   *Falsified if*: after `mindspec init` (or any one `setup` verb) in a repo with a pre-existing `.gitignore`, `git check-ignore .mindspec/session.json` or `git check-ignore .mindspec/focus` fails to match; or running the verb twice yields a different `.gitignore` than running it once; or `doctor` reports all-OK on a repo where a runtime file is unignored-untracked.

5. **`adr create` emits slugged filenames; every surface reports and accepts the canonical `ADR-NNNN` ID (#206).** (a) `create` MUST derive a kebab slug from the title (lowercase; non-alphanumeric runs collapse to single hyphens; leading/trailing hyphens trimmed; length-capped — cap value plan-level) and write `ADR-NNNN-<slug>.md` (`create.go:139` today); a `--slug` flag overrides the derivation; both derived and supplied slugs MUST yield a filename stem that passes `idvalidate.ADRID` (`ids.go:33`), and a title that derives an empty slug falls back to the bare form rather than an invalid name. This slugging is applied at the `create` EMISSION site only — it is by design NOT a rename of mindspec's own (or any consumer's) existing bare ADR files (see Out of Scope). (b) `ParseADR` MUST derive `ADR.ID` as the canonical `ADR-<digits>` prefix of the stem (`parse.go:47` today), never the full slugged stem — `list`/`show` report `ADR-0001` for `ADR-0001-integrate-at-contracts.md`. (c) ID→file resolution MUST resolve a canonical `ADR-NNNN` to whichever file carries that number — bare or slugged — and MUST also accept the full slugged form: `show`'s glob fallback already tolerates slugs (`show.go:45-58`) and is preserved, but the exact-join resolvers that do NOT — `--supersedes` and any other `workspace.ADRFilePath` caller (`workspace.go:578-583`) — MUST gain the same bare-or-slugged resolution. When BOTH a bare and a slugged file share one number, resolution MUST error naming both paths with an ADR-0035 recovery line (rename or remove the redundant file so exactly one carries the number) — never the current silent short-circuit to the exact-`<id>.md` match. (d) Backward compatibility: existing bare files keep their IDs and behavior; number allocation (`maxADRNum`, `parse.go:260-300`) is already slug-aware and MUST remain covered against mixed directories.
   *Falsified if*: `adr create "<multi-word title>"` still writes a bare `ADR-NNNN.md`; or `adr show`/`adr list` reports a slugged file's ID as anything other than `ADR-NNNN`; or `adr create --supersedes ADR-NNNN` cannot resolve a slugged predecessor through the exact-join path; or a bare/slugged number collision resolves silently instead of erroring with the recovery line.

6. **`models:` reaches guidance parity with `source_globs:` — schema doc, populate prompt, doctor nudge, honest enforcement status (#210).** (a) A literal commented schema block for `models:` (mirroring `sourceGlobsBlock`, `internal/doctor/config.go:18-29`) documenting: the free-form phase→model-id map shape (`config.go:63`), the canonical advisory phase keys (`authoring`, `implementation`, `review` — documented vocabulary, not an enforced enum), and — verbatim honesty — its enforcement status: today the key is declared-and-inert (`cmd/mindspec/config.go:22` `inertAnnotation`), nothing in the binary changes behavior based on it, and the authoritative consumers of the model protocol remain the orchestration skills; the block says exactly that and names wiring enforcement as a follow-up. (b) `mindspec models populate` — a ZFC prompt emitter mirroring `mindspec source populate` (`cmd/mindspec/source.go:23-45`): prints an agent prompt to declare the per-phase protocol in `.mindspec/config.yaml`; writes nothing. (c) A `missing-models` doctor `Warn` when `len(cfg.Models) == 0` (mirroring `checkSourceGlobs`, `config.go:63-96`), disclosing the inert status, hinting `mindspec models populate`, with a `--fix` that scaffolds the schema block three-state byte-preservingly (file absent / key absent / key present — the `scaffoldSourceGlobs` contract, `config.go:98-145`). (d) `mindspec config` output for `models:` keeps the inert annotation until an enforcement spec removes it.
   *Falsified if*: an empty-`models:` repo produces no doctor nudge; or `mindspec models populate` is absent or writes files; or the scaffolded block omits schema or overstates enforcement (claims any binary behavior reads the key); or the `--fix` scaffold rewrites operator-authored config bytes.

7. **Managed/scaffolded content carries the CONSUMER's identity, never the framework's (#211).** (a) All content mindspec writes into a consuming repo's agent docs — `init`'s `starterAgentsMD` (`bootstrap.go:275-351`) and `appendAgentsBlock` (`:353-`), `setup codex`'s `agentsMDManagedBlock` (`codex.go:53-104`), and every other managed block — MUST contain NO mindspec-repo-specific facts: no `make build` / `make test` (`bootstrap.go:287-288`, `:364-365`, `codex.go:62-63`), no "# AGENTS.md — MindSpec Project" title (`bootstrap.go:275`); identity framing is "This project uses MindSpec" (already the body phrasing), with a neutral `# AGENTS.md` title. (b) A new declared L2 config surface for the consumer's build/test guidance (exact key shape plan-level; rendered by `mindspec config`): when POPULATED, `init`/`setup` render its commands as the managed block's Build & Test section, and re-running `setup` (whose wholesale block replacement, `claude.go:573-582`, is retained) re-renders from config — the operator's declaration survives every refresh; when UNSET, the Build & Test section is OMITTED entirely (never a placeholder that reads as runnable). (c) The unset state gets the ADR-0036 stack: a doctor `Warn` nudging the declaration with a ZFC populate-prompt path (analogous to Requirement 6's; command naming plan-level), so a consumer learns the declared home exists. (d) `mindspec setup --check` and re-runs stay idempotent under both states.
   *Falsified if*: a greenfield `init` or `setup codex` in a repo with no Makefile produces an `AGENTS.md` whose managed content tells an agent to run `make build`/`make test` or titles the repo a "MindSpec Project"; or a populated build declaration is lost by a subsequent `setup` refresh; or the unset state renders framework or placeholder build commands; or doctor gives no cue that the declaration exists and is empty.

8. **`panel create` can scaffold the ad-hoc panel the shipped skill documents (#209).** (a) `mindspec panel create <slug> --gate adhoc --target <ref>` MUST succeed WITHOUT `--spec`, writing the panel dir + `panel.json` to `<repo>/.mindspec/reviews/<slug>/` — exactly the location `ms-panel-run` documents (`plugins/mindspec/skills/ms-panel-run/SKILL.md:43-52`) — via a new ad-hoc branch in `panelDirFor` (`panel.go:352-366`); the existing slug/target/round validation and `panel.json` stamping (expected reviewers, threshold, gate `adhoc`) apply unchanged. (b) `--spec` remains REQUIRED for every non-adhoc gate (`panel.go:113-115` retained); supplying `--spec` WITH `--gate adhoc` is refused with a recovery line naming both valid forms (an ad-hoc panel has no owning spec by definition — a silent ignore would misfile the panel). (c) `panel tally` (and `panel show`-class readers) MUST operate on the ad-hoc dir, restoring the deterministic tally for design/proposal reviews. (d) Ad-hoc panels stay OUTSIDE the lifecycle gate: `mindspec complete`'s panel scanning never consults `.mindspec/reviews/` (the skill's stated contract), and the `ms-panel-run` SKILL.md ad-hoc note is updated in the same change to state the now-real `panel create --gate adhoc` invocation instead of a path the binary can't produce.
   *Falsified if*: the #209 repro (`mindspec panel create adr-review --gate adhoc --target "commit <sha>"`, no `--spec`) still errors; or the panel lands anywhere other than `.mindspec/reviews/<slug>/`; or `panel tally` cannot read it; or an ad-hoc `panel.json` influences any `mindspec complete` gate decision; or the shipped skill still documents an invocation the binary rejects.

9. **ADR-0040 amendment.** ADR-0040 MUST be amended with the consumer-identity clause named in ADR Touchpoints (managed/scaffolded consumer content is framework-generic or L2-sourced, never framework-repo-specific; declared-inert keys are surfaced honestly with their guidance stack naming today's authoritative consumer), landing in the same bead as the first code that cites it, so the ADR-divergence gate sees the declared touchpoint.
   *Falsified if*: the code touching managed-content generation or the `models:` block lands without an ADR-0040 amendment carrying the consumer-identity clause, or cites a clause the amendment does not contain (the ADR-divergence gate goes green with no declared touchpoint) — operationally pinned by AC-18.

10. **Regression pinning.** Every failure class fixed here MUST be pinned by an automated test that reproduces the original issue's repro and goes RED if the fix is reverted (per-AC mapping below). The Requirement-3 "mapped" predicate MUST be one shared helper consumed by both `appendContextMap`'s emission side and doctor's detection side, pinned by a test that fails if either side is rewired to a private reimplementation (the established anti-drift pattern).
   *Falsified if*: any fixed class (any of #206–#211's breaks) has no test that fails on today's `main`/on fix-revert, or the "mapped" predicate exists in two independent implementations (emission and detection can silently diverge) — operationally pinned by AC-4.
