design:
## Requirements

1. **Auto-open the finalize PR (`mindspec-uxl4`).** When `impl approve`'s finalize lands the epic-close export on a `chore/finalize-<specID>` carrier (`result.FinalizeBranch` non-empty, `internal/approve/impl.go:562`) and the `gh` CLI is available, the verb MUST open a PR from that branch into `main` with the templated title `chore(beads): finalize epic <epicID> for spec <specID>` (the existing commit-message shape, `mindspec_executor.go:937`; note today's NOTE-suggested title at `cmd/mindspec/impl.go:196` OMITS the epicID — the automation's title includes it) and a templated body naming the spec, the epic, and the staleness consequence the NOTE states today (`impl.go:197`). Because the cmd-side automation home consumes `approve.ImplResult`, which today carries NO epic ID, the result surface MUST additionally expose the finalizing epic's ID (populated wherever `FinalizeBranch` is set) — a bounded result-surface addition, not new behavior. The PR URL MUST be surfaced in the verb's output escaped as free text, and any PR title or other remote-provided string echoed back renders escaped likewise (ADR-0042). The operation MUST be idempotent across re-runs, with a pinned adoption rule: an already-open PR is adopted as success (its URL re-surfaced, never a duplicate or an error) ONLY when its base is `main` AND its head is exactly `chore/finalize-<specID>`; a same-head PR with any other base is NOT adopted — the automation degrades (warning + NOTE) and such a PR is never auto-merged under Requirement 2. Every ID operand embedded in `gh` argv passes `idvalidate` at each construction site (ADR-0042 gate-all-ids); the `gh` invocations route through an injectable seam so the harness `gh` shim (`internal/harness/recorder.go:122`) can pin them. Governed by a new flat config key `auto_open_finalize_pr` (bool, default **true**), beside `auto_finalize` (`internal/config/config.go:21`), rendered by `mindspec config` (`cmd/mindspec/config.go:139` area).
2. **Opt-in auto-merge on green checks, with a merge commit (`mindspec-uxl4`).** Behind a second flat config key `auto_merge_finalize_pr` (bool, default **false** — merging to `main` without a human is opt-in policy, never default), after opening or ADOPTING a PR under Requirement 1 the verb MUST wait for its checks (the `gh pr checks --watch` equivalent through the same seam, bounded per Requirement 3) and, on affirmative all-green evidence, merge it with a TRUE MERGE COMMIT (`gh pr merge --merge`) — never squash or rebase, so the ancestry/net-effect consumers (the doctor merged-carrier suppression, `finalize_orphans.go:130`, and the Requirement 4 predicate) observe the carrier as landed. Three boundary semantics are pinned: **(a) merge only what R1 vetted** — auto-merge operates ONLY on a PR Requirement 1 opened or adopted (head/base pinned there); with `auto_open_finalize_pr: false` no PR is opened or adopted, so `auto_merge_finalize_pr: true` is INERT — no merge is attempted against any pre-existing operator PR, and a warning names the inert key combination. **(b) zero checks is not green** — a checks query reporting NO checks configured/reported (the conventional `gh pr checks` failure on a checkless PR) is NOT green: the PR is left open with the NOTE; auto-merge fires only on positive green evidence, never on absence of evidence. **(c) post-merge ref freshness, for BOTH finding kinds** — after a successful merge (including a merge observed via Requirement 3's reconcile query), the automation MUST refresh `origin/main` (a best-effort `git fetch origin main`, mirroring the probe's own fetch discipline inside `mindspec_executor.go:711-726`) so the suppression and predicate evaluate against real refreshed refs, not stale local ancestry; a fetch failure degrades to a warning (the doctor finding then clears on a later fetch — detection is delayed, never lost). The fetch alone only cures the `finalize_branch` finding: the sibling `stale_tracker` classifier today reads LOCAL `main`'s committed export (`finalize_orphans.go:186`), which no fetch advances — so post-auto-merge it would emit a factually-false "the finalize export never reached main" whose recovery line (`finalize_orphans.go:80`, `mindspec impl approve <spec>`) self-loops, violating this spec's own §2(i) doctrine. The classifier MUST therefore consult the refreshed `origin/main` committed export for this determination, aligning with the `finalize_branch` sibling's never-possibly-stale-local-`main` discipline (`finalize_orphans.go:99` area); a residual local-`main` lag behind an export that HAS reached `origin/main` may be surfaced only as a pull advisory whose recovery is a pull/update of local `main` — never a re-finalize of an epic whose export already landed. On success the finalize-orphan finding for that spec MUST no longer be reported by `lifecycle.ScanIntegrityFindings`. With the key false, no merge is attempted and the PR is left open for the operator (and doctor keeps flagging it until merged — the `mindspec-3xqm` item-2 surfacing interop preserved by construction).
3. **The PR automation is strictly post-finalize, best-effort, and evidence-honest about partial failure — it never fails or un-finalizes the verb.** Both legs run only AFTER the finalize mutation chain has durably completed (branch committed and pushed, epic closed). A nonzero `gh` result is NOT proof that nothing landed — GitHub may create or merge server-side and the client lose the response — so after ANY failed leg (`pr create`, the existing-PR lookup, `pr checks`, `pr merge`, or a timeout on any of them) the automation MUST reconcile by querying the exact head→base PR state through the same seam (itself bounded): an observed OPEN PR is create-success (its URL surfaced), an observed MERGED PR is merge-success (Requirement 2's post-merge path applies), and the stranded-carrier NOTE asserts "unmerged" ONLY when that query confirms no such open/merged PR exists — when the query itself fails, the warning names the state UNDETERMINED and the NOTE falls back without asserting either way. Every `gh` leg carries a bounded timeout; a timeout follows the same degrade-and-reconcile path. Every failure — `gh` absent from PATH, a failed leg, checks non-green, a watch timeout — MUST degrade to today's behavior: the NOTE with the manual `gh pr create` command (`cmd/mindspec/impl.go:194-197`), a warning naming the failed leg and (when one exists) the open PR, and **exit 0** — the finalize itself succeeded, the stranded-carrier state remains fully detected by the shipped doctor check, and tracker/git state is byte-identical to a no-`gh` run. `gh` stderr/error text embedded in any warning, and remote check names surfaced in any output, render `termsafe`-escaped (ADR-0042). These legs are classified DOCUMENTED-FORWARD-SAFE under ADR-0041 §3 (their errors are absorbed by design; the audit trail is the doctor finding), and the fault-injection suite MUST record that classification rather than fabricate kill tests against them.
4. **Content-aware already-merged detection — net-effect, one predicate, both consumers (`mindspec-3xqm` item 1).** The "this branch's work already landed on `origin/main`" decision MUST become a single exported predicate (home: `internal/lifecycle` or `internal/gitutil` — plan-level) whose meaning is NET-EFFECT equivalence against `origin/main`'s CURRENT state, not historical patch presence: when SHA ancestry fails, the content-level fallback (mechanism plan-level — e.g. a cherry/patch-id or committed-tree comparison evaluated against the current tree) reports landed iff the branch introduces NO content absent from `origin/main` as it stands NOW. Whether ancestry ALONE suffices is decided per consumer, because the two consumers answer different questions: for the PROBE, SHA ancestry remains sufficient as-is (the probe decides carrier ROUTING — an ancestor spec branch is a spent PR carrier regardless of later history, since nothing pushed to it can reach `main` again; a later revert of its work on `main` is a `main`-side state the doctor/stale-tracker surface detects, not a routing input); for the DOCTOR suppression, ancestry alone is NOT sufficient — the suppression decision is the net-effect/current-content test even when ancestry holds, so a carrier that was truly (non-squash) merged and then REVERTED on `origin/main` is flagged again (its tracker content is once more absent from `main` — suppressing it would hide a genuinely-stranded export behind a historical merge). Pinned consequences: a squash-merge whose content was later REVERTED on `origin/main` is NOT landed; a branch only PART of whose content is present (partially-landed-plus-novel) is NOT landed; a squash-merge followed by unrelated later `main` changes IS landed. BOTH existing SHA-only sites consume the one exported symbol, with the observable contract stated PER CARRIER: the protected-main probe in `FinalizeEpic` (`mindspec_executor.go:711-726`) evaluates a SPEC branch (code + tracker; net effect over the branch's full diff against its merge-base with `origin/main`) — a squash-merged spec branch routes to the `chore/finalize-` carrier instead of pushing the epic-close commit onto the dead carrier, retiring the known-blind-spot comment at `:700-704`; the doctor merged-carrier suppression (`finalize_orphans.go:126-130`) evaluates a `chore/finalize` carrier (tracker-JSONL-only; net effect over its single regenerated `.beads/issues.jsonl` payload) — a carrier whose epic-close content `main`'s committed export already carries, including via a LATER superseding export, is suppressed, while one whose JSONL still carries novel content keeps being flagged. A genuinely-unmerged branch carrying novel work MUST NOT be misdetected as landed (the normal push path is unchanged). Each consumer's infra-error fail-posture is pinned EXPLICITLY: the probe, on a content-fallback infra failure, WARNS naming the undetermined probe and proceeds on the ancestry answer alone — a fail-open (`orphaned=false` can push the epic-close onto a possibly-dead carrier) retained DELIBERATELY because that stranded outcome remains fully detected by the shipped doctor finalize-orphan finding, the same absorb that already covers the probe's fetch-failure leg; the suppression, on an infra failure, SKIPS the branch asserting nothing, surfacing the first error through the existing mixed-list contract (`finalize_orphans.go:130-135`).
5. **Landed-merge identity: durably corroborated, never subject-only (`mindspec-q9ea`).** `lifecycle.FindLandedMerge` MUST NOT positively identify a candidate on subject text alone, and no heuristic over the candidate's CONTENTS substitutes for identity — that the second parent carries non-empty work is explicitly NOT corroboration (it proves somebody merged something, not that THIS bead's work landed). (a) **Durable corroboration only**: a candidate is positively identified only when at least one independent identity datum CONFIRMS it (equals or is an ancestor of the candidate's second parent) and no available datum contradicts it. The admissible data are: a registered panel's `reviewed_head_sha` (existing, `landed.go:136-146`); a surviving bead-branch tip (existing, `:147-153`); and the lifecycle-recorded landed-binding of (b). (b) **The binding is recorded at merge time, FAIL-CLOSED before cleanup** (the small in-scope addition that makes (a) livable): both in-binary bead→spec merge producers — `CompleteBead`'s merge leg (`mindspec_executor.go:410`) and `FinalizeEpic`'s auto-merge leg (`:622`) — MUST, after `gitutil.MergeInto` succeeds and BEFORE any branch/worktree cleanup for that bead, durably record the bead→merge binding (the merge commit SHA and its second-parent SHA) in bd metadata through the existing `bead.MergeMetadata` surface (`internal/bead/bdcli.go:322`; Dolt is the state authority, ADR-0023; in-tree precedent: the reconcile-evidence write at `complete.go:1043`). The write's FAILURE posture is part of the contract, not an implementation choice: a failed binding write MUST suppress that bead's branch/worktree cleanup and refuse recoverably with an ADR-0035 recovery line naming the verb's own re-run — mirroring the refuse-recoverably shape of the cited reconcile-evidence precedent (`complete.go:1032-1055`), NOT the warn-and-continue style of the adjacent cleanup legs (`mindspec_executor.go:437-450`) — so the branch survives as the corroborating datum and re-invocation converges (a re-attempted `MergeInto` of an already-ancestor branch is a no-op). On that re-invocation the binding write MUST locate the already-landed merge BY IDENTITY (the subject-scan candidate corroborated by the surviving branch tip) and record THAT merge's SHAs — never assume the current tip or `HEAD` is the merge. The invariant that closes the evidence gap for every lifecycle-produced merge holds BECAUSE write-failure suppresses cleanup, not merely because of ordering: at any interruption OR failure point at least one corroborating datum exists — before the record lands, the bead branch still survives (cleanup has not run, and a failed write keeps it that way); after it lands, the binding itself corroborates. A no-datum state is therefore reachable only for out-of-band merges and pre-existing (pre-121) history. (c) **Fail-closed with a genuine forward exit**: a candidate with NO confirming datum is `ErrLandedMergeNotFound` — the reconcile refuses via 119's existing no-evidence path (119 AC-8) and NEVER closes on subject text. That refusal's recovery MUST be a forward exit that is NOT bare re-invocation (re-running cannot change the refusing fact): it names the candidate merge and second-parent SHAs the subject scan found and the exact attested-restore command — restore the bead branch ref at the candidate's second parent (`git branch bead/<id> <second-parent SHA>`) — whose execution is an explicit operator ATTESTATION that the merge carried this bead's work, converting the state into the surviving-branch corroboration leg; re-running then converges. Because orchestrators follow recovery lines mechanically, this refusal line MUST carry an explicit human-verification marker (to the effect of "running this command attests that merge <SHA> carried THIS bead's work — verify before running; do not execute blindly") distinguishing it from the mechanically-safe recovery lines every other refusal in this spec names. This keeps ADR-0041 §2 deadlock-free (Requirement 8 pins it in the amendment): the machine never self-loops, and never closes without evidence. (d) **Revert- and reapply-aware, defined as net effect SINCE the merge**: a candidate M whose merged work was subsequently reverted on the spec branch's first-parent chain and NOT re-applied MUST NOT be identified as landed (the refusal names the revert evidence). The contract is pinned against the mechanism shape that would otherwise deadlock it: a reapply (a revert-of-the-revert, or a cherry-pick of the work) creates NO new `Merge bead/<id>` merge commit — the newest-first subject scan still finds only M — so revert-awareness MUST be evaluated as the NET EFFECT of the first-parent chain SINCE M (a revert later canceled by a reapply does not disqualify M; the same doctrine as Requirement 4, detection mechanism plan-level). A reverted-then-reapplied M therefore IS identified and the reconcile closes; "reject any M that was ever reverted" is a non-conforming implementation (it would manufacture a permanent refusal for an honest landed state, violating the §2 deadlock-free rule of (c)). (e) **Regression floor, per-datum**: 119's AC-5/AC-7/AC-9 fixtures — genuine landed merges, panel-free and panel-registered, branch deleted — MUST still reconcile and close (assertions unchanged), plus new honest multi-commit and conflict-resolution merge fixtures that likewise reconcile and close. Each admissible datum of (a) MUST be pinned as INDEPENDENTLY sufficient: the panel-registered variant stays binding-ABSENT (its real-world counterpart is pre-121 history that has no binding — a binding-REQUIRED implementation must fail it), a surviving-branch-only binding-absent variant closes, and a binding-only variant closes (AC-12).
6. **Orphan-preflight convergence — no mutual refusal (`mindspec-tpjn`).** `complete`'s step-1.6 preflight already excludes the invoked bead from the orphan enumeration (`findOrphanedClosedBeadsFn(specID, root, beadID)` passes `excludeBeadID = beadID`, `complete.go:491`) — the deadlock is two beads each refusing on the OTHER. The preflight MUST converge for ANY set of simultaneously closed-but-unmerged siblings: (a) the preflight additionally determines whether the INVOKED bead is ITSELF orphaned-closed (closed in the tracker with its branch unmerged — the recovery in progress); when it is, the other-orphan refusal demotes to a WARN naming EVERY orphaned sibling, and the invoked bead's recovery proceeds. When that self-orphan determination hits an infra/ancestry error, the invoked bead is treated as NOT self-orphaned and the refusal is RETAINED — a retryable preflight refusal with nothing mutated (ADR-0041 §1), never a demotion on unproven evidence. (b) when the invoked bead is NOT itself orphaned, the refusal is retained but MUST name ALL orphaned siblings (not just `orphans[0]`) with a single recovery sequence (`mindspec complete <A>`, `mindspec complete <B>`, then re-run) — so the full non-manual exit is knowable from one refusal. (c) the WARN-demotion path deliberately admits an INTERMEDIATE state — completing A lands A while WARN'd siblings linger orphaned — and that is safe by construction: each step strictly shrinks the orphan set (the sequence is monotone and finite), and the shipped fail-closed impl-approve orphan gate (`ScanOrphanedClosedBeads`, `orphans.go:142`, 119 Bead 2) backstops it by refusing to finalize the epic while ANY orphan remains. Net contract: from any such state there exists a finite sequence of `mindspec complete` invocations, each named by the previous output, that converges with no manual git surgery — ADR-0041 §2 made true for this gate. IDs in the new warning/refusal text render via `idrender`/`termsafe` per the shipped conventions at this site.
7. **Containment-gate the destructive worktree wrapper (`mindspec-17bd`).** `gitutil.WorktreeRemoveForce` (`gitops.go:935`) MUST run the same wrapper-level symlink-aware containment check as `WorktreeAddDetach` (`gitops.go:895`) and `WorktreeAdd` (`:920`) — `containment.CheckContainment(workdir, wtPath)` — BEFORE invoking `git worktree remove --force`; on violation it refuses with the containment error and removes nothing. The 3xqm item-5 finding names a SECOND half beyond containment: the wrapper's argv carries the composed path with no `--` separator, so an option-like composed path could parse as a git flag — the wrapper MUST also guard that operand (the sibling `rejectOptionLike` discipline, or a `--` separator before the path), refusing/neutralizing an option-like `wtPath` before invocation. In-tree, plainly-named removals are byte-identical in behavior. The caller-level gate spec 120's final review added before the finalize self-heal remains (defense-in-depth); this closes every OTHER present and future caller at the wrapper, per ADR-0042's check-at-use discipline.
8. **ADR-0041 amendment.** ADR-0041 MUST be amended with the two additions named in ADR Touchpoints — §2 convergence-completeness (deadlock-free recovery graph whose every refusal names a genuine forward exit, including the attested-restore exit for the no-evidence landed-merge state; durably corroborated, revert/reapply-aware landed evidence, its binding recorded fail-closed-before-cleanup at merge time; net-effect content-aware already-merged re-derivation) and §4 machine-owned finalize-carrier automation (auto-open always-safe; auto-merge opt-in default-false + affirmative green checks + head/base adoption pin + merge commit; failures degrade with reconcile-by-query, never fail the verb) — landing in the same bead as the code that first cites it, so the ADR-divergence gate sees the declared touchpoint.
9. **Regression pinning and anti-drift.** Every failure class fixed by this spec MUST be pinned by an automated test that reproduces the original trigger and goes RED if the fix is reverted. The shared already-merged predicate MUST be consumed by both Requirement 4 sites via the SAME exported symbol, pinned by a test that fails if either site is rewired to a private reimplementation (the 119 AC-12 anti-drift pattern). New mutation/automation points introduced by Requirement 1–3 MUST be classified kill-tested vs documented-forward-safe per ADR-0041 §3, honestly, in the existing fault-injection suites. The Requirement 5 landed-binding write is classified NOW, by this spec: it is **KILL-TESTED** — its failure genuinely terminates the run with a recoverable refusal and suppresses cleanup (R5(b)), so it is never recorded documented-forward-safe; AC-22 is its kill test at both producer legs.

title: [121-lifecycle-completion-integrity] Bead 1: Net-effect already-merged predicate — one symbol, both consumers, refreshed stale-tracker classifier
description:
R4 in full plus R2(c)'s classifier leg, and the ADR-0041 §2 amendment
(the first citing code — see the preamble re-cut rationale). Makes
"already landed on `origin/main`" a single exported content-aware
predicate consumed by the `FinalizeEpic` probe and the doctor
merged-carrier suppression; retires the known-blind-spot comment;
moves the stale-tracker classifier off possibly-stale local `main`.

**Steps**

1. Add `internal/gitutil/neteffect.go`:
   `ContentSubsumed(workdir, base, ref, target string) (bool, error)`
   — the shared three-way primitive (merge-tree --write-tree; result
   tree == target tree, no conflicts ⇒ subsumed) — and the ONE
   exported predicate `NetEffectLanded(workdir, ref, target string)
   (bool, error)` implementing the two-leg mechanism from the plan
   choice above (tree subsumption; tracker-payload subsumption for a
   diff confined to `.beads/issues.jsonl`). The `merge-tree`
   EXIT-CODE TRICHOTOMY is part of the contract (panel O1): exit 0 ⇒
   compare the result tree OID against target's tree OID; exit 1 ⇒
   CONFLICT — a leg-(a) NOT-landed answer (or, for a JSONL-confined
   diff, the fall-through into leg (b)), NEVER an infra error; exit
   ≥ 2 ⇒ infra error, propagated. Conflating exit 1 with infra would
   silently break the "later superseding export ⇒ suppressed" clause
   and R2(c)'s self-loop avoidance (AC-19's superseding leg pins
   it). Leg (b) subsumes by the status TOTAL ORDER
   `open < in_progress < closed`: a changed id→status assertion is
   satisfied only by an equal-or-LATER status in target's export — a
   non-terminal status on `main` can never subsume a carrier's
   close. Doc comment cites ADR-0041 §2(iii) and states the pinned
   consequences verbatim: squash-then-revert ⇒ NOT landed;
   partially-landed-plus-novel ⇒ NOT landed;
   squash-then-unrelated-later-changes ⇒ landed. Infra failures
   (including git < 2.38, where `--write-tree` is unsupported)
   return errors, never a guessed boolean.
2. Amend `.mindspec/adr/ADR-0041-gate-before-mutate.md` with the §2
   convergence-completeness additions exactly as the spec's ADR
   Touchpoints state them: (i) deadlock-free recovery graph / genuine
   forward exits (naming the tpjn all-orphans sequence and the q9ea
   attested-restore exit as the two instances); (ii) durably
   corroborated, never-subject-only, revert/reapply-aware-by-net-
   effect landed evidence, with the merge-time binding recorded
   fail-closed-before-cleanup; (iii) content-aware already-merged
   re-derivation where the hosting workflow can discard SHAs. Cite §2
   from the predicate's doc comment (this bead's citing code).
3. Rewire the PROBE (`internal/executor/mindspec_executor.go:711-726`)
   through a package seam var (`netEffectLandedFn =
   gitutil.NetEffectLanded`): ancestry remains sufficient as-is (the
   spent-carrier routing rationale, restated in the comment); when
   ancestry is false, fall back to the net-effect predicate over the
   spec branch's full diff. On a content-fallback INFRA failure: warn
   naming the undetermined probe and proceed on the ancestry answer
   alone — the DELIBERATE fail-open the spec pins (the stranded
   outcome stays fully detected by the shipped doctor finding).
   Retire the known-blind-spot comment at `:700-704`, replacing it
   with the per-consumer contract note.
4. Rewire the DOCTOR suppression
   (`internal/lifecycle/finalize_orphans.go:126-139`) through its own
   seam var (`finalizeOrphanNetEffectFn = gitutil.NetEffectLanded`):
   the suppression decision becomes the net-effect test EVEN WHEN
   ancestry holds (a true-merged-then-reverted carrier is flagged
   again); on an infra failure the branch is SKIPPED asserting
   nothing, surfaced through the existing mixed-list `firstErr`
   contract (`:130-135` discipline unchanged).
5. R2(c) classifier leg: `StaleTrackerOnMain` and
   `ScanIntegrityFindings`' committed-export read
   (`finalize_orphans.go:186`, `scan.go`) consult the refreshed
   `origin/main:.beads/issues.jsonl` for the "export never reached
   main" determination (falling back to local `main` only when no
   `origin/main` ref exists — the no-remote direct workflow); a
   residual local-`main` lag behind an export that HAS reached
   `origin/main` surfaces only as a pull advisory whose recovery is a
   pull/update of local `main` — never `mindspec impl approve`
   (the self-loop the spec's §2(i) forbids). The
   `internal/doctor/lifecycle_integrity.go` wiring is UNCHANGED
   (interop pins only, per Impacted Domains).
6. AC-17 anti-drift pin: a function-identity test asserting BOTH seam
   defaults (executor probe, lifecycle suppression) are
   `gitutil.NetEffectLanded`.
7. Fixtures (real bare-origin, per Testing Strategy): AC-8 (squash-
   merged spec branch → predicate landed; probe routes to the
   `chore/finalize-` carrier); AC-9 both consumers both polarities
   (genuinely-unmerged novel branch NOT landed / normal push path
   unchanged; squash-merged carrier no longer flagged; truly-unmerged
   carrier still flagged); AC-19 all four halves incl. (iv)
   true-merge-then-revert flagged at the doctor while the same shape
   stays ancestry-routed at the probe (asserted unchanged); the
   superseding-export suppression leg; an OLD-GIT subtest (a stubbed
   primitive seam returning the unsupported-`--write-tree` error:
   the predicate propagates an ERROR, never a boolean — panel O1);
   INFRA-POSTURE sentinel-stub subtests PER CONSUMER (seam stubbed
   to a sentinel error: the probe WARNS naming the undetermined
   probe and proceeds on the ancestry answer alone; the suppression
   SKIPS the branch asserting nothing, sentinel surfaced as the
   mixed-list `firstErr` — panel F2); the AC-16 §2 anchor test
   (amendment text covers the §2 anchors; predicate doc cites §2).

**Verification**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/gitutil/... ./internal/executor/... ./internal/lifecycle/... ./internal/doctor/...` passes; `golangci-lint run ./...` clean
- [ ] AC-8 subtest RED on today's `main` (the documented blind spot); probe routes squash-merged spec branch to the carrier
- [ ] AC-9 subtests: both consumers, both polarities, normal push path byte-identical for a novel branch
- [ ] AC-19 subtests: (i)/(ii) pass as anti-false-positive guards (tag deviation stated in-test), (iii)/(iv) RED on revert; probe ancestry-split asserted
- [ ] AC-17 identity pin fails when either consumer is rewired to a private copy
- [ ] Old-git subtest: unsupported `--write-tree` propagates as an error, never a boolean; per-consumer infra-posture subtests green (probe warn+ancestry-only; suppression skip+`firstErr`)
- [ ] Stale-tracker classifier reads `origin/main`'s export; pull-advisory recovery line asserted (never a re-finalize); no-remote fallback covered
- [ ] AC-16 §2 half: amendment text anchors present (`rg -n 'convergence' .mindspec/adr/ADR-0041-gate-before-mutate.md` non-empty); predicate cites §2

design:
## Requirements

1. **Auto-open the finalize PR (`mindspec-uxl4`).** When `impl approve`'s finalize lands the epic-close export on a `chore/finalize-<specID>` carrier (`result.FinalizeBranch` non-empty, `internal/approve/impl.go:562`) and the `gh` CLI is available, the verb MUST open a PR from that branch into `main` with the templated title `chore(beads): finalize epic <epicID> for spec <specID>` (the existing commit-message shape, `mindspec_executor.go:937`; note today's NOTE-suggested title at `cmd/mindspec/impl.go:196` OMITS the epicID — the automation's title includes it) and a templated body naming the spec, the epic, and the staleness consequence the NOTE states today (`impl.go:197`). Because the cmd-side automation home consumes `approve.ImplResult`, which today carries NO epic ID, the result surface MUST additionally expose the finalizing epic's ID (populated wherever `FinalizeBranch` is set) — a bounded result-surface addition, not new behavior. The PR URL MUST be surfaced in the verb's output escaped as free text, and any PR title or other remote-provided string echoed back renders escaped likewise (ADR-0042). The operation MUST be idempotent across re-runs, with a pinned adoption rule: an already-open PR is adopted as success (its URL re-surfaced, never a duplicate or an error) ONLY when its base is `main` AND its head is exactly `chore/finalize-<specID>`; a same-head PR with any other base is NOT adopted — the automation degrades (warning + NOTE) and such a PR is never auto-merged under Requirement 2. Every ID operand embedded in `gh` argv passes `idvalidate` at each construction site (ADR-0042 gate-all-ids); the `gh` invocations route through an injectable seam so the harness `gh` shim (`internal/harness/recorder.go:122`) can pin them. Governed by a new flat config key `auto_open_finalize_pr` (bool, default **true**), beside `auto_finalize` (`internal/config/config.go:21`), rendered by `mindspec config` (`cmd/mindspec/config.go:139` area).
2. **Opt-in auto-merge on green checks, with a merge commit (`mindspec-uxl4`).** Behind a second flat config key `auto_merge_finalize_pr` (bool, default **false** — merging to `main` without a human is opt-in policy, never default), after opening or ADOPTING a PR under Requirement 1 the verb MUST wait for its checks (the `gh pr checks --watch` equivalent through the same seam, bounded per Requirement 3) and, on affirmative all-green evidence, merge it with a TRUE MERGE COMMIT (`gh pr merge --merge`) — never squash or rebase, so the ancestry/net-effect consumers (the doctor merged-carrier suppression, `finalize_orphans.go:130`, and the Requirement 4 predicate) observe the carrier as landed. Three boundary semantics are pinned: **(a) merge only what R1 vetted** — auto-merge operates ONLY on a PR Requirement 1 opened or adopted (head/base pinned there); with `auto_open_finalize_pr: false` no PR is opened or adopted, so `auto_merge_finalize_pr: true` is INERT — no merge is attempted against any pre-existing operator PR, and a warning names the inert key combination. **(b) zero checks is not green** — a checks query reporting NO checks configured/reported (the conventional `gh pr checks` failure on a checkless PR) is NOT green: the PR is left open with the NOTE; auto-merge fires only on positive green evidence, never on absence of evidence. **(c) post-merge ref freshness, for BOTH finding kinds** — after a successful merge (including a merge observed via Requirement 3's reconcile query), the automation MUST refresh `origin/main` (a best-effort `git fetch origin main`, mirroring the probe's own fetch discipline inside `mindspec_executor.go:711-726`) so the suppression and predicate evaluate against real refreshed refs, not stale local ancestry; a fetch failure degrades to a warning (the doctor finding then clears on a later fetch — detection is delayed, never lost). The fetch alone only cures the `finalize_branch` finding: the sibling `stale_tracker` classifier today reads LOCAL `main`'s committed export (`finalize_orphans.go:186`), which no fetch advances — so post-auto-merge it would emit a factually-false "the finalize export never reached main" whose recovery line (`finalize_orphans.go:80`, `mindspec impl approve <spec>`) self-loops, violating this spec's own §2(i) doctrine. The classifier MUST therefore consult the refreshed `origin/main` committed export for this determination, aligning with the `finalize_branch` sibling's never-possibly-stale-local-`main` discipline (`finalize_orphans.go:99` area); a residual local-`main` lag behind an export that HAS reached `origin/main` may be surfaced only as a pull advisory whose recovery is a pull/update of local `main` — never a re-finalize of an epic whose export already landed. On success the finalize-orphan finding for that spec MUST no longer be reported by `lifecycle.ScanIntegrityFindings`. With the key false, no merge is attempted and the PR is left open for the operator (and doctor keeps flagging it until merged — the `mindspec-3xqm` item-2 surfacing interop preserved by construction).
3. **The PR automation is strictly post-finalize, best-effort, and evidence-honest about partial failure — it never fails or un-finalizes the verb.** Both legs run only AFTER the finalize mutation chain has durably completed (branch committed and pushed, epic closed). A nonzero `gh` result is NOT proof that nothing landed — GitHub may create or merge server-side and the client lose the response — so after ANY failed leg (`pr create`, the existing-PR lookup, `pr checks`, `pr merge`, or a timeout on any of them) the automation MUST reconcile by querying the exact head→base PR state through the same seam (itself bounded): an observed OPEN PR is create-success (its URL surfaced), an observed MERGED PR is merge-success (Requirement 2's post-merge path applies), and the stranded-carrier NOTE asserts "unmerged" ONLY when that query confirms no such open/merged PR exists — when the query itself fails, the warning names the state UNDETERMINED and the NOTE falls back without asserting either way. Every `gh` leg carries a bounded timeout; a timeout follows the same degrade-and-reconcile path. Every failure — `gh` absent from PATH, a failed leg, checks non-green, a watch timeout — MUST degrade to today's behavior: the NOTE with the manual `gh pr create` command (`cmd/mindspec/impl.go:194-197`), a warning naming the failed leg and (when one exists) the open PR, and **exit 0** — the finalize itself succeeded, the stranded-carrier state remains fully detected by the shipped doctor check, and tracker/git state is byte-identical to a no-`gh` run. `gh` stderr/error text embedded in any warning, and remote check names surfaced in any output, render `termsafe`-escaped (ADR-0042). These legs are classified DOCUMENTED-FORWARD-SAFE under ADR-0041 §3 (their errors are absorbed by design; the audit trail is the doctor finding), and the fault-injection suite MUST record that classification rather than fabricate kill tests against them.
4. **Content-aware already-merged detection — net-effect, one predicate, both consumers (`mindspec-3xqm` item 1).** The "this branch's work already landed on `origin/main`" decision MUST become a single exported predicate (home: `internal/lifecycle` or `internal/gitutil` — plan-level) whose meaning is NET-EFFECT equivalence against `origin/main`'s CURRENT state, not historical patch presence: when SHA ancestry fails, the content-level fallback (mechanism plan-level — e.g. a cherry/patch-id or committed-tree comparison evaluated against the current tree) reports landed iff the branch introduces NO content absent from `origin/main` as it stands NOW. Whether ancestry ALONE suffices is decided per consumer, because the two consumers answer different questions: for the PROBE, SHA ancestry remains sufficient as-is (the probe decides carrier ROUTING — an ancestor spec branch is a spent PR carrier regardless of later history, since nothing pushed to it can reach `main` again; a later revert of its work on `main` is a `main`-side state the doctor/stale-tracker surface detects, not a routing input); for the DOCTOR suppression, ancestry alone is NOT sufficient — the suppression decision is the net-effect/current-content test even when ancestry holds, so a carrier that was truly (non-squash) merged and then REVERTED on `origin/main` is flagged again (its tracker content is once more absent from `main` — suppressing it would hide a genuinely-stranded export behind a historical merge). Pinned consequences: a squash-merge whose content was later REVERTED on `origin/main` is NOT landed; a branch only PART of whose content is present (partially-landed-plus-novel) is NOT landed; a squash-merge followed by unrelated later `main` changes IS landed. BOTH existing SHA-only sites consume the one exported symbol, with the observable contract stated PER CARRIER: the protected-main probe in `FinalizeEpic` (`mindspec_executor.go:711-726`) evaluates a SPEC branch (code + tracker; net effect over the branch's full diff against its merge-base with `origin/main`) — a squash-merged spec branch routes to the `chore/finalize-` carrier instead of pushing the epic-close commit onto the dead carrier, retiring the known-blind-spot comment at `:700-704`; the doctor merged-carrier suppression (`finalize_orphans.go:126-130`) evaluates a `chore/finalize` carrier (tracker-JSONL-only; net effect over its single regenerated `.beads/issues.jsonl` payload) — a carrier whose epic-close content `main`'s committed export already carries, including via a LATER superseding export, is suppressed, while one whose JSONL still carries novel content keeps being flagged. A genuinely-unmerged branch carrying novel work MUST NOT be misdetected as landed (the normal push path is unchanged). Each consumer's infra-error fail-posture is pinned EXPLICITLY: the probe, on a content-fallback infra failure, WARNS naming the undetermined probe and proceeds on the ancestry answer alone — a fail-open (`orphaned=false` can push the epic-close onto a possibly-dead carrier) retained DELIBERATELY because that stranded outcome remains fully detected by the shipped doctor finalize-orphan finding, the same absorb that already covers the probe's fetch-failure leg; the suppression, on an infra failure, SKIPS the branch asserting nothing, surfacing the first error through the existing mixed-list contract (`finalize_orphans.go:130-135`).
5. **Landed-merge identity: durably corroborated, never subject-only (`mindspec-q9ea`).** `lifecycle.FindLandedMerge` MUST NOT positively identify a candidate on subject text alone, and no heuristic over the candidate's CONTENTS substitutes for identity — that the second parent carries non-empty work is explicitly NOT corroboration (it proves somebody merged something, not that THIS bead's work landed). (a) **Durable corroboration only**: a candidate is positively identified only when at least one independent identity datum CONFIRMS it (equals or is an ancestor of the candidate's second parent) and no available datum contradicts it. The admissible data are: a registered panel's `reviewed_head_sha` (existing, `landed.go:136-146`); a surviving bead-branch tip (existing, `:147-153`); and the lifecycle-recorded landed-binding of (b). (b) **The binding is recorded at merge time, FAIL-CLOSED before cleanup** (the small in-scope addition that makes (a) livable): both in-binary bead→spec merge producers — `CompleteBead`'s merge leg (`mindspec_executor.go:410`) and `FinalizeEpic`'s auto-merge leg (`:622`) — MUST, after `gitutil.MergeInto` succeeds and BEFORE any branch/worktree cleanup for that bead, durably record the bead→merge binding (the merge commit SHA and its second-parent SHA) in bd metadata through the existing `bead.MergeMetadata` surface (`internal/bead/bdcli.go:322`; Dolt is the state authority, ADR-0023; in-tree precedent: the reconcile-evidence write at `complete.go:1043`). The write's FAILURE posture is part of the contract, not an implementation choice: a failed binding write MUST suppress that bead's branch/worktree cleanup and refuse recoverably with an ADR-0035 recovery line naming the verb's own re-run — mirroring the refuse-recoverably shape of the cited reconcile-evidence precedent (`complete.go:1032-1055`), NOT the warn-and-continue style of the adjacent cleanup legs (`mindspec_executor.go:437-450`) — so the branch survives as the corroborating datum and re-invocation converges (a re-attempted `MergeInto` of an already-ancestor branch is a no-op). On that re-invocation the binding write MUST locate the already-landed merge BY IDENTITY (the subject-scan candidate corroborated by the surviving branch tip) and record THAT merge's SHAs — never assume the current tip or `HEAD` is the merge. The invariant that closes the evidence gap for every lifecycle-produced merge holds BECAUSE write-failure suppresses cleanup, not merely because of ordering: at any interruption OR failure point at least one corroborating datum exists — before the record lands, the bead branch still survives (cleanup has not run, and a failed write keeps it that way); after it lands, the binding itself corroborates. A no-datum state is therefore reachable only for out-of-band merges and pre-existing (pre-121) history. (c) **Fail-closed with a genuine forward exit**: a candidate with NO confirming datum is `ErrLandedMergeNotFound` — the reconcile refuses via 119's existing no-evidence path (119 AC-8) and NEVER closes on subject text. That refusal's recovery MUST be a forward exit that is NOT bare re-invocation (re-running cannot change the refusing fact): it names the candidate merge and second-parent SHAs the subject scan found and the exact attested-restore command — restore the bead branch ref at the candidate's second parent (`git branch bead/<id> <second-parent SHA>`) — whose execution is an explicit operator ATTESTATION that the merge carried this bead's work, converting the state into the surviving-branch corroboration leg; re-running then converges. Because orchestrators follow recovery lines mechanically, this refusal line MUST carry an explicit human-verification marker (to the effect of "running this command attests that merge <SHA> carried THIS bead's work — verify before running; do not execute blindly") distinguishing it from the mechanically-safe recovery lines every other refusal in this spec names. This keeps ADR-0041 §2 deadlock-free (Requirement 8 pins it in the amendment): the machine never self-loops, and never closes without evidence. (d) **Revert- and reapply-aware, defined as net effect SINCE the merge**: a candidate M whose merged work was subsequently reverted on the spec branch's first-parent chain and NOT re-applied MUST NOT be identified as landed (the refusal names the revert evidence). The contract is pinned against the mechanism shape that would otherwise deadlock it: a reapply (a revert-of-the-revert, or a cherry-pick of the work) creates NO new `Merge bead/<id>` merge commit — the newest-first subject scan still finds only M — so revert-awareness MUST be evaluated as the NET EFFECT of the first-parent chain SINCE M (a revert later canceled by a reapply does not disqualify M; the same doctrine as Requirement 4, detection mechanism plan-level). A reverted-then-reapplied M therefore IS identified and the reconcile closes; "reject any M that was ever reverted" is a non-conforming implementation (it would manufacture a permanent refusal for an honest landed state, violating the §2 deadlock-free rule of (c)). (e) **Regression floor, per-datum**: 119's AC-5/AC-7/AC-9 fixtures — genuine landed merges, panel-free and panel-registered, branch deleted — MUST still reconcile and close (assertions unchanged), plus new honest multi-commit and conflict-resolution merge fixtures that likewise reconcile and close. Each admissible datum of (a) MUST be pinned as INDEPENDENTLY sufficient: the panel-registered variant stays binding-ABSENT (its real-world counterpart is pre-121 history that has no binding — a binding-REQUIRED implementation must fail it), a surviving-branch-only binding-absent variant closes, and a binding-only variant closes (AC-12).
6. **Orphan-preflight convergence — no mutual refusal (`mindspec-tpjn`).** `complete`'s step-1.6 preflight already excludes the invoked bead from the orphan enumeration (`findOrphanedClosedBeadsFn(specID, root, beadID)` passes `excludeBeadID = beadID`, `complete.go:491`) — the deadlock is two beads each refusing on the OTHER. The preflight MUST converge for ANY set of simultaneously closed-but-unmerged siblings: (a) the preflight additionally determines whether the INVOKED bead is ITSELF orphaned-closed (closed in the tracker with its branch unmerged — the recovery in progress); when it is, the other-orphan refusal demotes to a WARN naming EVERY orphaned sibling, and the invoked bead's recovery proceeds. When that self-orphan determination hits an infra/ancestry error, the invoked bead is treated as NOT self-orphaned and the refusal is RETAINED — a retryable preflight refusal with nothing mutated (ADR-0041 §1), never a demotion on unproven evidence. (b) when the invoked bead is NOT itself orphaned, the refusal is retained but MUST name ALL orphaned siblings (not just `orphans[0]`) with a single recovery sequence (`mindspec complete <A>`, `mindspec complete <B>`, then re-run) — so the full non-manual exit is knowable from one refusal. (c) the WARN-demotion path deliberately admits an INTERMEDIATE state — completing A lands A while WARN'd siblings linger orphaned — and that is safe by construction: each step strictly shrinks the orphan set (the sequence is monotone and finite), and the shipped fail-closed impl-approve orphan gate (`ScanOrphanedClosedBeads`, `orphans.go:142`, 119 Bead 2) backstops it by refusing to finalize the epic while ANY orphan remains. Net contract: from any such state there exists a finite sequence of `mindspec complete` invocations, each named by the previous output, that converges with no manual git surgery — ADR-0041 §2 made true for this gate. IDs in the new warning/refusal text render via `idrender`/`termsafe` per the shipped conventions at this site.
7. **Containment-gate the destructive worktree wrapper (`mindspec-17bd`).** `gitutil.WorktreeRemoveForce` (`gitops.go:935`) MUST run the same wrapper-level symlink-aware containment check as `WorktreeAddDetach` (`gitops.go:895`) and `WorktreeAdd` (`:920`) — `containment.CheckContainment(workdir, wtPath)` — BEFORE invoking `git worktree remove --force`; on violation it refuses with the containment error and removes nothing. The 3xqm item-5 finding names a SECOND half beyond containment: the wrapper's argv carries the composed path with no `--` separator, so an option-like composed path could parse as a git flag — the wrapper MUST also guard that operand (the sibling `rejectOptionLike` discipline, or a `--` separator before the path), refusing/neutralizing an option-like `wtPath` before invocation. In-tree, plainly-named removals are byte-identical in behavior. The caller-level gate spec 120's final review added before the finalize self-heal remains (defense-in-depth); this closes every OTHER present and future caller at the wrapper, per ADR-0042's check-at-use discipline.
8. **ADR-0041 amendment.** ADR-0041 MUST be amended with the two additions named in ADR Touchpoints — §2 convergence-completeness (deadlock-free recovery graph whose every refusal names a genuine forward exit, including the attested-restore exit for the no-evidence landed-merge state; durably corroborated, revert/reapply-aware landed evidence, its binding recorded fail-closed-before-cleanup at merge time; net-effect content-aware already-merged re-derivation) and §4 machine-owned finalize-carrier automation (auto-open always-safe; auto-merge opt-in default-false + affirmative green checks + head/base adoption pin + merge commit; failures degrade with reconcile-by-query, never fail the verb) — landing in the same bead as the code that first cites it, so the ADR-divergence gate sees the declared touchpoint.
9. **Regression pinning and anti-drift.** Every failure class fixed by this spec MUST be pinned by an automated test that reproduces the original trigger and goes RED if the fix is reverted. The shared already-merged predicate MUST be consumed by both Requirement 4 sites via the SAME exported symbol, pinned by a test that fails if either site is rewired to a private reimplementation (the 119 AC-12 anti-drift pattern). New mutation/automation points introduced by Requirement 1–3 MUST be classified kill-tested vs documented-forward-safe per ADR-0041 §3, honestly, in the existing fault-injection suites. The Requirement 5 landed-binding write is classified NOW, by this spec: it is **KILL-TESTED** — its failure genuinely terminates the run with a recoverable refusal and suppresses cleanup (R5(b)), so it is never recorded documented-forward-safe; AC-22 is its kill test at both producer legs.

title: impl-approve: auto-open (and optionally auto-merge on green CI) the chore/finalize-* PR on protected main
description:
On protected main, 'mindspec impl approve' cannot push the epic-close .beads/issues.jsonl export directly, so (per wu7t/PR #174) it lands the finalize commit on a chore/finalize-<specID> branch cut from origin/main. Today the operator must MANUALLY open + merge a SECOND PR for that branch (spec 120 needed PR #201 for the spec then PR #202 for the finalize export) — otherwise doctor flags 'finalize branch unmerged' + 'issues.jsonl shows open' and bead/epic state looks stale on main.

IMPROVEMENT: after impl-approve pushes the chore/finalize-<specID> branch, auto-open a PR against main (title/body templated), and — gated on the same 'gh pr checks --watch' green + a config/flag opt-in — optionally auto-merge it, so the operator never hand-opens the finalize PR. Fall back to today's push-branch+NOTE behavior when gh is unavailable / auto-merge is off. Must interop with 3xqm's doctor-surfacing (a still-open finalize branch remains detectable).

Relates: wu7t (closed, designed the chore/finalize mechanism), 3xqm (open, detection/surfacing hardening), o4fd (closed, panel-gate). Context: spec 120 overnight run, 2026-07-19.

Eight two-way `go/ast` scans in `internal/lint` (precedent

3. **(c) Join scan** (`TestJoinWithIDForbidden`): any `filepath.Join`

   `specID`/`beadID`-named identifier fails unless allowlisted-with-gate.

   `budgeter.go:179` specifically GATED per its agent-writable

4. **(e)/(f) Reverse defense-in-depth pair**
   (`TestTrimPrefixReverseDerivationGated`,

   `TrimPrefix` scan and the specs-root/worktrees-root enumeration scan —
   both LABELED defense-in-depth, NO completeness assertion anywhere (the

5. **(g) Whole-tree wrapper-agnostic exec-operand audit**
   (`TestArgvIDOperandGated`): every `bd`/`git` invocation across
   `cmd/`+`internal/` — `bead.RunBD`/`RunBDCombined`/`ListJSON`, the

   `idvalidate` at or before the call; **(ii) AUDITED-ALLOWLISTED —

6. **(h) Raw-ID-render scan** (`TestRawIDRenderForbidden`): any

7. **(d) Template classification**

   `{{.Field}}`/`{{termsafe .Field}}` interpolation in
   `internal/instruct/templates/*.md` classified two-way {spine-gated ID,

   `.SpecGoal` pinned as fenced payload under 116's inherited persuasion
   Non-Goal.

9. **Ownership self-claim**: add `internal/lint/**` to

- [ ] Every negative fixture provably flagged; every

title: [120-trust-boundary-render-audit] Bead 3: worktree_root predicate, symlink containment, check-at-use, shell-safe emitter
description:
R5 — the config path-component gate. `worktree_root` is agent-writable,
NOT ID-derived, and participates in every composed worktree path; it gets
ingress validation, symlink-aware containment with an honestly bounded
TOCTOU residual, check-at-use at the grep-complete use-site inventory, and
one exported shell-safe `cd` emitter that every executable-`cd` render
routes.

**Steps**

1. **Predicate home (OQ1)**: NEW `internal/workspace/containment.go` —
   the `worktree_root` ingress predicate, applied where the default is
   applied (`internal/config/config.go:424-425`): relative (no leading
   `/`), segments in the conservative charset (letters, digits, `.`, `-`,
   `_`; `/` separator), no `..` segment; `filepath.Rel`/lexical checks
   explicitly NAMED lexical-only in the doc comment. Cite ADR-0042 from
   the predicate's doc comment (AC-22 leg) and record the plan-level
   `O_NOFOLLOW` doctrine there (no file-open use exists in today's
   inventory — see the plan preamble).
2. **Symlink-aware containment** in the same home:
   `filepath.EvalSymlinks` on the resolved root AND on the deepest
   EXISTING ancestor of the composed path, which must resolve under the
   resolved root; any symlink component inside the agent-controlled
   suffix ancestry rejected; leaf validated lexically, existing-ancestor
   chain physically (the in-repo precedents: `validate/specid.go:
   SafePath`, `config.CanonicalPath`, the `journal.go:164`
   nearest-existing-ancestor pattern).
3. **Refusal/degrade routing**: lifecycle verbs REFUSE convergently on a
   failing `worktree_root` (lever: ``set worktree_root to .worktrees (the
   default) in .mindspec/config.yaml, then re-run``); never-block
   consumers that swallow config errors into `DefaultConfig()`
   (`guard.go:46-47`) degrade to the default + one escaped warning.
4. **Check-at-use** immediately before each USE of a composed worktree
   path, at the grep-complete inventory (AC-11 pins set-equality):
   worktree-create — `mindspec_executor.go:132` (`WorktreeOps.Create`,
   the primary spec-worktree create), `:227` (bead worktrees, inside
   `withWorkingDir(anchorRoot)`), `:759` (`gitutil.WorktreeAdd`,
   chore/finalize carrier) + its `:756` `MkdirAll`, and the
   `gitutil.WorktreeAdd`/`WorktreeAddDetach` wrappers themselves (the
   wrapper-level check covers any future caller by construction);
   composed-path chdir — `cmd/mindspec/impl.go:66`,
   `cmd/mindspec/complete.go:76`, and the executor
   `withWorkingDir(anchorRoot)` at `:226`; composed worktree-root mkdir —
   `mindspec_executor.go:112/:216`. Root-only chdirs (`impl.go:127`,
   `complete.go:78/:980`, `mindspec_executor.go:93`) are trusted-root,
   excluded. The check-at-use-to-operation window is the accepted
   residual (Non-Goals) — no atomicity claim.
5. **The single shell-safe `cd` emitter**, exported beside the predicate
   (representation per `cmd/mindspec/panel.go:shellQuoteTarget`:
   byte-identical when all bytes are unquoted-safe, else POSIX
   single-quoted). Route every executable-`cd` render: `guard.go:130`
   `CheckCWD`, `mindspec_executor.go:1195/:1221`,
   `complete.FormatResult`, `next/guard.go:DirtyTreeFailure`,
   `cmd/mindspec/next.go:196/:271`, `cmd/mindspec/spec.go:61`,
   `cmd/mindspec/instruct_tail.go:39` + the `run.go` redirect,
   `instruct/worktree.go:33`, `templates/implement.md:41`,
   `cwdsafety.go:emitCdBackNote`, `hook/dispatch.go`. Root-only sinks
   quote-emit and NEVER refuse (round-2 C8).
6. **Tests**: `TestWorktreeRootPredicate` (neg: metacharacter/absolute/
   `..`; the symlinked-ancestor fixture that lexical `Rel` alone would
   pass — the lexical-insufficiency discriminator; each printable-hostile
   value asserted to pass `termsafe.Escape` unchanged — the
   escaping-is-insufficient proof; pos: `.worktrees` and nested clean
   values byte-identical), `TestContainmentCheckAtUse` (composition-time
   pass → ancestor swapped for an outside symlink → check-at-use REFUSES,
   operation never attempted; the `WorktreeOps.Create` subtest pinning
   G3's site; the grep-complete set-equality companion over the pinned
   call-site list), `TestExecutableCdRendersShellSafe` (table-driven over
   the sink set; space-bearing root → quoted + `sh -c` round-trip; clean

   passes; the guard `DefaultConfig`-degrade companion subtest).

**Verification**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/workspace/... ./internal/config/...

title: [120-trust-boundary-render-audit] Bead 2: Composition waist, reverse/consumer gates, explicit-ingress + repair verb
description:

compiles + greens standalone as the waist + all consumer gates; 2b is pure
ingress ergonomics + the repair verb; split trigger — if the session
cannot get 2a compiling + green with context to spare, commit 2a and
dispatch 2b as a follow-on at this documented boundary, no re-plan
needed). This bead owns PRODUCTION packages only — all `internal/harness`
id-gating is Bead 5b's. Moves the hard guarantee to the ten
`workspace` composition helpers, lands the D1/D2 policy points, gates
every reverse-derivation site and all five consumer classes under the
round-9 gate-all-ids rule (NO bd-minted exemption), and adds the explicit
CLI early-gates plus the `mindspec repair spec-title` convergent lever.

**Steps**

*2a — the waist and the consumer gates:*

1. **The waist**: the nine pure composition helpers in
   `internal/workspace/worktree.go:39-99` (`SpecBranch`, `BeadBranch`,

   `idvalidate` and return `(string, error)` (OQ4-a — the `SpecDir`
   SEC-1 precedent, `workspace.go:463-468`; `SpecDir`'s existing contract

   10, SpecWorktreePath 13, BeadWorktreePath 3, FinalizeBranch 2,
   FinalizeWorktreePath 1): ambient callers map the error to their

1. In `internal/idvalidate/ids.go`, correct `specIDPattern` (`:19`) to

design:
## Requirements

1. **Preflight before mutation, modulo the idempotent migration.** Each mutating lifecycle verb (`complete`, `impl approve`, `plan approve`) MUST resolve every immutable gate fact — the bead's parent epic and owning spec, branch existence/ancestry, target-epic child set, plan parse and obligation state — and MUST evaluate every refusal condition derivable from those facts BEFORE its first state mutation (tracker write, branch creation/merge/deletion, commit, or file write). EXEMPT: the one-shot ADR-0034 legacy-to-metadata migration (`complete.go:286-293`, `impl.go:186-192`, `plan.go:70-76`), which is idempotent, already precedes all gates, and may keep running before preflight. A refusal raised in preflight MUST leave tracker and git state byte-identical to the pre-invocation state, modulo that idempotent migration.
2. **Spec resolution from bead lineage.** `complete` MUST resolve the bead's owning spec from the bead's parent epic as the AUTHORITATIVE source, for any invocation cwd inside the repository (a `main` checkout, the bead's own worktree, or a different spec's worktree). Outside-repo cwd behavior is unchanged: `findRoot()` fails before the bead is read (`cmd/mindspec/complete.go:41-44`). An explicit `--spec` hint that RESOLVES to the same spec as the lineage proceeds; a hint that mismatches the lineage MUST refuse in preflight, naming both spec IDs — the hint never silently overrides lineage. Joint from-`main` end-state (with Requirement 3): a `complete` invoked from a `main` checkout acts on the lineage-resolved spec, routes any tracker commit to that spec's branch (or refuses with a named re-invocation command), and leaves `main`'s history untouched.
3. **`complete`'s tracker commits never target protected `main`; staging is pathspec-scoped.** Artifact/tracker auto-commits made by `complete` MUST target the spec branch. When the working checkout is on `main`, `complete` MUST either route the tracker commit to the spec branch or refuse with a named forward-reconciliation command — it MUST NOT create a commit on `main`. EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: the shipped protected-`main` finalize recovery (spec 115 / wu7t, `finalizeOrphanedSpecBranch`, `internal/executor/mindspec_executor.go:602`), which INTENTIONALLY commits the epic-close tracker export on a fresh `chore/finalize-<specID>` branch created from `origin/main` — that carrier is deliberately not-spec-branch (the spec branch is a dead PR carrier in that state) and is consumed as shipped, not re-routed by this requirement. Additionally, `complete`'s artifact auto-commit staging MUST use an explicit pathspec limited to lifecycle artifacts (e.g. `.beads/issues.jsonl`), never an `add -A` equivalent; unexpected dirty paths MUST be surfaced as a warning, not silently swept into the commit.
4. **Merged-unclosed and branch-less reconciliation — skip the plumbing, apply ADR-0037's actual decision.** `complete` MUST detect the merged-but-unclosed state (bead work already an ancestor of the spec branch, bead branch possibly deleted) in preflight and reconcile forward: positively identify the landed merge commit, skip ONLY the merge-base git plumbing that cannot run against a deleted branch (`complete.go:492-495`) and the merge/branch-cleanup legs, and evaluate the doc-sync and ADR-divergence gates against the landed merge commit's content. The ADR-0037 panel gate is evaluated with its decision ladder UNCHANGED and IN FULL: every decision applies on the reconcile path exactly as on the normal path — in particular a registered-but-malformed/unparseable panel STILL Blocks at decision (2) (`internal/panel/gate.go:173-178`) and a round-mismatched registered panel STILL Blocks at decision (4) (`gate.go:200-205`), because those decisions PRECEDE the missing-ref check; a deleted ref does not short-circuit them. Decision (5), MissingRef → Allow + Warn (`gate.go:139`, `:208-218`), applies specifically to a READABLE, NON-ABANDONED, ROUND-CONSISTENT registered panel whose `bead/<id>` ref is genuinely deleted — the state the merged-unclosed reconcile inherently presents for a well-formed registration — and there the reconcile path MUST surface the rerun-after-merge warning and MUST NOT fabricate a panel Block the ladder does not produce; the ladder's own earlier Blocks, (2) and (4), remain in force. §6's registered-panels-only fail-open scope is likewise preserved (`ADR-0037-panel-gate-enforced-contract.md:56-59`; `panel_advisory.go:176-177` returns no gate when no panel is registered): a panel-free bead completes through the reconcile path exactly as it would through the normal path, with no panel warning at all. No ADR-0037 amendment is made or required. The anti-bypass property is carried by two mandatory legs OUTSIDE the panel decision: (a) POSITIVE landed-merge evidence — the reconcile path MUST record durable evidence identifying the landed merge commit it reconciled against, and MUST refuse (not close) when no landed merge commit can be positively identified (bead open, work NOT merged, branch deleted → refusal, not close); and (b) the doc-sync and ADR-divergence gates evaluated against the landed content — an unsatisfied gate there refuses, naming the failing gate, not a close. The same skip-legs path MUST reconcile an already-closed, branch-less bead carrying an unsettled `refutation_pending_entries` obligation (reaching `reconcilePendingRefutations`) without requiring manual branch-ref restoration. The stronger fail-closed variant — refusing when a REGISTERED panel's gate facts are unsatisfied in the deleted-ref state — is a NAMED FOLLOWUP (see Out of Scope): it requires an ADR-0037 decision-5 amendment plus a reconstructed landed-bead-tip staleness target, and no criterion in this spec compares `reviewed_head_sha` to the merge commit (a non-fast-forward merge commit's SHA differs from the bead tip, so that comparison would false-stale a normally-reviewed bead).
5. **Doctor stale-OPEN cross-check — landed work, not mere ancestry.** `doctor` MUST gain a NEW check — the inverse of the shipped `checkOrphanedBeads` — flagging a bead that (a) is OPEN or in_progress in the tracker, (b) whose `bead/<id>` branch carries at least ONE commit beyond its fork point from the spec branch (the bead did work), and (c) all of that work is an ancestor of the spec branch (the work landed) — reporting `Status=Error` with the recovery command `mindspec complete <id>`, and reporting healthy when tracker and git agree. Mere ancestry is NOT sufficient to flag: bead branches fork AT the spec tip (`DispatchBead` creates the branch from the spec branch), so a freshly-claimed bead branch with ZERO commits beyond its fork point is trivially an ancestor of the spec branch and MUST NOT be flagged — otherwise every in-progress bead would fail the CI doctor run (Requirement 7). The git mechanism for computing the fork point after the work has merged (plain `merge-base` collapses to the bead tip once it is an ancestor — e.g. `merge-base --fork-point`/reflog, the recorded creation base, or first-parent-history exclusion) is a plan-level choice; the observable contract is fixed by AC-10's positive and negative fixtures.
6. **Lifecycle-scoped finalization, BOTH enumerations, fail-closed.** `FinalizeEpic` enumerates `bead/`-prefixed worktree branches in TWO independent legs: the auto-merge leg (`mindspec_executor.go:383-386`) and the lingering-worktree/branch CLEANUP leg (`mindspec_executor.go:526-534`, which removes the worktree and deletes the branch for every `bead/`-prefixed entry). The allow-set for BOTH enumerations MUST be the finalizing spec's PLAN-DECLARED LIFECYCLE BEADS — the task-type children in the plan's bead set, per the explicit lifecycle classification phase derivation already uses (`internal/phase/derive.go` `classifyChild`: only `task` and empty/unknown issue types are lifecycle; `bug` and every other explicit non-`task`, non-`epic` type is a non-lifecycle follow-up) — with `parent == finalizing epic` as a NECESSARY cross-check but NOT the sole selector. Parent-only scoping is insufficient: spec 095 deliberately permits an OPEN non-lifecycle follow-up child (e.g. a `bug`) to remain attached to the epic through impl approve (`internal/approve/impl.go:240-263`, advisory-only, never blocking), so a same-epic child can hold a live worktree and branch while sitting OUTSIDE the lifecycle. Neither leg may merge, worktree-remove, or branch-delete (i) a bead of a DIFFERENT epic or (ii) a NON-LIFECYCLE child of the finalizing epic itself — open or closed; the exclusion boundary is lifecycle identity, not open-status or worktree presence. Enumeration and classification failures MUST be fail-closed: an error listing worktrees, resolving a candidate's epic membership, or resolving its lifecycle classification aborts the finalize with a named error rather than silently skipping the leg or silently admitting the candidate.
7. **Finalize-orphan surfacing, CI wiring, and remote-ref hardening.** `doctor` (and the corresponding `instruct` guidance, generated from the same check) MUST detect and report (a) an outstanding unmerged `chore/finalize-*` branch and (b) stale committed tracker state on `main` left by an interrupted finalize. Orphan-case `CommitCount`/`DiffStat` MUST be computed against `origin/main`, not possibly-stale local `main` (`mindspec_executor.go:433-437`). `gitutil.RemoteHeadSHA` MUST match the exact refname on the `ls-remote` refname column (a decoy ref such as `refs/heads/aaa/chore/finalize-105` MUST NOT match `chore/finalize-105`), and the `PushBranchForceWithLease` doc comment MUST be corrected: the read-then-lease pattern protects only against races between the `RemoteHeadSHA` read and the push — it overwrites whatever tip was observed, so "never silently clobbered" overstates the guarantee. Finally, CI MUST run `mindspec doctor` so that its non-zero exit fails the build — wiring the shipped orphan checks and the new checks into `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (today no workflow invokes doctor).
8. **Narrow the vestigial refusal — preserve the retention.** The now-unreachable refusal DISJUNCTION inside `impl approve`'s pre-finalize check (`impl.go:440-445`: `count == 0 && (planErr != nil || len(beadIDs) == 0)`, unreachable past spec 115's Leg 3 gate) MUST be removed. The `exec.CommitCount` CALL and its consensus-revision-9 position between the phase-metadata write and `FinalizeEpic` MUST be PRESERVED, with `TestApproveImplCallOrder` continuing to pin that order — the call is a documented retention, not dead code. A test MUST continue to pin that a missing/empty plan is refused pre-mutation by the Leg 3 orphan-obligation gate.
9. **The scaffold emits structured dependencies — no prose parser; wiring gaps are loud.** The plan scaffold emitted at spec approve (`internal/approve/spec.go` `scaffoldPlan`) MUST emit a `work_chunks` frontmatter block with per-chunk `id` and `depends_on` fields (matching the shape `internal/validate/plan.go`'s `WorkChunk` parses), so that an author who fills the scaffold as given gets dependency edges wired by the SHIPPED `work_chunks[].depends_on` path (`plan.go:354-373`, spec 097 R3). The per-bead prose `**Depends on**` section is KEPT in the scaffold — the plan validator's `bead-depends` check (`internal/validate/plan.go:841-842`) warns on any bead section lacking a "Depends on" declaration, so removing it would make every filled-as-given scaffold warn — but the scaffold MUST label it as human-readable documentation that is never parsed; `work_chunks[].depends_on` is the SOLE wired source of truth. No prose dependency parsing may be introduced — it would reverse 097 R3 and create dual conflicting sources of truth. Two silent fail-opens MUST become visible warnings: (a) `plan approve` on a plan with NO `work_chunks` frontmatter MUST emit a warning naming the absence (edges cannot be wired), with approve behavior otherwise unchanged for legacy plans; and (b) the shipped edge wiring is best-effort (`internal/approve/plan.go:368-370` `continue`s on a `bd dep add` error with no output) — a failed `bd dep add` invocation MUST emit a warning naming the unwired edge (both bead IDs), with approve still proceeding (best-effort behavior otherwise preserved).
10. **Validator-complete scaffolds.** The plan scaffold MUST include every section the plan validator hard-requires — in particular a per-bead `**Acceptance Criteria**` section (`bead-acceptance-criteria`, `internal/validate/plan.go:838`) — and a "templates round-trip through their own validators" test MUST pin, for BOTH the plan scaffold and the spec scaffold, that the emitted template, minimally filled, passes its own validator. The plan-scaffold round-trip MUST additionally pin that the filled scaffold's `work_chunks` produce wired dependency edges (coupling to Requirement 9).

New path/ID-bearing warning output introduced by this spec MUST be routed through spec 116's `internal/termsafe` escaping. The jli8 per-path ownership-RECORDING leg is OPTIONAL and out of scope (see Scope).
12. **Hermetic test isolation.** `setupRunTestProject` (`internal/instruct/run_test.go` — the only definition; there is no `internal/harness` twin) MUST be hermetic: phase/git resolution from within the test sandbox MUST NOT escape to an enclosing real worktree — via `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, a real `git init` in the temp dir, or an explicit root override honored by `phase.ResolveContextFromDirWithCache`. `go test ./...` (harness excluded per existing convention) MUST pass when run from inside an active-spec worktree whose enclosing repo is mid-lifecycle.
13. **Fault-injection regression coverage; doctor shares the verbs' predicates.** Every failure class fixed by this spec MUST be pinned by an automated regression test that reproduces the original trigger and goes RED if the fix is reverted.
