title: [106-layout-flatten] Bead 2: Phase 1 — diff-string layout classifier, permanently multi-prefix gate matchers (ADDITIVE reviews), tier-aware enumerating consumers (Reqs 3, 6, 14)
description:
**Scope:** The git-DIFF-STRING classifiers and every root-enumerating consumer.
Lands fully green against the EXISTING two forms while ALREADY recognizing the flat
prefix (the panel R3 constraint). ZERO layout change on disk.

**Changed files:** `internal/validate/docsync.go`, `internal/validate/divergence.go`,
`internal/validate/ownership.go`, `internal/contextpack/budgeter.go`,
`internal/spec/list.go`, `internal/domain/list.go`, `internal/domain/show.go`,
`internal/doctor/docs.go`, with `*_test.go`.

**Steps**
1. Introduce a relative-path layout-classifier predicate and make EVERY git-ref
   matcher recognize all three prefixes (flat + canonical + legacy):
   `isDocFile`/`isSourceFile` (docsync.go:330/338), the
   `.mindspec/docs/specs/<id>/` literals in `validateSpecArtifactSync`/`specMDID`
   (docsync.go:561-622), the domain-doc prefixes in `checkInternalPackages`
   (docsync.go:485-488), the cmd-docs accept-set (docsync.go:534-538),
   `listDomainDirs`/`TreeDirsAtRef(".mindspec/docs/domains")` (docsync.go:352,
   ownership.go:198), `LoadOwnership`'s manifest path (ownership.go:79), and
   `isProcessArtifact` (divergence.go:277-281).
2. **CRITICAL:** make the ref-anchored ownership pair `LoadOwnershipAtRef`
   (ownership.go:150) + `domainManifestRelPath` (ownership.go:123-125) multi-prefix
   too. The `complete` ADR-divergence gate loads ownership through THIS pair, not
   `LoadOwnership` at :79; missing it leaves every flat-tree domain manifest reading
   "missing" and hard-blocks EVERY 106 bead on `adr-divergence-unowned`. Pin a
   flat-tree `LoadOwnershipAtRef` test that returns the domain's claims.
3. **Reviews exclusion is ADDITIVE, never a destructive REPLACE (R5 blocker 3).**
   `isProcessArtifact` (divergence.go:277-281) today excludes
   `strings.HasPrefix(path, "review/")`. KEEP that root `review/**` exclusion as a
   PERMANENT historical-ref compatibility matcher — analogous to the permanently
   multi-prefix doc/ownership matchers, and decoupled from the read-tier deprecation
   lifecycle (historical refs, old branches, and external forks never stop emitting
   the root `review/` path). ADD, alongside it, a NEW `/reviews/`-segment exclusion
   that classifies `<spec-dir>/reviews/<slug>/...` non-source (note: the literal
   `review/` does NOT substring-match `reviews/`, so the two are independent
   matchers). BOTH must classify non-source so that, during the transition (root
   `review/**` still live until Bead 5 migrates it, co-located `<spec-dir>/reviews/**`
   appearing after), neither reads as source/unowned and trips a gate. Mirror the
   same additive posture wherever doc-sync references `review/`.
4. Classify `project-docs/**` as NON-SOURCE docs in the predicate (Req 14) so
   dogfood eviction trips neither `adr-divergence-unowned` nor the doc-sync source
   lane; make the cmd-docs accept-set accept the post-flatten `core/USAGE.md` and the
   evicted `project-docs/user/**`.
5. Make `internal/contextpack/budgeter.go` consume the Bead-1 per-artifact accessors
   instead of the hardcoded `.mindspec/docs/specs/<id>` (budgeter.go:170) and
   `.mindspec/docs/domains/<d>/<kind>` (budgeter.go:218) joins, so a context pack
   assembles byte-identically — same sections, same bytes — on a flat vs canonical
   vs legacy project (no silent spec/domain drop).
6. Make EVERY other root-enumerating `DocsDir` consumer tier-aware via the Bead-1
   accessors: `mindspec spec list` (`internal/spec/list.go:22`, joins
   `workspace.DocsDir`+"specs"), `mindspec domain list`/`show`
   (`internal/domain/list.go:102`, `internal/domain/show.go:32,74`), context-map
   enrichment, the `core/` doc paths, and the doctor orphan/docs scans
   (`internal/doctor/docs.go` — `checkDocs`/`checkDomains`/`checkStaleFocusLifecycle`/
   `docsRootRel`, all via `workspace.DocsDir`).
7. Add the three-prefix equivalence tests, the flat-tree ref-anchored-ownership
   test, the ADDITIVE reviews test (root `review/<slug>/...` AND
   `<spec-dir>/reviews/<slug>/...` both non-source), the `project-docs/**`
   classification test, the context-pack flat-vs-canonical byte-identity test, and
   command-level flat-fixture tests for the enumerating consumers (spec list, domain
   list/show, doctor scans).

**Verification**
- [ ] `go test ./internal/validate/... ./internal/contextpack/... ./internal/spec/... ./internal/domain/... ./internal/doctor/...` PASS (NEVER `./internal/harness/...`)
- [ ] A legacy-, canonical-, and flat-prefix diff classify identically across doc-sync / ownership / divergence; `project-docs/foo.md` is neither source nor `adr-divergence-unowned` (AC11)
- [ ] `isProcessArtifact` classifies BOTH a root `review/<slug>/...` path (permanent historical matcher) AND a `<spec-dir>/reviews/<slug>/...` path (new segment matcher) as non-source (AC11)
- [ ] A flat-tree `LoadOwnershipAtRef` returns the domain's claims (not "missing") so beads do not hard-block `adr-divergence-unowned` (AC11)
- [ ] The context-pack builder yields byte-identical sections on flat vs an otherwise-identical canonical fixture (AC6); spec-list/domain-list/doctor scans return the same inventory on a flat fixture (AC5)
- [ ] `project-docs/**` is classified non-source docs by the predicate (AC21 classification half)

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] Doc-sync, ownership (incl. the ref-anchored `LoadOwnershipAtRef`/`domainManifestRelPath` pair), and divergence classify flat/canonical/legacy diff paths identically, keep the permanent root `review/**` exclusion AND add the `<spec-dir>/reviews/` exclusion, and treat `project-docs/**` as non-source docs (AC11); enumerating consumers resolve on flat fixtures (AC5); context packs assemble byte-identically flat vs canonical (AC6).

**Depends on**
Bead 1 (the budgeter and the enumerating consumers CONSUME Bead 1's per-artifact
accessors; the diff-string matcher portion is independent but ships in the same
bead).
design:
## Requirements

1. **Per-artifact three-tier resolver; non-breaking reads.** Add a FLAT tier to every artifact accessor in `internal/workspace`, ordered FIRST in resolution PRECEDENCE (first-exists-wins): flat (`.mindspec/specs/<id>`, `.mindspec/adr/`, `.mindspec/domains/<d>`, `.mindspec/context-map.md`, `.mindspec/core/`) → canonical (`.mindspec/docs/…`) → legacy (`docs/…`). "FIRST" here is read-order precedence, NOT delivery order: the flat directories do not physically exist until the Phase-3 moves, so a Phase-1 tree (canonical or legacy) resolves exactly as it does today. The single `DocsDir` join-point (workspace.go:116) that today funnels `ADRDir` (workspace.go:188), `DomainDir` (workspace.go:235), and `ContextMapPath` (workspace.go:178) MUST dissolve into per-artifact resolvers; `SpecDir` (workspace.go:153) gains the flat tier alongside its existing worktree/canonical/legacy tiers. Reading an existing canonical OR legacy project MUST stay byte-for-byte non-breaking — a project with no flat tree resolves exactly as it does today.

2. **Whole-tree `DetectLayout(root) → {flat | canonical | legacy | greenfield | mixed}`, computed once, drives the write-default.** `DetectLayout` MUST distinguish the two non-flat WRITE shapes — `canonical` (a `.mindspec/docs/…` lifecycle tree exists) and `legacy` (a root `docs/…` lifecycle tree exists) — because they are DISTINCT write targets, not one "legacy" bucket; collapsing them cannot drive the never-split write-default for a canonical-only vs a legacy-only project. The write-side "born flat" decision MUST key off this WHOLE-TREE classification ("no canonical/legacy lifecycle tree exists ANYWHERE under root"), never a per-ID existence probe — a per-ID probe cannot distinguish a greenfield project from a brand-new spec inside an existing legacy project, so it would split a project's layout. `greenfield` and post-migration `flat` projects write flat; a `canonical` or `legacy` project keeps writing to its existing form until migrated. `mixed` — ANY flat lifecycle tree coexisting with ANY canonical/legacy lifecycle tree (whether different spec ids OR different artifact classes, e.g. a flat `specs/` beside a canonical `adr/`) — is a HARD ERROR: first-exists-wins reads would mask the residue while writes go flat, reintroducing the exact half-old/half-flat split the panel rejected. The ONLY exception is a recorded in-progress migration recovery (a live `.mindspec/migrations/<run-id>/` run-state, Req 4), where a transient mixed tree is expected and the recovery path — not first-exists-wins — drives resolution. `mindspec init`/`bootstrap` create the flat directories for new projects (replacing the bootstrap.go:222-223 `.mindspec/docs/{domains,specs}` manifest entries).

3. **All root-enumerating `DocsDir` consumers become layout-tier-aware (incl. the context-pack budgeter).** Beyond the named accessors (Req 1), EVERY consumer that joins onto the `DocsDir` root or enumerates under it MUST resolve through a layout-aware accessor, or it silently reads an empty flat tree: `mindspec spec list`, `mindspec domain list`/`show`, context-map enrichment, the authored `core/` doc paths, and the doctor orphan/docs scans (`internal/doctor/docs.go`, also Req 9). In particular `internal/contextpack/budgeter.go` hardcodes `.mindspec/docs/specs/<id>` (budgeter.go:170) and `.mindspec/docs/domains/<d>/<kind>` (budgeter.go:218); on a flat project it feeds those joins empty directories and SILENTLY drops the spec + domain context from the assembled pack. The budgeter MUST consume the per-artifact accessors so a context pack assembles identically — same sections, same bytes — on a flat vs canonical vs legacy project.

4. **Net-new deterministic, transactional, idempotent mover with a DEFINED run-state machine + rollback semantics.** Build a history-preserving git-mv driver (routed through `internal/executor` per ADR-0030, not direct shell-out) that is idempotent (re-running on an already-flat tree is a no-op) and lands each artifact-group move as TWO commits: a pure 100%-similarity `git mv` first, then the link-rewrite (Req 5) second — so `git log --follow` and 3-way-merge rename detection stay reliable. It writes a lineage manifest under `.mindspec/lineage/` and a per-run state record under `.mindspec/migrations/<run-id>/` consistent with the existing doctor migration-metadata schema (`internal/doctor/migration.go`).
   **Run-state machine + crash recovery (DEFINED, not merely named).** The run records an ordered, durable checkpoint at every mutation boundary: (a) pre-run base ref captured; then for EACH artifact group — (b) before the `git mv`, (c) after the `git mv` / before the pure-move commit, (d) after the pure-move commit, (e) after the link-rewrite, (f) after the rewrite commit; then (g) the lineage/state finalize. Required RESUME behavior after a crash: the resumer reads the last durable checkpoint and — at (b)/(c) discards or re-stages the working-tree-only partial `git mv` (nothing is committed yet) and retries the group; at (d)/(f) detects the commit already landed and SKIPS it (idempotent); at (e) re-runs the deterministic link-rewrite (a pure function of the moved tree) and commits. **Rollback semantics (CHOSEN, in git terms): hard-reset-to-pre-run-ref while nothing is published.** On any failure or `--abort` BEFORE the run's commits are pushed/merged, the mover hard-resets the branch to the (a) pre-run ref and cleans the working tree — NO compensating revert commits. AFTER the run's commits are published, the mover REFUSES to auto-rollback and instead emits the forward-only recovery line (re-migrate / rebase), consistent with ADR-0023.

5. **Net-new finite-pattern markdown link-rewriter, gated by a doctor link-existence check that scans EVERY link.** Rewrite ONLY the closed, breaking subset of relative links — NOT a general markdown parser. Because the flatten is SYMMETRIC (specs and adr both shed the same `docs/` level), spec→ADR links like `../../adr/ADR-NNNN.md` are PRESERVED unchanged; the breaking set is small and enumerable: one-level `../adr/` cases, absolute `docs/core/` and `.mindspec/docs/core/`/context-map references, review-co-location links whose relative depth changed under the `<spec-dir>/reviews/` move, dogfood cross-links whose depth changed under eviction, and repo-root `README.md`/`AGENTS.md` references that point INTO the moved trees from OUTSIDE them. The GATING doctor link-existence check MUST scan EVERY markdown link in the post-migration moved tree AND the affected root docs — NOT merely the finite set the rewriter touched — and FAIL the migration (and the run-state machine, Req 4) if ANY link 404s, so a breaking link the finite rewriter failed to anticipate is caught at the gate rather than shipped.

6. **Gate matchers are git-DIFF-string classifiers, permanently multi-prefix.** The doc-sync, ownership, and ADR-divergence lanes match diff PATH STRINGS, not filesystem reads, so the accessors cannot absorb them. Introduce a relative-path layout-classifier predicate and make every git-ref matcher recognize ALL THREE prefixes (flat + canonical + legacy): `isDocFile`/`isSourceFile` (docsync.go:330/338), the `.mindspec/docs/specs/<id>/` literals in `validateSpecArtifactSync`/`specMDID` (docsync.go:561-622), the domain-doc prefixes in `checkInternalPackages` (docsync.go:485-488), the cmd-docs accept-set (docsync.go:534-538), `listDomainDirs`/`TreeDirsAtRef(".mindspec/docs/domains")` (docsync.go:352, ownership.go:198), `LoadOwnership`'s manifest path (ownership.go:79), AND — CRITICALLY — the ref-anchored ownership pair `LoadOwnershipAtRef` (ownership.go:150) + `domainManifestRelPath` (ownership.go:123-125), plus `isProcessArtifact` (divergence.go:277-281). The `complete` ADR-divergence gate loads ownership through the ref-anchored `LoadOwnershipAtRef`/`domainManifestRelPath` pair (NOT `LoadOwnership` at :79); updating only :79 leaves every domain manifest reading "missing" on a flat tree, so every 106 bead would hard-block `adr-divergence-unowned`. This multi-prefix posture is PERMANENT and DECOUPLED from the resolver-tier lifecycle: historical refs, old branches, and external forks never stop emitting legacy paths, so a "drop legacy tiers after N releases" deprecation applies ONLY to filesystem reads (Req 1), NEVER to git-ref matchers. The predicate MUST also classify `project-docs/**` as non-source docs (Req 14) so dogfood eviction does not trip `adr-divergence-unowned` or the doc-sync source lane; the cmd-docs accept-set must accept the post-flatten `core/USAGE.md` and the evicted `project-docs/user/**`.

7. **Worktree-aware fixes + regression tests.** `SpecDir`'s worktree tier must additionally probe the flat worktree shape (`.worktrees/worktree-spec-<id>/.mindspec/specs/<id>`). `TreeRootForSpecDir` (workspace.go:206-222) must recognize the flat `.mindspec/specs/<id>` shape — its current `filepath.Base(docs) != "docs"` assertion (workspace.go:214) returns `""` for a flat dir and would regress the mindspec-ew79 cross-worktree ADR-visibility fix. `guard.go` worktree-add recipes must be layout-aware. Regression tests MUST pin both worktree shapes.

8. **Reviews co-location wiring.** `internal/panel.Scan` and `PanelDirScanRoot` (panel.go:118-142, gate.go:420-422) move from the repo-root `review/*/panel.json` glob to the spec-scoped `<spec-dir>/reviews/*/panel.json` glob (a sibling of `RecordingDir`, workspace.go:244-250); the `mindspec complete` panel-gate scan becomes spec-scoped instead of repo-root. `divergence.go`'s `HasPrefix(path,"review/")` exclusion (divergence.go:280) becomes a `/reviews/`-segment exclusion under spec dirs. Update the `ms-panel-run` + `ms-panel-tally` skill bodies, their `historical_skills` snapshots (`internal/setup/skills.go`), and amend ADR-0037 for the new `panel.json` location. Reviews are TRACKED (durable audit, travel with the spec); the root `review/` tree is eliminated, resolving **adwu**.

9. **Doctor: real layout detection + dual-layout duplicate-ID error.** `mindspec doctor` MUST gain a real layout detector (reusing `DetectLayout`), a `would-migrate-layout` Warn (analogous to the existing `would-migrate: spec=…` Warn, migration.go:101-106), and an ERROR when the SAME spec id exists under two layouts simultaneously (kills the stale-duplicate read hazard the first-exists-wins resolver would otherwise mask). `checkDryRunMigration` (migration.go:39) and the orphan/docs scans (docs.go via `workspace.DocsDir`) must become tier-aware rather than hardcoded to `.mindspec/docs/specs`.

10. **Merge-time layout-fingerprint HARD-FAIL.** `internal/complete` `MergeBranch` (and any spec→main / bead→spec merge) MUST compute a layout fingerprint of source and target and HARD-FAIL a cross-layout merge (nested source onto flat target, or vice versa) with a "rebase onto post-flatten main" recovery line, instead of trusting git's heuristic rename / directory-rename detection. This makes the pre-flatten drain enforced, not advisory (ADR-0023 forward-only).

11. **`migrate layout` precondition: a feasible, testable pre-flatten branch/PR discovery algorithm.** The flatten command's precondition is the absence of any unmerged BRANCH or PR that predates the flatten — NOT "zero worktrees" (unreachable in this repo, and mis-attributed to impl-approve). DISCOVERY ALGORITHM (deterministic source-of-truth): scan (1) local branch refs, (2) remote-tracking refs (`refs/remotes/<remote>/*`), and (3) hosted PR metadata when a remote + token are available; compute a flatten base/fingerprint from the post-flatten layout SIGNATURE (does the ref's merge-base tree still carry the canonical/legacy `.mindspec/docs/` lifecycle layout, vs the flat shape?). A ref BLOCKS the migration iff it is unmerged into the target AND its fingerprint is pre-flatten. OFFLINE / no-remote behavior: the scan degrades to local + remote-tracking refs only and WARNS that hosted PRs could not be consulted (it does NOT silently pass). The command MUST require a clean idle working tree before mutating. Locked agent worktrees and long-lived external forks are explicitly TOLERATED — they cannot be drained, only fingerprint-guarded at merge (Req 10) — so the precondition MUST NOT count them as blockers.

12. **Skills + snapshots correctness on flat projects.** `ms-spec-grill`'s SKILL.md reads the domain set from `.mindspec/docs/domains/` (SKILL.md:30/38/40) and computes the next ADR number by scanning `.mindspec/docs/adr/` (SKILL.md:31); on a flat project these read empty dirs and mis-fire (reject-invented-domains and next-ADR-number both break) — this is the CENTRAL correctness claim of this requirement, so the skill MUST read the layout-correct path. Also update the `lifecycleSkillFiles` literals, the `setup/claude.go` and `setup/codex.go` generated text, the other path-bearing skill bodies (ms-panel-run/tally, ms-bead-impl/cycle/fix, ms-spec-final-review) and plugin README/FINDINGS + bootstrap text, and EVERY path-bearing `historical_skills` snapshot in `internal/setup/skills.go`. The plan MUST either update each path-bearing artifact or explicitly classify it out of scope with a recorded reason.

13. **The moves + the drops.** Flatten `specs/`, `adr/`, `domains/`, and `core/` to top-level `.mindspec/` children; move `context-map.md` to `.mindspec/context-map.md`. KEEP the name `adr` (load-bearing across `ADRDir`, `ADR-NNNN` filenames, `mindspec adr`, and ~150+ inbound links) and KEEP the name `core` (do NOT rename to `reference/` in this spec). Evict dogfood docs (`user/`, `installation/`, `research/`) to top-level `project-docs/`. CRITICAL: the evicted tree MUST NOT be named `docs/` — `workspace.DocsDir` falls back to `LegacyDocsDir = root/docs` (workspace.go:121,130), so a top-level `docs/` would alias the live legacy resolver tier and make `ADRDir`/`DomainDir`/`ContextMapPath` silently resolve INTO the evicted tree. When `domains/` flattens, each domain's OWNERSHIP.yaml that self-claims `.mindspec/docs/domains/<d>/OWNERSHIP.yaml` MUST have that self-glob updated to the flat `.mindspec/domains/<d>/OWNERSHIP.yaml` — non-blocking (doc files, not gate matchers) but a latent staleness that must not be left behind. Drop `glossary.md` (`.mindspec/docs/glossary.md`), `policies.yml` (`.mindspec/policies.yml`), and the stale `internal/instruct/templates/spec.md:35` glossary line, ADR-0018-consistent, with no dangling references left.

14. **Ownership + classification deliverables.** Any net-new mover package (e.g. `internal/layout/**`) MUST be added to the workflow `OWNERSHIP.yaml` so it is owned and does not trip `adr-divergence-unowned` at complete. `project-docs/**` MUST be classified as non-source docs by the Req 6 predicate (it is dogfood reference, not governable source) so its tracked move is neither flagged unowned nor mis-classified as a source change requiring doc-sync. No `bench/**`, `viz/**`, or `agentmind/**` glob may be added (excluded first-segments; a hard `LoadOwnership` schema error, ownership.go:60).

15. **Test/fixture migration is first-class and budgeted.** ~99 exact-slash-form `.mindspec/docs/{specs,adr,domains,core}` occurrences across 21 non-test Go files (~110 once the `filepath.Join` forms are counted) plus the harness scenario files and testdata fixtures encode the physical layout. The plan MUST budget fixture migration explicitly and add a flat-layout test matrix so the resolvers, classifier predicate, mover, panel scan, doctor detector, AND the context-pack builder (Req 3) are all exercised on flat AND canonical/legacy trees. Phase 1 MUST land fully green with ZERO layout change (revertible), proving the refactor is behavior-preserving before any file moves.

16. **Amend `DOCS-LAYOUT.md` to the flat layout.** `.mindspec/docs/core/DOCS-LAYOUT.md` (which itself flattens to `.mindspec/core/DOCS-LAYOUT.md`) documents the current `.mindspec/docs/` layout and is an in-this-spec deliverable (Background, Scope). Like the ADR-0037 amendment (Req 8) it MUST be GOVERNED, not left implicit: amend it to describe the flat `.mindspec/{specs,adr,domains,core}` + `project-docs/` layout, the per-artifact three-tier read order, and the reviews co-location, so the authored reference does not contradict the shipped tree.

17. **Reconcile the `cmd/mindspec/migrate.go` prompt rubric with the flat target.** The legacy `mindspec migrate` prompt EMITTER's classification rubric still routes user docs to `.mindspec/docs/user/` and agent files to `.mindspec/docs/agent/` (migrate.go:286-287) and presents `.mindspec/docs/` as the canonical destination (migrate.go:264-298). It MUST be reconciled with this spec's targets: dogfood/user docs route to top-level `project-docs/`, and lifecycle/authored artifacts to the flat `.mindspec/{specs,adr,domains,core}` children — so the prompt emitter and the deterministic `migrate layout` mover agree on the destination shape instead of emitting prompts that would re-create the evicted `.mindspec/docs/user/`/`…/agent/` trees.

## ADR Decisions

Cited by ID — full text under `.mindspec/docs/adr/`:

- see ADR-0037 — Panel Gate as Enforced Contract — panel.json Convention, Thresholds, and the Trust Boundary
- see ADR-0018 — Lean Bootstrap — Remove Glossary and Policies Subsystems
- see ADR-0023 — Eliminate Focus and Lifecycle Files — Beads as Single State Authority
- see ADR-0025 — `.beads/issues.jsonl` Is a Build Artifact, Not User Authorship

title: [106-layout-flatten] Bead 1: Phase 1 — per-artifact three-tier resolvers, `DetectLayout`, shared layout-signature helper, flat worktree tier, born-flat bootstrap (Reqs 1, 2, 7, 15)
description:
**Scope:** The HEART of the refactor, entirely in `internal/workspace` plus the
`internal/bootstrap` greenfield manifest. ZERO layout change on disk: the flat
directories do not exist yet, so a canonical/legacy tree resolves exactly as today.

**Changed files:** `internal/workspace/workspace.go`, `internal/workspace/worktree.go`,
`internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go`, plus `*_test.go` for the resolver matrix.

**Steps**
1. Dissolve the single `DocsDir` join-point (workspace.go:116) into PER-ARTIFACT
   three-tier resolvers ordered flat → canonical → legacy, first-exists-wins:
   `SpecDir` (gain the flat `.mindspec/specs/<id>` tier alongside its existing
   worktree/canonical/legacy tiers), `ADRDir` (`.mindspec/adr/`), `DomainDir`
   (`.mindspec/domains/<d>`), `ContextMapPath` (`.mindspec/context-map.md`),
   `RecordingDir`, and a new `CoreDir` (`.mindspec/core/`). "Flat FIRST" is
   READ-PRECEDENCE, not delivery order — with no flat tree present the resolver
   returns the canonical/legacy path byte-for-byte as today.
2. Add `DetectLayout(root) → {flat | canonical | legacy | greenfield | mixed}` as a
   WHOLE-TREE probe. Distinguish `canonical` (a `.mindspec/docs/…` lifecycle tree)
   from `legacy` (a root `docs/…` tree) as DISTINCT write targets. `mixed` (ANY flat
   lifecycle tree coexisting with ANY canonical/legacy tree, across spec ids OR
   artifact classes) is a HARD ERROR, with the SOLE exception of a recorded
   in-progress `.mindspec/migrations/<run-id>/` recovery. The write-default keys off
   this whole-tree classification ("no canonical/legacy lifecycle tree exists
   ANYWHERE under root" → born flat), never a per-ID probe.
3. **Extract the shared layout-signature helper (minor 12).** Factor the pure
   tree-shape classification — given the set of present `.mindspec` lifecycle child
   names (or the presence of `.mindspec/docs/` vs the flat `.mindspec/{specs,adr,
   domains,core}` children), return the layout kind — into a small PURE function in
   `internal/workspace` (the sibling of `DetectLayout`, which consumes it for the
   filesystem probe). It takes pre-listed directory entries, so it does NO git or
   filesystem I/O itself and has no cycle risk. The Bead-4 merge guard (in
   `internal/executor`, which already imports `internal/workspace`) consumes THIS
   helper to fingerprint source/target trees from `executor.TreeDirsAtRef` output —
   one source of truth for the signature. (The Bead-3 mover keeps a thin local
   pre/post-flatten ref-shape probe of its own to preserve its captured-fixture
   golden-test independence — the small, intentional residual duplication is recorded
   here; a follow-up may converge the mover onto the same helper once the layout cut
   has landed and Bead 3's independence is no longer load-bearing.)
4. Make `SpecDir`'s worktree tier additionally probe the flat worktree shape
   (`.worktrees/worktree-spec-<id>/.mindspec/specs/<id>`), and make
   `TreeRootForSpecDir` (workspace.go:206-222) recognize the flat
   `.mindspec/specs/<id>` shape — its current `filepath.Base(docs) != "docs"`
   assertion (:214) returns `""` for a flat dir and would regress the mindspec-ew79
   cross-worktree ADR-visibility fix. Make the worktree-add recipes in
   `internal/workspace/worktree.go` layout-aware.
5. Replace the bootstrap greenfield manifest (`bootstrap.go:222-223`,
   `.mindspec/docs/{domains,specs}`) with the flat `.mindspec/{specs,domains}`
   (and any other born-flat dirs), so `mindspec init`/`bootstrap` creates a flat
   tree that `DetectLayout` classifies `flat`.
6. Add the resolver matrix test (canonical / legacy / flat fixtures), the
   `DetectLayout` five-state test (incl. `mixed`-hard-error and the
   new-id-in-legacy → `legacy` non-split case and the recorded-recovery exception),
   the signature-helper unit test, both worktree shapes, the `TreeRootForSpecDir`
   flat ew79 regression, and the bootstrap born-flat assertion. The fixtures carry no
   flat tree for the non-breaking cases (AC1) and a full flat tree for the flat cases
   (AC2).

**Verification**
- [ ] `go test ./internal/workspace/... ./internal/bootstrap/...` PASS (NEVER `./internal/harness/...`)
- [ ] Resolver matrix: canonical + legacy fixtures with NO flat tree resolve byte-identically to pre-spec behavior (AC1); the flat fixture resolves flat first-exists-wins (AC2)
- [ ] `DetectLayout` returns each of the five states; `mixed` is a hard error except under a recorded `.mindspec/migrations/<run-id>/` recovery; new-id-in-legacy classifies `legacy` (AC3)
- [ ] The pure layout-signature helper classifies each tree shape and is the single source of truth the Bead-4 merge guard reuses (minor 12)
- [ ] Both worktree shapes resolve and `TreeRootForSpecDir` returns the root for the flat shape (mindspec-ew79 regression green) (AC12)
- [ ] `go test ./internal/bootstrap/...` asserts the greenfield manifest writes flat dirs and `DetectLayout` classifies them `flat` (AC4)

**Acceptance Criteria**
- [ ] Every accessor resolves byte-identically on canonical/legacy with no flat tree (AC1) and flat-first on a flat tree (AC2); `DetectLayout` is whole-tree five-state with `mixed` as a hard error (AC3); greenfield bootstrap is born flat (AC4); both worktree shapes + the ew79 flat-shape `TreeRootForSpecDir` are pinned (AC12).

**Depends on**
None
design:
## Requirements

1. **Per-artifact three-tier resolver; non-breaking reads.** Add a FLAT tier to every artifact accessor in `internal/workspace`, ordered FIRST in resolution PRECEDENCE (first-exists-wins): flat (`.mindspec/specs/<id>`, `.mindspec/adr/`, `.mindspec/domains/<d>`, `.mindspec/context-map.md`, `.mindspec/core/`) → canonical (`.mindspec/docs/…`) → legacy (`docs/…`). "FIRST" here is read-order precedence, NOT delivery order: the flat directories do not physically exist until the Phase-3 moves, so a Phase-1 tree (canonical or legacy) resolves exactly as it does today. The single `DocsDir` join-point (workspace.go:116) that today funnels `ADRDir` (workspace.go:188), `DomainDir` (workspace.go:235), and `ContextMapPath` (workspace.go:178) MUST dissolve into per-artifact resolvers; `SpecDir` (workspace.go:153) gains the flat tier alongside its existing worktree/canonical/legacy tiers. Reading an existing canonical OR legacy project MUST stay byte-for-byte non-breaking — a project with no flat tree resolves exactly as it does today.

2. **Whole-tree `DetectLayout(root) → {flat | canonical | legacy | greenfield | mixed}`, computed once, drives the write-default.** `DetectLayout` MUST distinguish the two non-flat WRITE shapes — `canonical` (a `.mindspec/docs/…` lifecycle tree exists) and `legacy` (a root `docs/…` lifecycle tree exists) — because they are DISTINCT write targets, not one "legacy" bucket; collapsing them cannot drive the never-split write-default for a canonical-only vs a legacy-only project. The write-side "born flat" decision MUST key off this WHOLE-TREE classification ("no canonical/legacy lifecycle tree exists ANYWHERE under root"), never a per-ID existence probe — a per-ID probe cannot distinguish a greenfield project from a brand-new spec inside an existing legacy project, so it would split a project's layout. `greenfield` and post-migration `flat` projects write flat; a `canonical` or `legacy` project keeps writing to its existing form until migrated. `mixed` — ANY flat lifecycle tree coexisting with ANY canonical/legacy lifecycle tree (whether different spec ids OR different artifact classes, e.g. a flat `specs/` beside a canonical `adr/`) — is a HARD ERROR: first-exists-wins reads would mask the residue while writes go flat, reintroducing the exact half-old/half-flat split the panel rejected. The ONLY exception is a recorded in-progress migration recovery (a live `.mindspec/migrations/<run-id>/` run-state, Req 4), where a transient mixed tree is expected and the recovery path — not first-exists-wins — drives resolution. `mindspec init`/`bootstrap` create the flat directories for new projects (replacing the bootstrap.go:222-223 `.mindspec/docs/{domains,specs}` manifest entries).

3. **All root-enumerating `DocsDir` consumers become layout-tier-aware (incl. the context-pack budgeter).** Beyond the named accessors (Req 1), EVERY consumer that joins onto the `DocsDir` root or enumerates under it MUST resolve through a layout-aware accessor, or it silently reads an empty flat tree: `mindspec spec list`, `mindspec domain list`/`show`, context-map enrichment, the authored `core/` doc paths, and the doctor orphan/docs scans (`internal/doctor/docs.go`, also Req 9). In particular `internal/contextpack/budgeter.go` hardcodes `.mindspec/docs/specs/<id>` (budgeter.go:170) and `.mindspec/docs/domains/<d>/<kind>` (budgeter.go:218); on a flat project it feeds those joins empty directories and SILENTLY drops the spec + domain context from the assembled pack. The budgeter MUST consume the per-artifact accessors so a context pack assembles identically — same sections, same bytes — on a flat vs canonical vs legacy project.

4. **Net-new deterministic, transactional, idempotent mover with a DEFINED run-state machine + rollback semantics.** Build a history-preserving git-mv driver (routed through `internal/executor` per ADR-0030, not direct shell-out) that is idempotent (re-running on an already-flat tree is a no-op) and lands each artifact-group move as TWO commits: a pure 100%-similarity `git mv` first, then the link-rewrite (Req 5) second — so `git log --follow` and 3-way-merge rename detection stay reliable. It writes a lineage manifest under `.mindspec/lineage/` and a per-run state record under `.mindspec/migrations/<run-id>/` consistent with the existing doctor migration-metadata schema (`internal/doctor/migration.go`).
   **Run-state machine + crash recovery (DEFINED, not merely named).** The run records an ordered, durable checkpoint at every mutation boundary: (a) pre-run base ref captured; then for EACH artifact group — (b) before the `git mv`, (c) after the `git mv` / before the pure-move commit, (d) after the pure-move commit, (e) after the link-rewrite, (f) after the rewrite commit; then (g) the lineage/state finalize. Required RESUME behavior after a crash: the resumer reads the last durable checkpoint and — at (b)/(c) discards or re-stages the working-tree-only partial `git mv` (nothing is committed yet) and retries the group; at (d)/(f) detects the commit already landed and SKIPS it (idempotent); at (e) re-runs the deterministic link-rewrite (a pure function of the moved tree) and commits. **Rollback semantics (CHOSEN, in git terms): hard-reset-to-pre-run-ref while nothing is published.** On any failure or `--abort` BEFORE the run's commits are pushed/merged, the mover hard-resets the branch to the (a) pre-run ref and cleans the working tree — NO compensating revert commits. AFTER the run's commits are published, the mover REFUSES to auto-rollback and instead emits the forward-only recovery line (re-migrate / rebase), consistent with ADR-0023.

5. **Net-new finite-pattern markdown link-rewriter, gated by a doctor link-existence check that scans EVERY link.** Rewrite ONLY the closed, breaking subset of relative links — NOT a general markdown parser. Because the flatten is SYMMETRIC (specs and adr both shed the same `docs/` level), spec→ADR links like `../../adr/ADR-NNNN.md` are PRESERVED unchanged; the breaking set is small and enumerable: one-level `../adr/` cases, absolute `docs/core/` and `.mindspec/docs/core/`/context-map references, review-co-location links whose relative depth changed under the `<spec-dir>/reviews/` move, dogfood cross-links whose depth changed under eviction, and repo-root `README.md`/`AGENTS.md` references that point INTO the moved trees from OUTSIDE them. The GATING doctor link-existence check MUST scan EVERY markdown link in the post-migration moved tree AND the affected root docs — NOT merely the finite set the rewriter touched — and FAIL the migration (and the run-state machine, Req 4) if ANY link 404s, so a breaking link the finite rewriter failed to anticipate is caught at the gate rather than shipped.

6. **Gate matchers are git-DIFF-string classifiers, permanently multi-prefix.** The doc-sync, ownership, and ADR-divergence lanes match diff PATH STRINGS, not filesystem reads, so the accessors cannot absorb them. Introduce a relative-path layout-classifier predicate and make every git-ref matcher recognize ALL THREE prefixes (flat + canonical + legacy): `isDocFile`/`isSourceFile` (docsync.go:330/338), the `.mindspec/docs/specs/<id>/` literals in `validateSpecArtifactSync`/`specMDID` (docsync.go:561-622), the domain-doc prefixes in `checkInternalPackages` (docsync.go:485-488), the cmd-docs accept-set (docsync.go:534-538), `listDomainDirs`/`TreeDirsAtRef(".mindspec/docs/domains")` (docsync.go:352, ownership.go:198), `LoadOwnership`'s manifest path (ownership.go:79), AND — CRITICALLY — the ref-anchored ownership pair `LoadOwnershipAtRef` (ownership.go:150) + `domainManifestRelPath` (ownership.go:123-125), plus `isProcessArtifact` (divergence.go:277-281). The `complete` ADR-divergence gate loads ownership through the ref-anchored `LoadOwnershipAtRef`/`domainManifestRelPath` pair (NOT `LoadOwnership` at :79); updating only :79 leaves every domain manifest reading "missing" on a flat tree, so every 106 bead would hard-block `adr-divergence-unowned`. This multi-prefix posture is PERMANENT and DECOUPLED from the resolver-tier lifecycle: historical refs, old branches, and external forks never stop emitting legacy paths, so a "drop legacy tiers after N releases" deprecation applies ONLY to filesystem reads (Req 1), NEVER to git-ref matchers. The predicate MUST also classify `project-docs/**` as non-source docs (Req 14) so dogfood eviction does not trip `adr-divergence-unowned` or the doc-sync source lane; the cmd-docs accept-set must accept the post-flatten `core/USAGE.md` and the evicted `project-docs/user/**`.

7. **Worktree-aware fixes + regression tests.** `SpecDir`'s worktree tier must additionally probe the flat worktree shape (`.worktrees/worktree-spec-<id>/.mindspec/specs/<id>`). `TreeRootForSpecDir` (workspace.go:206-222) must recognize the flat `.mindspec/specs/<id>` shape — its current `filepath.Base(docs) != "docs"` assertion (workspace.go:214) returns `""` for a flat dir and would regress the mindspec-ew79 cross-worktree ADR-visibility fix. `guard.go` worktree-add recipes must be layout-aware. Regression tests MUST pin both worktree shapes.

8. **Reviews co-location wiring.** `internal/panel.Scan` and `PanelDirScanRoot` (panel.go:118-142, gate.go:420-422) move from the repo-root `review/*/panel.json` glob to the spec-scoped `<spec-dir>/reviews/*/panel.json` glob (a sibling of `RecordingDir`, workspace.go:244-250); the `mindspec complete` panel-gate scan becomes spec-scoped instead of repo-root. `divergence.go`'s `HasPrefix(path,"review/")` exclusion (divergence.go:280) becomes a `/reviews/`-segment exclusion under spec dirs. Update the `ms-panel-run` + `ms-panel-tally` skill bodies, their `historical_skills` snapshots (`internal/setup/skills.go`), and amend ADR-0037 for the new `panel.json` location. Reviews are TRACKED (durable audit, travel with the spec); the root `review/` tree is eliminated, resolving **adwu**.

9. **Doctor: real layout detection + dual-layout duplicate-ID error.** `mindspec doctor` MUST gain a real layout detector (reusing `DetectLayout`), a `would-migrate-layout` Warn (analogous to the existing `would-migrate: spec=…` Warn, migration.go:101-106), and an ERROR when the SAME spec id exists under two layouts simultaneously (kills the stale-duplicate read hazard the first-exists-wins resolver would otherwise mask). `checkDryRunMigration` (migration.go:39) and the orphan/docs scans (docs.go via `workspace.DocsDir`) must become tier-aware rather than hardcoded to `.mindspec/docs/specs`.

10. **Merge-time layout-fingerprint HARD-FAIL.** `internal/complete` `MergeBranch` (and any spec→main / bead→spec merge) MUST compute a layout fingerprint of source and target and HARD-FAIL a cross-layout merge (nested source onto flat target, or vice versa) with a "rebase onto post-flatten main" recovery line, instead of trusting git's heuristic rename / directory-rename detection. This makes the pre-flatten drain enforced, not advisory (ADR-0023 forward-only).

11. **`migrate layout` precondition: a feasible, testable pre-flatten branch/PR discovery algorithm.** The flatten command's precondition is the absence of any unmerged BRANCH or PR that predates the flatten — NOT "zero worktrees" (unreachable in this repo, and mis-attributed to impl-approve). DISCOVERY ALGORITHM (deterministic source-of-truth): scan (1) local branch refs, (2) remote-tracking refs (`refs/remotes/<remote>/*`), and (3) hosted PR metadata when a remote + token are available; compute a flatten base/fingerprint from the post-flatten layout SIGNATURE (does the ref's merge-base tree still carry the canonical/legacy `.mindspec/docs/` lifecycle layout, vs the flat shape?). A ref BLOCKS the migration iff it is unmerged into the target AND its fingerprint is pre-flatten. OFFLINE / no-remote behavior: the scan degrades to local + remote-tracking refs only and WARNS that hosted PRs could not be consulted (it does NOT silently pass). The command MUST require a clean idle working tree before mutating. Locked agent worktrees and long-lived external forks are explicitly TOLERATED — they cannot be drained, only fingerprint-guarded at merge (Req 10) — so the precondition MUST NOT count them as blockers.

12. **Skills + snapshots correctness on flat projects.** `ms-spec-grill`'s SKILL.md reads the domain set from `.mindspec/docs/domains/` (SKILL.md:30/38/40) and computes the next ADR number by scanning `.mindspec/docs/adr/` (SKILL.md:31); on a flat project these read empty dirs and mis-fire (reject-invented-domains and next-ADR-number both break) — this is the CENTRAL correctness claim of this requirement, so the skill MUST read the layout-correct path. Also update the `lifecycleSkillFiles` literals, the `setup/claude.go` and `setup/codex.go` generated text, the other path-bearing skill bodies (ms-panel-run/tally, ms-bead-impl/cycle/fix, ms-spec-final-review) and plugin README/FINDINGS + bootstrap text, and EVERY path-bearing `historical_skills` snapshot in `internal/setup/skills.go`. The plan MUST either update each path-bearing artifact or explicitly classify it out of scope with a recorded reason.

13. **The moves + the drops.** Flatten `specs/`, `adr/`, `domains/`, and `core/` to top-level `.mindspec/` children; move `context-map.md` to `.mindspec/context-map.md`. KEEP the name `adr` (load-bearing across `ADRDir`, `ADR-NNNN` filenames, `mindspec adr`, and ~150+ inbound links) and KEEP the name `core` (do NOT rename to `reference/` in this spec). Evict dogfood docs (`user/`, `installation/`, `research/`) to top-level `project-docs/`. CRITICAL: the evicted tree MUST NOT be named `docs/` — `workspace.DocsDir` falls back to `LegacyDocsDir = root/docs` (workspace.go:121,130), so a top-level `docs/` would alias the live legacy resolver tier and make `ADRDir`/`DomainDir`/`ContextMapPath` silently resolve INTO the evicted tree. When `domains/` flattens, each domain's OWNERSHIP.yaml that self-claims `.mindspec/docs/domains/<d>/OWNERSHIP.yaml` MUST have that self-glob updated to the flat `.mindspec/domains/<d>/OWNERSHIP.yaml` — non-blocking (doc files, not gate matchers) but a latent staleness that must not be left behind. Drop `glossary.md` (`.mindspec/docs/glossary.md`), `policies.yml` (`.mindspec/policies.yml`), and the stale `internal/instruct/templates/spec.md:35` glossary line, ADR-0018-consistent, with no dangling references left.

14. **Ownership + classification deliverables.** Any net-new mover package (e.g. `internal/layout/**`) MUST be added to the workflow `OWNERSHIP.yaml` so it is owned and does not trip `adr-divergence-unowned` at complete. `project-docs/**` MUST be classified as non-source docs by the Req 6 predicate (it is dogfood reference, not governable source) so its tracked move is neither flagged unowned nor mis-classified as a source change requiring doc-sync. No `bench/**`, `viz/**`, or `agentmind/**` glob may be added (excluded first-segments; a hard `LoadOwnership` schema error, ownership.go:60).

15. **Test/fixture migration is first-class and budgeted.** ~99 exact-slash-form `.mindspec/docs/{specs,adr,domains,core}` occurrences across 21 non-test Go files (~110 once the `filepath.Join` forms are counted) plus the harness scenario files and testdata fixtures encode the physical layout. The plan MUST budget fixture migration explicitly and add a flat-layout test matrix so the resolvers, classifier predicate, mover, panel scan, doctor detector, AND the context-pack builder (Req 3) are all exercised on flat AND canonical/legacy trees. Phase 1 MUST land fully green with ZERO layout change (revertible), proving the refactor is behavior-preserving before any file moves.

16. **Amend `DOCS-LAYOUT.md` to the flat layout.** `.mindspec/docs/core/DOCS-LAYOUT.md` (which itself flattens to `.mindspec/core/DOCS-LAYOUT.md`) documents the current `.mindspec/docs/` layout and is an in-this-spec deliverable (Background, Scope). Like the ADR-0037 amendment (Req 8) it MUST be GOVERNED, not left implicit: amend it to describe the flat `.mindspec/{specs,adr,domains,core}` + `project-docs/` layout, the per-artifact three-tier read order, and the reviews co-location, so the authored reference does not contradict the shipped tree.

17. **Reconcile the `cmd/mindspec/migrate.go` prompt rubric with the flat target.** The legacy `mindspec migrate` prompt EMITTER's classification rubric still routes user docs to `.mindspec/docs/user/` and agent files to `.mindspec/docs/agent/` (migrate.go:286-287) and presents `.mindspec/docs/` as the canonical destination (migrate.go:264-298). It MUST be reconciled with this spec's targets: dogfood/user docs route to top-level `project-docs/`, and lifecycle/authored artifacts to the flat `.mindspec/{specs,adr,domains,core}` children — so the prompt emitter and the deterministic `migrate layout` mover agree on the destination shape instead of emitting prompts that would re-create the evicted `.mindspec/docs/user/`/`…/agent/` trees.

title: Documentation governance as a mindspec capability: help consumer projects self-document (Diátaxis + docs-as-code + doc-sync DoD + prose-lint) — likely its own spec
description:
SCOPE (clarified 2026-06-17 w/ Max): the PRIMARY goal is NOT to tidy mindspec's own docs — it is to make MINDSPEC HELP THE PROJECTS THAT USE IT self-document effectively, as a capability of the agent-driven spec lifecycle. mindspec already ships docs-as-code governance PRIMITIVES that consumer projects adopt (specs/plans, ADRs under .mindspec/docs/adr, per-domain OWNERSHIP.yaml, the doc-sync validator internal/validate/docsync.go, mindspec doctor). This effort EXTENDS those so a consumer project also gets governed, industry-best-practice USER documentation:
  - SCAFFOLD + VALIDATE a Diátaxis doc structure in the consumer repo (tutorials / how-to / reference / explanation), the way mindspec already scaffolds specs/ADRs/domains.
  - Extend DOC-SYNC into a doc Definition-of-Done gate: code/spec changes must keep the matching user-doc mode current (reference regenerated from CLI/specs; how-to/tutorial reviewed).
  - Optional PROSE-LINT integration (Vale + a shareable style guide) the consumer project can enable, gated in its CI like golangci-lint.
  - Drive doc authoring through the agent layer: the spec lifecycle (and the new ms-spec-grill skill) can grill for doc completeness / correct Diátaxis mode, not just spec completeness.
  - Extend the OWNERSHIP model to the consumer's user-doc areas (named owners, audit loop).
mindspec's OWN repo is the FIRST dogfood consumer of all the above, not the point of the work. The research below (Diátaxis + docs-as-code + Vale) is what mindspec should help consumer projects adopt.

--- RESEARCH & ORIGINAL NOTES ---
Improve MindSpec's documentation governance to follow industry best practices. Backlog item from a deep-research web search (Max, 2026-06-17). Likely warrants its OWN multi-bead spec rather than a single bead.

## Where we are today (grounded in the repo)
Strong docs-as-code FOUNDATIONS already exist: 38 ADRs (.mindspec/docs/adr/), per-domain OWNERSHIP.yaml governance (.mindspec/docs/domains/, internal/validate/ownership.go), a doc-sync validator (internal/validate/docsync.go), mindspec doctor, and source classification (internal/source). BUT gaps:
- Doc structure is by lifecycle/process, not by READER NEED: .mindspec/docs/{specs(106),adr,domains,core,user,installation,research} mixes process docs with user docs; no clean tutorials/how-to/reference/explanation split.
- NO prose linter / style guide (no Vale/.vale.ini/style config anywhere).
- doc-sync is lenient — every spec this cycle needed `--allow-doc-skew`; see the recurring review/-deletion + deferred bead adwu (untrack review/ + run golangci-lint/whole-suite in bead gates).
- Single-source-of-truth risk: AGENTS.md vs CLAUDE.md overlap; the bd-managed CLAUDE.md block churns (hash bumps) on tooling runs.

## Best practices to adopt (researched)
1. **Diátaxis** (https://diataxis.fr , https://diataxis.fr/start-here/) — organize USER-FACING docs into the four modes on two axes (action↔cognition, study↔work): TUTORIALS (learning-oriented, hands-on), HOW-TO GUIDES (task-oriented), REFERENCE (information-oriented, neutral/complete), EXPLANATION (understanding-oriented, the 'why'). Mixing modes is the root of most doc problems. ADOPT INCREMENTALLY (the framework's own guidance: 'do that thing, then repeat' — one targeted improvement at a time). Map .mindspec/docs/user + installation → tutorials/how-to; ADRs are already 'explanation/decision'; generated CLI/command docs → reference.
2. **Docs-as-code Definition-of-Done** — docs in-repo, Markdown, versioned, REVIEWED like code, built+deployed by CI on merge; periodic audits; remove stale docs. (https://deepdocs.dev/technical-documentation-best-practices/ , https://www.netlify.com/blog/a-key-to-high-quality-documentation-docs-linting-in-ci-cd/)
3. **Prose linting in CI** — add **Vale** (https://vale.sh/docs) with a style guide as single-source-of-truth: base on the Google or Microsoft developer style guide + a mindspec terminology/vocab package; run in CI + a git hook so style issues fail before merge (like Datadog/Elastic: https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/engineering/how-we-use-vale-to-improve-our-documentation-editing-process/ , https://github.com/elastic/vale-rules). Mirrors how we already gate golangci-lint.
4. **Explicit doc governance policy** — named owners per doc area (extend the existing per-domain OWNERSHIP model to user-facing docs), a documented style/voice standard, and a feedback loop / scheduled doc audits.
5. **Tighten doc-sync + single-source-of-truth** — make doc-sync less reliant on `--allow-doc-skew`; de-duplicate AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md (one canonical source, the other generated/linked); stabilize the managed-block churn. Coordinate with deferred bead adwu.

## Suggested decomposition (when specced)
(a) Diátaxis IA: re-organize .mindspec/docs/ + a top-level docs/ map into the 4 modes (incremental, non-breaking). (b) Vale + style guide + CI gate. (c) Doc DoD + governance policy doc + extend OWNERSHIP to user docs. (d) doc-sync tightening + AGENTS/CLAUDE single-source.

title: TestRun_IdleNoBeads test-isolation leak: fake .git escapes to real worktree when suite runs inside an active-spec worktree
description: Surfaced during spec 105 whole-spec final review (adversarial). internal/instruct (and the shared internal/harness TestRun_IdleNoBeads) FAIL when the full suite is run from inside an active-spec worktree that is itself mid-lifecycle (e.g. review mode): setupRunTestProject creates a fake .git dir, but Run's git/state resolution (phase.ResolveContextFromDirWithCache) doesn't anchor on it and walks UP to the real enclosing worktree, reads its review-mode state, and emits impl-approve guidance instead of 'No Active Work'. PRE-EXISTING (untouched by 105; passes in fresh CI checkout — CI runs in a clean clone, not a mindspec worktree). Fix: make setupRunTestProject's isolation hermetic — set GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES / a real git init in the temp dir, or have Run honor an explicit root override so resolution can't escape the test sandbox. Domain: core/workflow (internal/instruct).
notes: 2026-07-17 (spec 118): recurred hard. This non-hermetic failure fires on EVERY bead's full-suite `go test ./...` during an active spec, and repeatedly TRAPPED implementer/reviewer subagents into waiting for a green ./... that never comes (they yield 'standing by for full-suite completion' without committing). Bumped P3→P2. It's now an active drag on the multi-agent bead loop, not just a cosmetic CI-clean-only nuisance. Fix as described (hermetic setupRunTestProject: GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES or explicit root override so phase.ResolveContextFromDirWithCache can't walk up to the enclosing worktree).

**RED tests** (all hermetic; bead-blocking)

design:
## Requirements

1. **Grill protocol — relentless one-at-a-time interrogation grounded in the live repo.** The SKILL.md MUST instruct the agent to ask exactly ONE question at a time, never batching, and to refuse to advance until the current answer is concrete. Grounding MUST be live: cross-check every declared domain against the directories under `.mindspec/docs/domains/`; surface the real ADRs under `.mindspec/docs/adr/` relevant to each impacted domain and suggest the next-free ADR number when a new principle appears; and reality-check factual claims ("X already does Y") against the actual code/tree before accepting them.
2. **Coaching technique — domain & glossary alignment.** The SKILL.md MUST require the agent to validate each `## Impacted Domains` entry against the real domain set and reject invented domains (e.g. "caching", "scheduling"), mapping file-path entries to owning domains per the ADR-0036 model.
3. **Coaching technique — synonym / fuzzy-language detection.** The SKILL.md MUST require the agent to flag and reject requirements and ACs that use support/enable/improve/handle-style verbs with no falsifiable behavior (e.g. "Enable resumable exports", "improve reliability") — the SYNONYM/SEMANTIC class the deterministic detector scores 0 on.
4. **Coaching technique — falsifiability coaching.** The SKILL.md MUST require the agent to refuse non-falsifiable claims ("it works", "is fast", "reasonable time", "performance is acceptable") and coach the author into a measurable assertion with a threshold and an observable.
5. **Coaching technique — contradiction detection.** The SKILL.md MUST require the agent to scan requirements pairwise for mutual contradiction (e.g. "run concurrently" vs "at most one at a time") and force resolution — the CONTRADICTION class no deterministic rule set can reach.
6. **Coaching technique — scenario-driven edge-case probing.** The SKILL.md MUST require the agent to drive concrete scenarios (failure, concurrency, empty-input, boundary) to expose unstated edge cases and convert them into requirements or explicit Non-Goals.
7. **Thinness refusal & AC floor.** The SKILL.md MUST instruct the agent to refuse thin/empty answers and to require at least 3 falsifiable acceptance criteria, each pairing an assertion with a runnable proof, and to resolve or explicitly defer every Open Question before the grill is considered complete.
8. **Composition with the non-interactive binary.** The skill MUST drive `mindspec spec create <id>` to produce the scaffold, then grill the author to fill it; the binary MUST remain the non-interactive scaffold with no new blocking stdin read, so non-agent automation/CI is unaffected (the grilling is agent reasoning, not a binary prompt).
9. **Install & registration as a PLUGIN skill.** The grill MUST ship as a NEW **plugin** skill: the single source of truth is ONE file at `plugins/mindspec/skills/ms-spec-grill/SKILL.md` with valid frontmatter (`name` + `description`). It MUST follow the PLUGIN-skill mechanism used by `ms-bead-*`/`ms-panel-*` — filesystem-discovered via `plugins/mindspec`'s `//go:embed skills/*/SKILL.md` and merged by `pluginmindspec.SkillFiles()` — NOT the lifecycle-gate inline-literal mechanism (`lifecycleSkillFiles()` in `internal/setup/claude.go`) that `ms-spec-create` uses. (`ms-spec-create` is a lifecycle-gate skill physically defined as an inline raw-string literal and present only under `.claude/skills/` + `.agents/skills/`, never under `plugins/`; grill must NOT be added there.) `mindspec setup` propagates the embedded plugin SKILL.md to `.claude/skills/ms-spec-grill/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/ms-spec-grill/SKILL.md`. The 3-path `test -f` install ACs therefore pass only AFTER `mindspec setup` runs.
10. **`ms-spec-create` auto-chains into the grill (trigger contract).** `ms-spec-create` MUST auto-invoke `ms-spec-grill` by default: after scaffolding via `mindspec spec create <id>`, the updated `ms-spec-create` SKILL.md (all replicas) MUST contain an explicit, grep-provable handoff that invokes `ms-spec-grill` to grill the draft — the grill fires UNLESS the author explicitly opts out. Auto-chain-by-default is chosen over opt-in precisely because the failure mode being fixed is *authors skipping rigor*; an opt-in reference the author must remember to trigger would let the grill ship dead. The invocation MUST NOT be left to author discretion (the handoff text is the contract).
11. **New skill, not an inline rewrite of ms-spec-create.** The deliverable MUST be a NEW skill named `ms-spec-grill` (rationale: a single-responsibility grill skill is independently testable by the eval, reusable from contexts beyond create, and aligns with ADR-0034's collapse-don't-duplicate posture); `ms-spec-create` is updated only to auto-invoke it (Req 10).
12. **Ownership deliverable: claim `.agents/skills/**`.** This spec MUST add `- .agents/skills/**` to the workflow `.mindspec/docs/domains/workflow/OWNERSHIP.yaml` so the git-tracked `.agents/skills/ms-spec-grill/SKILL.md` normalizes to the workflow domain and does NOT trigger `adr-divergence-unowned` on `mindspec complete`. The eval tree MUST NOT be claimed: NO `bench/**` glob may be added (`bench` is an excluded first-segment — the divergence gate skips it; adding it is a hard `LoadOwnership` schema error).
13. **Setup count assertions stay green.** Adding the 8th plugin skill breaks hardcoded count assertions in workflow-owned `internal/setup/**`. This spec MUST update them so impl does not ship red tests: `internal/setup/skills_test.go` (`len(all)` must become 12: 4 lifecycle + 8 plugin) and `internal/setup/claude_test.go` (the "7 plugin skills" / "11 total" expectations become 8 plugin / 12 total, and any dependent created/skipped item counts adjusted accordingly).
14. **Eval scoring is deterministic, model-pinned, and `claude`-CLI gated.** The eval MUST score the LLM grill's free-text findings against `ground_truth.tsv` using a DETERMINISTIC free-text→problem-id matching rule (keyword/line-anchored matching), NOT an LLM mapping/judging step (no LLM-judging-LLM). It MUST invoke `claude -p` with a FIXED model id and `temperature 0` so the recall figure is reproducible run-to-run. `claude` is an eval PRECONDITION: it must be installed and authenticated (logged-in CLI or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); `run_eval.sh` MUST SKIP-with-notice (exit 0, print a skip message) when `claude` is absent rather than hard-fail, so the eval AC is runnable on fresh machines/CI.

## ADR Decisions

Cited by ID — full text under `.mindspec/docs/adr/`:

- see ADR-0019 — Deterministic Worktree and Branch Enforcement for Agent Workflows
- see ADR-0034 — Ceremony Collapse — Single-Bead Lifecycle Epic + Legacy Auto-Migrator
- see ADR-0036 — Ownership Discovery — Zero Framework Cognition for OWNERSHIP.yaml and source_globs

- [ ] `ms-spec-create` (literal + both replicas after setup) auto-invokes
`ms-spec-grill` — grep-provable (AC10).
- [ ] After `mindspec setup`, the grill exists at all three paths with valid
frontmatter (AC2).
- [ ] `mindspec spec create <fresh-id> </dev/null` exits 0 — binary stays
non-interactive (AC9).
- [ ] `.agents/skills/**` is workflow-owned, NO `bench/**` glob, and
`go test ./internal/setup/...` passes with 12-skill (4 lifecycle + 8
plugin) counts (AC11, R13).

title: [105-spec-grill-skill] Bead 2: track the grill detection eval under bench/grill/ (Req 14)
description:
**Scope:** Bring the cleaned `/tmp/grill-bench` prototype into the repo at
`bench/grill/` and complete it to the spec's contract: fixtures (the cleaned 3
+ ≥1 held-out/blind, CONTRADICTION raised to ≥3 items), `ground_truth.tsv`,
the deterministic baseline `det_detect.sh`, and the model-pinned,
deterministic-matching, `claude`-gated `run_eval.sh`. ⚠️ `bench` is an excluded
first-segment — this tree gets NO OWNERSHIP glob (that is Bead 3's negative AC).

**Changed files:** `bench/grill/fixtures/spec1.md`, `bench/grill/fixtures/spec2.md`,
`bench/grill/fixtures/spec3.md`, `bench/grill/fixtures/spec4-heldout.md` (new held-out/blind),
`bench/grill/ground_truth.tsv`, `bench/grill/det_detect.sh`, `bench/grill/run_eval.sh` (new)

**Steps**
1. Copy the cleaned fixtures from the prototype, KEEPING the deterministic-leak
   fix already applied: spec2-P4 and spec3-P4 are re-phrased so the
   `functions? properly` / `handles .* correctly` regexes in `det_detect.sh`
   no longer accidentally catch them — this is what makes the AC5 baseline a
   TRUE 0/M on the LLM-only classes rather than 2/M.
   - ⚠️ **IMPL NOTE:** verify the leak is closed by running `det_detect.sh`
     over spec2/spec3 and confirming it flags ZERO SEMANTIC/SYNONYM items.
2. Add **≥1 HELD-OUT/blind fixture** (`spec4-heldout.md`) NOT used while
   authoring or tuning the grill (Bead 1), and **raise CONTRADICTION to ≥3
   items** total across the fixture set (the prototype had n=1, which is
   unfalsifiable). Record every planted problem in `ground_truth.tsv` with its
   `category` (SEMANTIC/SYNONYM/CONTRADICTION/GROUNDING/EXACT_PHRASE/STRUCTURAL),
   `catchable_by` (llm/both), and the **`anchor`** column (see § Eval matcher
   below).
   - ⚠️ **IMPL NOTE:** the held-out fixture's LLM-only items and all ≥3
     CONTRADICTION items MUST be INCLUDED in M — they may not be excluded from
     the scored denominator. M = count of all SEMANTIC+SYNONYM+CONTRADICTION
     rows in the FINAL tracked `ground_truth.tsv`.
3. Track `det_detect.sh` (the prototype's deterministic ceiling: empty/
   placeholder detection, exact bad-phrase lists, domain-set membership, <3
   ACs). It MUST still catch 100% of GROUNDING/EXACT_PHRASE/STRUCTURAL and 0/M
   of the LLM-only classes.
   - ⚠️ **ANTI-GAMING (det_detect is a FIXED baseline, NOT tunable):**
     `det_detect.sh`'s heuristic regex set is the **faithful deterministic
     ceiling** — it is FIXED, not a lever. The AC5 `0/M` result MUST be achieved
     by **FIXTURE RE-PHRASING ONLY** (closing the leak in spec2-P4/spec3-P4 etc.,
     per step 1), NEVER by narrowing `det_detect.sh`'s regexes to dodge the
     LLM-only items. An impl that narrows a regex to fake `0/M` would break the
     POSITIVE recall assertion in AC5 (below), not just the negative one.
4. Author `run_eval.sh` (R14):
   - Invoke `claude -p` with a **FIXED full model id** (`--model <pinned id>`) so
     the recall is as reproducible run-to-run as the CLI allows. **There is NO
     `--temperature` flag** in the Claude Code CLI (verified v2.1.178) — do NOT
     attempt to pass one; determinism is realized by the model-pin + N-run
     aggregation below, not a temperature knob (see Testing Strategy §
     Reproducibility mechanism note).
   - Loop **N≥5** times; compute **M** from the tracked `ground_truth.tsv`
     (count the SEMANTIC+SYNONYM+CONTRADICTION rows — NOT a frozen literal);
     score each run's grill findings against `ground_truth.tsv` by the
     **DETERMINISTIC STRUCTURED-ANCHOR match** defined in § Eval matcher below
     (NO LLM judging an LLM); report MIN (or median) recall over the runs and the
     deterministic baseline (0/M) for comparison; MAY additionally print the
     held-out fixture's recall separately. Exit 0 only when min/median ≥
     **⌈0.9·M⌉**.
   - **`claude` is a PRECONDITION:** if `claude` is not installed/authenticated
     (logged-in CLI or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), **SKIP-with-notice** (print a skip
     message, exit 0) — never hard-fail — so the eval is runnable on fresh
     machines/CI.
   - ⚠️ **IMPL NOTE:** make `run_eval.sh` and `det_detect.sh` executable
     (`chmod +x`) and shellcheck-clean.

**§ Eval matcher — STRUCTURED-ANCHOR design (replaces hand-waved keyword/line matching)**

The match rule is the load-bearing part of the eval: it must credit a planted
problem deterministically without an LLM judge, and it must survive the LLM
paraphrasing its own prose run-to-run. The design:

- **C1 — `anchor` column.** `ground_truth.tsv` gains a unique **`anchor`** per
  row: a unique substring of the **FIXTURE'S OWN text** for that problem (e.g.
  the requirement/AC phrase exactly as written in the fixture — NOT the LLM's
  paraphrase). Paired with this, the grill prompt (Bead 1, step 6) instructs the
  agent to echo, for each finding, the **verbatim quoted fixture span** plus a
  `[CATEGORY]` tag.
- **C2 — credit rule.** The matcher credits a problem-id **IFF** (the finding's
  `[CATEGORY]` tag matches the row's `category`) **AND** (that row's `anchor`
  appears as a **NORMALIZED substring** in a finding line). Normalization =
  case-fold + strip punctuation/quotes (so `"Function Properly,"` matches
  `function properly`). One-to-one: **each P-id is credited at most once**;
  **surplus findings** (the LLM finds more than were planted) **neither credit
  nor penalize**. Recall = matched-planted / M.
- **C3 — anchor is pinned to the FIXTURE, not the paraphrase.** The anchor MUST
  be the fixture phrase (stable across runs), never the LLM's wording. Real
  prototype runs proved paraphrase drift — the model wrote "function properly"
  where the fixture said "behave as expected", and "handles concurrency
  correctly" where the fixture said "robust under load" — which an
  LLM-paraphrase anchor would have scored as FALSE NEGATIVES. Pinning the anchor
  to the fixture text (which the prompt instructs the agent to quote verbatim)
  removes that drift.
- **C4 — author-time anchor/fixture self-check.** `run_eval.sh` (or a tiny
  companion check, run at author time and on every eval invocation) MUST assert
  that **every `ground_truth.tsv` row's `anchor` is actually a substring of its
  own fixture file**. This catches anchor/fixture skew at author time (a typo'd
  or stale anchor would otherwise silently fail to ever match). This check is
  hermetic (no `claude`) and may run even in the SKIP-with-notice path.

**RED tests**
- **AC5 (hermetic, bead-blocking) — NEGATIVE 0/M AND POSITIVE recall:**
  `bench/grill/det_detect.sh bench/grill/fixtures/*.md` (a) flags ZERO

design:
## Requirements

1. **Grill protocol — relentless one-at-a-time interrogation grounded in the live repo.** The SKILL.md MUST instruct the agent to ask exactly ONE question at a time, never batching, and to refuse to advance until the current answer is concrete. Grounding MUST be live: cross-check every declared domain against the directories under `.mindspec/docs/domains/`; surface the real ADRs under `.mindspec/docs/adr/` relevant to each impacted domain and suggest the next-free ADR number when a new principle appears; and reality-check factual claims ("X already does Y") against the actual code/tree before accepting them.
2. **Coaching technique — domain & glossary alignment.** The SKILL.md MUST require the agent to validate each `## Impacted Domains` entry against the real domain set and reject invented domains (e.g. "caching", "scheduling"), mapping file-path entries to owning domains per the ADR-0036 model.
3. **Coaching technique — synonym / fuzzy-language detection.** The SKILL.md MUST require the agent to flag and reject requirements and ACs that use support/enable/improve/handle-style verbs with no falsifiable behavior (e.g. "Enable resumable exports", "improve reliability") — the SYNONYM/SEMANTIC class the deterministic detector scores 0 on.
4. **Coaching technique — falsifiability coaching.** The SKILL.md MUST require the agent to refuse non-falsifiable claims ("it works", "is fast", "reasonable time", "performance is acceptable") and coach the author into a measurable assertion with a threshold and an observable.
5. **Coaching technique — contradiction detection.** The SKILL.md MUST require the agent to scan requirements pairwise for mutual contradiction (e.g. "run concurrently" vs "at most one at a time") and force resolution — the CONTRADICTION class no deterministic rule set can reach.
6. **Coaching technique — scenario-driven edge-case probing.** The SKILL.md MUST require the agent to drive concrete scenarios (failure, concurrency, empty-input, boundary) to expose unstated edge cases and convert them into requirements or explicit Non-Goals.
7. **Thinness refusal & AC floor.** The SKILL.md MUST instruct the agent to refuse thin/empty answers and to require at least 3 falsifiable acceptance criteria, each pairing an assertion with a runnable proof, and to resolve or explicitly defer every Open Question before the grill is considered complete.
8. **Composition with the non-interactive binary.** The skill MUST drive `mindspec spec create <id>` to produce the scaffold, then grill the author to fill it; the binary MUST remain the non-interactive scaffold with no new blocking stdin read, so non-agent automation/CI is unaffected (the grilling is agent reasoning, not a binary prompt).
9. **Install & registration as a PLUGIN skill.** The grill MUST ship as a NEW **plugin** skill: the single source of truth is ONE file at `plugins/mindspec/skills/ms-spec-grill/SKILL.md` with valid frontmatter (`name` + `description`). It MUST follow the PLUGIN-skill mechanism used by `ms-bead-*`/`ms-panel-*` — filesystem-discovered via `plugins/mindspec`'s `//go:embed skills/*/SKILL.md` and merged by `pluginmindspec.SkillFiles()` — NOT the lifecycle-gate inline-literal mechanism (`lifecycleSkillFiles()` in `internal/setup/claude.go`) that `ms-spec-create` uses. (`ms-spec-create` is a lifecycle-gate skill physically defined as an inline raw-string literal and present only under `.claude/skills/` + `.agents/skills/`, never under `plugins/`; grill must NOT be added there.) `mindspec setup` propagates the embedded plugin SKILL.md to `.claude/skills/ms-spec-grill/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/ms-spec-grill/SKILL.md`. The 3-path `test -f` install ACs therefore pass only AFTER `mindspec setup` runs.
10. **`ms-spec-create` auto-chains into the grill (trigger contract).** `ms-spec-create` MUST auto-invoke `ms-spec-grill` by default: after scaffolding via `mindspec spec create <id>`, the updated `ms-spec-create` SKILL.md (all replicas) MUST contain an explicit, grep-provable handoff that invokes `ms-spec-grill` to grill the draft — the grill fires UNLESS the author explicitly opts out. Auto-chain-by-default is chosen over opt-in precisely because the failure mode being fixed is *authors skipping rigor*; an opt-in reference the author must remember to trigger would let the grill ship dead. The invocation MUST NOT be left to author discretion (the handoff text is the contract).
11. **New skill, not an inline rewrite of ms-spec-create.** The deliverable MUST be a NEW skill named `ms-spec-grill` (rationale: a single-responsibility grill skill is independently testable by the eval, reusable from contexts beyond create, and aligns with ADR-0034's collapse-don't-duplicate posture); `ms-spec-create` is updated only to auto-invoke it (Req 10).
12. **Ownership deliverable: claim `.agents/skills/**`.** This spec MUST add `- .agents/skills/**` to the workflow `.mindspec/docs/domains/workflow/OWNERSHIP.yaml` so the git-tracked `.agents/skills/ms-spec-grill/SKILL.md` normalizes to the workflow domain and does NOT trigger `adr-divergence-unowned` on `mindspec complete`. The eval tree MUST NOT be claimed: NO `bench/**` glob may be added (`bench` is an excluded first-segment — the divergence gate skips it; adding it is a hard `LoadOwnership` schema error).
13. **Setup count assertions stay green.** Adding the 8th plugin skill breaks hardcoded count assertions in workflow-owned `internal/setup/**`. This spec MUST update them so impl does not ship red tests: `internal/setup/skills_test.go` (`len(all)` must become 12: 4 lifecycle + 8 plugin) and `internal/setup/claude_test.go` (the "7 plugin skills" / "11 total" expectations become 8 plugin / 12 total, and any dependent created/skipped item counts adjusted accordingly).
14. **Eval scoring is deterministic, model-pinned, and `claude`-CLI gated.** The eval MUST score the LLM grill's free-text findings against `ground_truth.tsv` using a DETERMINISTIC free-text→problem-id matching rule (keyword/line-anchored matching), NOT an LLM mapping/judging step (no LLM-judging-LLM). It MUST invoke `claude -p` with a FIXED model id and `temperature 0` so the recall figure is reproducible run-to-run. `claude` is an eval PRECONDITION: it must be installed and authenticated (logged-in CLI or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); `run_eval.sh` MUST SKIP-with-notice (exit 0, print a skip message) when `claude` is absent rather than hard-fail, so the eval AC is runnable on fresh machines/CI.

- see ADR-0034 — Ceremony Collapse — Single-Bead Lifecycle Epic + Legacy Auto-Migrator

title: [SPEC 105-spec-grill-skill] Spec Grill Skill
[104-interactive-spec-grill] Bead 3: mindspec-104a.3 — CLI flags, TTY decision, fallback notice, and create seam
description:
**Scope:** `cmd/mindspec/spec.go` gains the `--interactive` / `--no-interactive`
flag pair and the interview-active decision (flag AND TTY via
`os.ModeCharDevice` AND not `--no-interactive`; `--no-interactive` wins); the
non-TTY / EOF fallback emits an ADR-0035-shaped stderr notice and exits 0;
`internal/spec/create.go` gains a body seam so `spec.Run` accepts a pre-rendered
body while the DEFAULT path stays byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Changed files:** `cmd/mindspec/spec.go`, `cmd/mindspec/spec_test.go`,
`internal/spec/create.go`, `internal/spec/create_test.go`

**Steps**
1. Add a body seam to `internal/spec/create.go`: introduce the EXACT signature
   `RunWithBody(root, specID, title string, body []byte, exec executor.Executor)
   (*Result, error)`. `RunWithBody` OWNS the EXISTING Phases 1–4 verbatim
   (`InitSpecWorkspace` → write `spec.md` → `CommitAll "chore: initialize spec %s"`
   → `githooks.InstallAll` + recording) AND the `validate.SpecID(specID)` guard —
   so BOTH the default and the interactive paths run ID validation plus the same
   commit/hook/recording side effects exactly once, in the same order, with no
   duplication. It writes the provided `body` instead of the substituted template.
   `Run` becomes a PURE wrapper: resolve the title via the existing
   `titleFromSlug` fallback, build the `<ID>`/`<Title>`-substituted template bytes,
   and call `RunWithBody`.
   - ⚠️ **IMPL NOTE: the `<ID>`/`<Title>` substitution lives in `Run` ONLY** (no
     double-substitution — `RunWithBody` writes its `body` argument verbatim) so the
     existing `internal/spec/create_test.go` template assertions and the AC3 golden
     stay green. `RunWithBody` performs NO template substitution; the interactive
     caller passes the already-assembled interview body.
2. In `cmd/mindspec/spec.go`, add the flag pair on `specCreateCmd` and a pure
   decision helper `interviewActive(stdin *os.File, interactive, noInteractive
   bool) bool`. The predicate MUST be evaluated in this EXACT short-circuit order:
   `interactive && !noInteractive && isCharDevice(stdin)`. Because Go `&&`
   short-circuits left-to-right, the flag checks (`interactive`, `!noInteractive`)
   are evaluated BEFORE `isCharDevice(stdin)` ever stats stdin — so `--no-interactive`
   (and the both-flags case) returns false on the FLAG alone, never reaching the
   char-device stat. `isCharDevice` wraps `stat.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice != 0`
   (the `internal/hook/hook.go` precedent). `--no-interactive` wins when both set
   (Req1). The TTY check MUST happen BEFORE any blocking read (Req2/HC1).
3. ⚠️ **IMPL NOTE (non-TTY/EOF fallback, Req2/Req10/HC1/HC7): never block, never
   error.** When `interviewActive` is false (no flag / non-TTY / `--no-interactive`),
   call `spec.Run` exactly as today (template). When it is true, run
   `interview.Run(root, os.Stdin, out)` (threading the same `root` the create-seam
   already resolved); if it returns `aborted=true` (EOF mid/at-start)
   emit the ADR-0035-shaped stderr notice ("stdin closed mid-interview; wrote the
   template scaffold instead") and fall back to `spec.Run` (template); if stdin
